informal.PackingBounds.FullMain.exact_binary_expo: The base-two logarithm of the unrestricted linear-program bound, divided by dimension, converges to -1/2 log_2(2 pi / e).
informal.PackingBounds.PackingBridge.sphere_packi: There is a vanishing error sequence such that, in every positive dimension, sphere-packing density is at most (sqrt(e / (2 pi)) plus that error) to the dimension.
informal.PackingBounds.sharpFullCohnElkiesManuscr: Packages the complete sharp asymptotic conclusions for the unrestricted program, including quotient-root, natural-logarithmic, and base-two limits, vanishing-error formulas, a universal bound for all admissible functions, and a certified decimal exponent interval.

records.title: Stafford 3.8
records.abstract: Lean formalization of Stafford's Conjecture 3.8 for every characteristic-zero field and every Weyl-algebra rank, proving that each nonzero d admits F, R, and S with 1 = d*R + F*d*S. The development also proves an exact Bernstein-degree fixed-source strengthening and derived localization, adjoint, and evolutionary results.

informal.Stafford38.universalStatement: For every characteristic-zero field, every Weyl algebra rank, and every nonzero d, there are F, R, S with 1 = d*R + F*d*S.
informal.Stafford38.universalFixedSourceStatement: The stated fixed-source strengthening holds with its exact Bernstein-degree bound.

records.title: Verified Stallings folding for finitely generated subgroups of F2
records.abstract: Constructs a finite inverse automaton recognizing the subgroup generated by any finite list of signed words in the rank-two free group. Proves exact subgroup preservation and correctness of canonical reduced-word membership testing. Reusable infrastructure includes inverse-automaton walks, reduction-compatible traversal, finite fold congruences, coset potentials, flower graphs, and basis roses. Folding uses exhaustive finite search over Boolean relations; no complexity bound, core pruning, subgroup basis, intersection, or index algorithm is claimed.

informal.Stallings.folded_recognizer_exists: For every finite list S of signed words on two generators, there exist a finite type of states, a base state, and a partial transition table with inverse-labelled reverse edges, such that traversing the canonical reduced word of any g in FreeGroup (Fin 2) returns to the base exactly when g lies in the subgroup generated by the word values in S. The witness is the computed flower-graph fold.
informal.Stallings.foldWords_loopSubgroup_eq_gene: For every finite input list of signed words in the rank-two free group, the based-loop subgroup of the computed folded flower graph equals the subgroup generated by the input words.
informal.Stallings.foldedMembershipTest_eq_true_i: For any finite generating list S and any rank-two free-group element g, the executable folded-automaton test returns true if and only if g belongs to the subgroup generated by S. There is no efficiency guarantee for constructing the automaton.

records.title: Monotonicity Formula for Stationary Harmonic Maps
records.abstract: Formalizes the monotonicity formula for stationary `W^{1,2}_{loc}` maps with Euclidean target. The proof is target independent: it uses only the displayed weak gradient and a vanishing domain first variation, so no target-manifold structure enters the argument. From a bundled stationary Sobolev witness `StationaryW12LocMap u Omega` it proves, for `0 < s <= r < R0`, that the normalized energy `Theta(Du, a, rho) = rho^(2-n) * integral over B(a, rho) of |Du|^2` is monotone: `weakTheta Du a s <= weakTheta Du a r`, together with the exact increment formula `weakTheta Du a r - weakTheta Du a s = weakMonotonicityRhs Du a s r`. The Sobolev layer is project-defined from Mathlib's `MemLp`, weak-derivative identities, Bochner integration, and Euclidean measure theory, following the De Giorgi-Nash-Moser engineering choice; the internal proof routes through a radial vector-field first variation, a coarea/Radon-Nikodym radius representation, smooth radial cutoffs, and an absolute-continuity boundary step.

informal.LeanStationaryHarmonicMaps.StationaryHar: The public input package: a domain-variation stationary `W^{1,2}_{loc}` Sobolev map bundling a chosen weak gradient (`W12LocMapWitness`) with the vanishing domain first-variation identity. This is the object users construct to invoke the monotonicity theorem.

Witness-style monotonicity: from a stationary `W^{1,2}_{loc}` map package, the normalized weak energy `weakTheta` is monotone in the radius, `weakTheta Du a s <= weakTheta Du a r` for `0 < s <= r < R0`.

Witness-style monotonicity formula: the increment of `weakTheta` equals the nonnegative annular radial-energy term, `weakTheta Du a r - weakTheta Du a s = weakMonotonicityRhs Du a s r` for `0 < s < r < R0`.

Componentwise convenience wrapper: the same monotonicity inequality stated directly from the local `L^2`, measurability, weak-gradient, and first-variation hypotheses, without first constructing the witness package.

records.title: Split, cograph and threshold graph structures
records.abstract: Connects split partitions, cotrees and threshold creation sequences on Mathlib SimpleGraph. Proves the finite forbidden-induced-subgraph characterizations, split iff chordal and co-chordal, and completeness of cotrees and creation sequences. Supplies certificate-preserving operations, twins and nonempty union/join decompositions for cographs, maximum-clique split partitions, and induced/isomorphic transport of existing chordal elimination orders and clique trees. Classical graph theory is formalized; no new mathematical theorem, canonical certificate or recognition-time bound is claimed.

informal.SimpleGraph.isSplit_iff_forbidden_induce: A finite graph is split iff it contains no induced 2K2, C4 or C5.
informal.SimpleGraph.isSplit_iff_isChordal_and_co: A finite graph is split iff both it and its complement are chordal.
informal.SimpleGraph.isCograph_iff_nonempty_cotre: A finite graph is P4-free iff it is isomorphic to the graph of a cotree, whose constructors are empty, singleton, disjoint union and join.
informal.SimpleGraph.isThreshold_iff_isSplit_and_: A graph has a split partition with nested independent-side neighbourhoods iff it is both split and P4-free. No finiteness is required.
informal.SimpleGraph.isThreshold_iff_forbidden_in: A finite graph is threshold iff it contains no induced 2K2, C4 or P4.
informal.SimpleGraph.isThreshold_iff_nonempty_cre: A finite graph is threshold iff it is isomorphic to a graph constructed from the empty graph by successively adding an isolated or universal vertex.
informal.SimpleGraph.IsCograph.exists_twins: A finite cograph with at least two vertices has two distinct vertices with identical adjacency outside their pair, whether adjacent or not.
informal.SimpleGraph.IsCograph.exists_union_root: A finite cograph that is not preconnected admits a cotree representation with a union root and two nonempty children. This is an existence claim, not a claim about every unreduced cotree.
informal.SimpleGraph.IsCograph.exists_join_root: A preconnected finite cograph with at least two vertices admits a cotree representation with a join root and two nonempty children.
informal.SimpleGraph.IsSplit.exists_partition_wit: Every finite split graph admits a split partition whose clique part has maximum cardinality. Such a partition need not be unique.

records.title: The optimal exponent relating sumsets and difference sets
records.abstract: For a finite integer set A with at least two elements, proves that C(A) = log(|A+A|/|A|) / log(|A-A|/|A|) is strictly below 2, while explicit finite sets have exponents tending to 2. Thus 2 is the supremum and is never attained. Also gives an explicit witness within 10^(-999) of 2. This imports the upstream base-39 row-and-column variant, not the paper's base-12 automaton construction or its quantitative cardinality estimates. Supporting infrastructure includes injective digit expansions and the strict Pluennecke-Petridis equality argument for finite integer sets.

informal.SumDifferenceExponent.growthExponent_lt_: For every finite set A of integers with at least two elements, log(|A+A|/|A|) / log(|A-A|/|A|) is strictly less than 2.
informal.SumDifferenceExponent.tendsto_growthExpo: The growth exponents of the explicit finite integer sets approximatingSet l converge to 2 as l tends to infinity; these sets have at least two elements whenever l is positive.
informal.SumDifferenceExponent.isLUB_admissibleEx: The number 2 is the least upper bound of the growth exponents of all finite integer sets with at least two elements.
informal.SumDifferenceExponent.sSup_admissibleExp: The supremum of the growth exponents of all finite integer sets with at least two elements equals 2.
informal.SumDifferenceExponent.supremum_not_attai: No finite integer set with at least two elements has growth exponent equal to 2.
informal.SumDifferenceExponent.quantitative_examp: The explicitly defined finite integer set quantitativeSet has growth exponent strictly between 2 - 10^(-999) and 2.

records.title: Sums of Three Squares
records.abstract: Formalizes a blueprint step in the three-squares theorem using quadratic forms and geometry of numbers.

informal.LeanPool.SumsThreeSquares.blueprint_case: Proves the mod-8-equals-3 blueprint case for the three-squares theorem.

records.title: Sundog certificates
records.abstract: A referee-free, axiom-clean Lean development of coding-theory certificates: syndrome decoding soundness and lossiness bounds for GF(2) parity-check schemes (with a Reed–Solomon evaluation-dual variant), and a fully machine-checked correctness proof of the Karp reduction chain 3SAT ≤ 3DM ≤ X3C ≤ bounded-weight syndrome decoding. Only the logical iff of each reduction is formalized; polynomial-time bounds, NP classes, and Cook–Levin are unformalized external inputs, so NP-hardness of decoding is conditional on those standard facts.

informal.Sundog.SATReductionMain.sat_iff_decodes: The end-to-end reduction correctness: a formula is satisfiable iff its image under the composed 3SAT-to-decoding reduction is a yes-instance of bounded-weight syndrome decoding.
informal.Sundog.MatchingNPHard.threeDM_iff_X3C: The 3-dimensional matching instance has a perfect matching iff the reduced exact-cover-by-3-sets instance has an exact cover, both directions machine-checked.
informal.Sundog.Certificate.accept_sound: Soundness of the cheap syndrome-decoding verifier when it accepts: an exhibited light same-syndrome witness certifies the body is safe within the decoding radius.
informal.Sundog.Certificate.reject_sound: Soundness of the verifier when it rejects: a sound column-weight lower bound on the minimum same-syndrome weight rules out every light witness, so the body is genuinely unsafe.

records.title: Synthetic Euclidean geometry: Euclid's Elements Book I
records.abstract: Formalizes Book I of Euclid's Elements via an axiomatic synthetic-geometry system (incidence, betweenness, congruence, and area), culminating in the Pythagorean theorem and its converse.

informal.SyntheticEuclid4.IncidenceGeometry: The axiomatic class of synthetic Euclidean geometry, bundling points, lines, circles, and the incidence, betweenness, congruence, and area primitives with Euclid's axioms.
informal.SyntheticEuclid4.square_of_len: Constructs a square on a given segment off a given line.
informal.SyntheticEuclid4.pythagoras_construct: Constructs the three squares and parallelograms on the sides of a triangle used in the proof of the Pythagorean theorem.
informal.SyntheticEuclid4.pythagoras: Euclid I.47, the Pythagorean theorem, that the square on the hypotenuse of a right triangle equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.
informal.SyntheticEuclid4.pythagoras_converse: Euclid I.48, the converse of the Pythagorean theorem, that a triangle whose square areas satisfy the Pythagorean relation has a right angle.

records.title: The Three-Gap (Steinhaus) Theorem
records.abstract: Formalizes the three-gap (Steinhaus, three-distance) theorem: for every real `a` and every `N`, the `N`-point orbit `{i·a mod 1 : i < N}` partitions `[0,1)` into gaps taking at most three distinct lengths, and when exactly three occur the largest is the sum of the other two. The proof works in `[0,1)` via `Int.fract` (not `AddCircle`) through the two first-return times `η⁺` and `η⁻`, and is uniform in the rotation number, covering rational and irrational `a` with no case split.

informal.SteinhausThreeGap.three_gap_card_le_thre: For every real `a` and natural `N`, the gaps of the orbit `{i·a mod 1 : i < N}` take at most three distinct lengths.
informal.SteinhausThreeGap.three_gap_lengths_eq: When the gaps take exactly three distinct lengths, those lengths are precisely the two first returns `η⁺`, `η⁻`, and their sum `η⁺ + η⁻`; in particular the largest gap is the sum of the other two.

records.title: Turán's theorem (the "Book" weighting proof)
records.abstract: Formalizes the weighting/optimization proof of Turán's theorem from Proofs from THE BOOK, bounding the number of edges of a p-clique-free simple graph by (1/2)(1 - 1/(p-1)) n².

informal.Turan3.turans: Turán's theorem — a p-clique-free simple graph on n vertices has at most (1/2)(1 - 1/(p-1)) n² edges.
informal.Turan3.finale_bound: For any weight distribution on a p-clique-free graph, the total edge weight is at most ((p-1)(p-2)/2)·(1/(p-1))², the bound used to derive the edge count.
informal.Turan3.Better_forms_clique: Starting from any weight function, the minimal-support weight-non-decreasing improvement has support that forms a clique.
informal.Turan3.Enhance_total_weight_stricinc: Equalizing weights between a maximum- and minimum-weight vertex in the clique support strictly increases the total edge weight.

records.title: Tutte’s path theorem for matroids
records.abstract: Proves the modular-cut path theorem for finite matroids, with reusable rank-partition, hyperplane-separation, relative-complement, indecomposable-cover, and diamond constructions.

informal.TutteFormalization.path_theorem: In a finite connected matroid, any two hyperplanes containing a proper indecomposable flat and lying outside a modular cut are joined by a finite Tutte path all of whose vertices contain that flat and avoid the cut. Consecutive vertices are distinct hyperplanes with indecomposable corank-two intersection; repeated nonconsecutive vertices are permitted.
informal.TutteFormalization.path_theorem_of_indec: In any finite matroid, two hyperplanes containing an indecomposable flat F and lying outside a modular cut are joined by a Tutte path whose vertices contain F and avoid the cut. This strengthens the cited path theorem by requiring only connectedness of the contraction by F; properness of F follows from containment in an endpoint hyperplane.
informal.TutteFormalization.exists_indecomposable: If an indecomposable flat S and a flat U span the ground, every indecomposable flat T contained in both extends inside S to an indecomposable flat R spanning the ground with U, with corank R equal to rank U minus rank T.
informal.TutteFormalization.exists_relative_compl: For nested flats T contained in S, there is a flat U containing T whose intersection with S is T, whose join with S is the ground, and whose corank equals rank S minus rank T.

records.title: Ulm's theorem for countable reduced abelian p-groups
records.abstract: Formalizes Ulm's classification theorem for countable reduced abelian p-groups in arbitrary Lean universes. The development constructs the transfinite Ulm filtration and invariants, proves their invariance under additive equivalence, establishes Kaplansky's one-generator extension lemma, and completes the countable back-and-forth classification. A finite-group regression distinguishes Z/4 x Z/4 from Z/2 x Z/8 at the zeroth Ulm invariant.

informal.UlmsTheorem.ulm_theorem: For any prime p and any two countable reduced abelian p-groups in the same arbitrary Lean universe, the groups are additively isomorphic if and only if all of their classical Ulm invariants, indexed by universe-zero ordinals, agree.
informal.UlmsTheorem.iso_of_ulm_invariants: Equal Ulm invariants at every universe-zero ordinal imply an additive equivalence between countable reduced abelian p-groups, via finite height-preserving partial isomorphisms and a back-and-forth limit.
informal.UlmsTheorem.ulmInvariant_iso_invariant: An additive equivalence preserves every classical Ulm invariant.
informal.UlmsTheorem.UlmDifferentialRegression.no: The groups Z/4 x Z/4 and Z/2 x Z/8 are not additively isomorphic; the proof exercises the classification theorem and independently detects their different zeroth Ulm invariants.

records.title: Unconditional Schauder Bases
records.abstract: Develops an API for Schauder bases and unconditional Schauder bases of complete normed spaces, including ordered partial-sum convergence, rearrangement criteria for unconditionality, and an arbitrary-index variant built on unconditional summability, then proves a finite sign criterion: a family with dense closed span, nonzero vectors, and a uniform finite sign bound is the basis of an unconditional Schauder basis.

informal.UnconditionalCriterion.exists_unconditio: Finite sign criterion for sequences: if `x : ℕ → E` has dense closed linear span, every `x n` is nonzero, and finite sign changes are uniformly bounded by `C`, then `x` is the basis sequence of an unconditional Schauder basis.

Abstract-index form of the finite sign criterion: under the same dense span, nonzero, and uniform finite sign bound hypotheses for an arbitrarily indexed family, there is an abstractly indexed unconditional Schauder basis whose basis family is exactly `x`.

records.title: Virasoro Project
records.abstract: Formalizes the Virasoro algebra, its Witt-algebra central extension, Verma modules, and the basic bosonic Sugawara construction.

informal.VirasoroProject.VirasoroAlgebra: Defines the Virasoro algebra as a one-dimensional central extension of the Witt algebra.
informal.VirasoroProject.sugawaraRepresentation: Constructs the basic bosonic Sugawara representation of the Virasoro algebra from locally truncated Heisenberg actions.

records.title: Viscosity solutions, Aleksandrov differentiability and harmonic Dirichlet problems
records.abstract: Develops second-order semijets, smooth test-function equivalence, Jensen contact sets, convex Aleksandrov differentiability, the quadratic-penalty Ishii lemma and compact-domain comparison for degenerate elliptic equations. Perron assembly retains explicit comparison, barrier and bumping assumptions; these are discharged for classical harmonic Dirichlet existence on bounded open domains satisfying a uniform exterior sphere condition.

informal.AleksandrovDifferentiability.convexAleks: A convex real-valued function on an open subset of any finite-dimensional real inner product space is second-order differentiable at Lebesgue-almost every point.
informal.ViscositySolns.JensenContactSetPositiveM: Under the localized semiconvexity and strict-contact hypotheses, the contact set arising from sufficiently small linear perturbations has positive Lebesgue measure.
informal.ViscositySolns.QuadraticPenaltyIshiiLemm: For an upper semicontinuous function and a lower semicontinuous function on locally compact subsets of real coordinate space, doubled-variable maxima with the quadratic penalty yield closed semijets satisfying the Ishii block-matrix bounds.
informal.ViscositySolns.comparison_of_constantShi: A viscosity subsolution lies below a supersolution on a nonempty locally compact domain with compact closure, assuming boundary comparison, semicontinuity on the closure, properness, operator continuity, the Ishii structural condition and uniform scalar decrease.
informal.ViscositySolns.viscositySubsolution_iff_: On an open domain, semijet and smooth C² test-function formulations of viscosity subsolutions agree for Hessian-continuous, symmetric-part-invariant operators.
informal.ViscositySolns.dirichlet_harmonic_modulu: On a bounded open subset of finite-dimensional Euclidean space with a uniform exterior sphere condition, Lipschitz data on its closure admit a continuous extension that agrees on the boundary and is C² and harmonic in the domain, with a boundary modulus depending only on the domain and Lipschitz constant.

records.title: Vizing's theorem and equitable edge colourings
records.abstract: Proves the maximum-degree-plus-one edge-colouring bound for finite simple graphs by fans and Kempe exchanges. A separate component-swapping argument equitably rebalances any finite proper edge colouring on its original palette. Together they give equitable proper edge colourings on any palette of at least maximum degree plus one colours, with every class bounded by the ceiling of the average class size. Extracted from the published Paper IV formalization; these are classical colouring results, not a claim to new mathematics or to the paper's clique-partition bound.

informal.LeanPool.Vizing.lineGraph_colorable: The line graph of a finite simple graph G is colourable with maximum degree of G plus one colours.
informal.SimpleGraph.lineGraph_chromaticNumber_le: The chromatic number of the line graph of a finite simple graph G is at most maximum degree of G plus one.
informal.LeanPool.Vizing.Equitable.exists_equitab: Every proper edge colouring of a finite simple graph with a finite palette admits a proper recolouring on the same palette in which any two colour classes differ in size by at most one.
informal.LeanPool.Vizing.exists_equitable_edge_co: For every finite simple graph G and natural c at least maximum degree of G plus one, there is an equitable proper edge colouring with c colours; each colour class has at most ceiling(|E(G)|/c) edges.

records.title: Mean-field derivation and well-posedness of the Vlasov equation
records.abstract: Formalizes the mean-field limit, Dobrushin stability, and forward-in-time well-posedness for the Vlasov equation via Wasserstein-1 optimal transport.

informal.Vlasov.vlasovWellPosedness: Forward-in-time existence of a Lagrangian solution to the Vlasov equation on any finite horizon, for interaction forces that are Lipschitz gradients of an even pair potential (class AssW) — with no smallness restriction on the Lipschitz constant.
informal.Vlasov.dobrushin: A Wasserstein-1 form of Dobrushin's 1979 stability estimate (the original uses a truncated metric) - two Lagrangian Vlasov solutions with finite first moments at every time separate at most at an exponential Gronwall rate.
informal.Vlasov.meanFieldLimit: Conditional mean-field limit - given Wasserstein-1 convergence of the initial empirical data and a uniform Dobrushin stability estimate for the empirical curves, the N-particle empirical measures converge to the Vlasov solution uniformly on any finite horizon.
informal.Vlasov.weak_isLagrangianVlasovSolutionOn: On a time window with L * T^2 < 1, a weak solution with the standing regularity (even C^2 pair potential AssW2, finite first moments, narrow continuity, time-continuity of the convolution force at each point, continuity of the convolution-derivative field, and a uniform spatial first-moment bound on the window) is Lagrangian - the pushforward of its initial datum along the characteristic flow.

records.title: The Wallace problem in ZFC
records.abstract: Formalizes in ZFC a Hausdorff countably compact group topology without nontrivial convergent sequences on every torsion-free Abelian group of cardinality continuum. It specializes the construction to the rational direct sum and the additive real group, and derives a commutative Tychonoff countably compact cancellative semigroup that is not a group.

informal.Wallace.torsionFreeAbelianGroup_mainTheo: Every torsion-free Abelian group of cardinality continuum admits a Hausdorff countably compact group topology with no nontrivial convergent sequences.
informal.Wallace.continuumRationalGroup_and_real_: Both the continuum-indexed rational direct sum and the additive group of real numbers admit such Hausdorff countably compact group topologies without nontrivial convergent sequences.
informal.Wallace.commutativeTychonoffWallaceCount: There exists a commutative Tychonoff countably compact topological semigroup with two-sided cancellation which is not a group.

records.title: Whitehead's theorem for CW-complexes
records.abstract: Formalizes Whitehead's theorem — a continuous map between CW-complexes that induces isomorphisms on all homotopy groups is a homotopy equivalence — including the supporting theory of CW-complexes, relative homotopy groups, the homotopy extension property, and compression of maps.

informal.WhiteheadTheorem: Proves that a continuous map between CW-complexes inducing isomorphisms on all homotopy groups is a homotopy equivalence.

records.title: Irrationality of the Riemann zeta function at five
records.abstract: Proves that Mathlib's Riemann zeta function at five is an irrational real number, following Aabir Fauzan's September 2026 preprint. Constructs integer polynomials of degree 37n with positive values at zeta(5) that decay exponentially in n squared. Includes a general integer-polynomial irrationality criterion, Hankel determinant and moment-integral identities, logarithmic-energy estimates, prime-adic integrality bounds, and kernel-checked rational certificates. The formalization uses a different normalizer and a positive decay constant in place of the paper's specific constant 139/5. Reuses the prime number theorem infrastructure already in the MooreBound project.

informal.Zeta5Irrational.irrational_five: There exists an irrational real number x whose complex coercion equals Mathlib's Riemann zeta function evaluated at five.
informal.Zeta5Irrational.main_estimate: There is a positive real c such that, for all sufficiently large n, an integer polynomial Q of degree 37n is a positive rational multiple of the constructed determinant polynomial and satisfies 0 < Q(zeta(5)) < exp(-c*n^2).
informal.Zeta5Irrational.irrational_of_eventually: A real xi is irrational if, eventually, integer polynomials of degree at most d(n) have positive values at xi bounded by epsilon(n), and b^d(n)*epsilon(n) tends to zero for every positive natural b.

records.title: Thakur's hypotheses on power sums of F_q[t]
records.abstract: Formalizes four components of Thakur's hypotheses on power sums over finite polynomial rings, including uniqueness and monotonicity results for the carry-free digit optimization problems and the Laurent-series expansion of finite-field power sums.

informal.ZetaH123.H1.main_theorem: Proves uniqueness of the admissible base-q decomposition maximizing the H1 power-sum weight functional.
informal.ZetaH123.H2.main: Proves the H2 unique-minimizer statement for the recursive digit/carry-free optimization problem defining the values s_d(k).
informal.ZetaH123.H3.main_theorem: Proves the H3 monotonicity statement that s_d(k) is strictly less than s_d(k+1) when p does not divide k.
informal.ZetaH123.Lem41.main: Proves the Lemma 4.1 Laurent-series expansion for S_d(k), with nonzero coefficients indexed by the carry-free tuples.

records.title: Simple zeros of the Riemann zeta function
records.abstract: Formalizes Lamzouri's Hilbert-space proof of lower bounds for simple and distinct zeros of the Riemann zeta function. From explicit Riemann--von Mangoldt and unconditional pair-correlation hypotheses, the development proves that eventually more than 67.25% of nontrivial zeros are simple and on the critical line and more than 83.625% are distinct. It includes the finite-multiset Hilbert-space inequality, zeta-zero multiplicity symmetries, an admissible cutoff construction, and certified trigonometric estimates.

informal.ZetaZeros.simple_proportion_d4: Assuming the stated Riemann--von Mangoldt and unconditional pair-correlation formulas, beyond some height more than 67.25% of nontrivial zeta zeros are simple and lie on the critical line.
informal.ZetaZeros.distinct_proportion_d5: Under the same two explicit analytic hypotheses, beyond some height more than 83.625% of nontrivial zeta zeros are distinct.
informal.ZetaZeros.card_simpleRealPart_lower: Bounds from below the number of multiplicity-one real points in a finite nonempty conjugation-invariant multiset using the squared test-kernel sum of any admissible function.
informal.ZetaZeros.card_lower: Bounds from below the number of distinct points in a finite nonempty conjugation-invariant multiset using the same Hilbert-space kernel method.

records.title: Linear independence of 1, zeta(2), and zeta(3)
records.abstract: Proves that 1, the Riemann zeta function at 2, and its value at 3 are linearly independent over the rationals, using integer polynomial approximation, p-adic coefficient bounds, prime-edge nonvanishing, and logarithmic potential energy estimates for Hankel determinants. Includes reusable irrationality criteria, contour integration, Andreief identities, Newton-basis valuation bounds, and energy inequalities for finite measures. The cited source is the completed Lean proof; independent novelty of the informal argument is not claimed.

informal.Zeta32.one_zeta_two_zeta_three_linearInd: The three complex numbers 1, riemannZeta 2, and riemannZeta 3 are linearly independent over the rational numbers.
informal.Zeta32Acceptance.one_zeta_two_zeta_three: For rational a, b, and c, if a plus b times the real sum of 1/(k+1)^2 plus c times the real sum of 1/(k+1)^3 is zero, then all three coefficients are zero; both sums range over natural numbers k.
informal.Zeta32.zeta3_sub_rat_mul_zeta2_irrationa: For every rational r, the real series for zeta(3) minus r times the real series for zeta(2) is irrational.

records.title: Irrationality of ζ(3)
records.abstract: Formalizes Beukers' proof of Apéry's theorem for ζ(3), including the integral identities, denominator estimates, positivity, upper bounds, and final irrationality contradiction.

informal.LeanPool.Zeta3Irrational.linear_int: Clears denominators in the Apéry integral to produce a linear form in 1 and ζ(3).
informal.LeanPool.Zeta3Irrational.JJ_pos: Proves positivity of the transformed Beukers-Apéry integral.
informal.LeanPool.Zeta3Irrational.JJ_upper: Bounds the Beukers-Apéry integral by a geometric factor times the ζ(3) series.
informal.LeanPool.Zeta3Irrational.fun1_tendsto_ze: Shows that the denominator-cleared Apéry linear forms tend to zero.

records.title: ZFLean
records.abstract: Develops a practical ZFC set-theory framework with von Neumann naturals, integers, rationals, functions, embeddings, isomorphisms, booleans, and sums.

informal.ZFSet.isIso_of_biembedding: Proves a Cantor-Bernstein theorem for ZF sets.
informal.ZFSet.ZFNat.induction: Provides induction for the von Neumann natural numbers.
informal.ZFSet.ZFInt.induction: Provides induction for the quotient construction of ZF integers.

records.title: The Zhang-Yeung non-Shannon information inequality
records.abstract: Formalizes the Zhang-Yeung inequality, the first known non-Shannon-type entropy inequality, together with its dual and averaged forms derived through the copy lemma.

informal.ZhangYeung.zhangYeung: Proves the Zhang-Yeung non-Shannon-type information inequality for four discrete random variables.
informal.ZhangYeung.zhangYeung_dual: Proves the dual form of the Zhang-Yeung inequality.
informal.ZhangYeung.zhangYeung_averaged: Proves the averaged symmetric form of the Zhang-Yeung inequality.

records.title: The Arithmetic of Time: chirality of the Padovan substitution
records.abstract: A kernel-checked chirality package for the Padovan substitution (0 ↦ 1, 1 ↦ 2, 2 ↦ 01 on Fin 3; its incidence matrix has characteristic polynomial x³ − x − 1, an orientation fact that is not used or compared). Three compared theorems, all at the iterate-factor level — they quantify over factors of the concrete words S^[n] [x], never over an abstract subshift. (1) The successor invariant: in every positive iterate from any seed, the letter 0 ("a") is immediately followed by 1 ("b"). (2) Chirality: the word 20 ("ca") is a factor of an iterate while its reversal 02 ("ac") is a factor of no iterate from any seed — the factor language reads differently backwards — proved from the invariant, with no enumeration on the ac side. (3) No palindromic factor: no factor of length ≥ 4 of any iterate from any seed (including the zeroth iterate) is a palindrome, via a complete length-≤5 window certificate for the seed a together with the index shift S [0] = [1], S [1] = [2], which exhibits every seed's iterate as a seed-a iterate. These are the three compared statements of the registered record (PALOMAR-2026-08-19-000006 at revision c48eb12), unchanged in this revision. The uniqueness results proved in this repository (Supplement.lean: padovan_minimal_unique, padovan_eigenvalue_unique, padovan_matrix_unique, pisot_ge_plastic, padovan_rules_chiral) are registered separately as PALOMAR-2026-10-18-000019 (stalex444/arithmetic-of-time-slowest-clock, revision 49eafbab4af8899b2a66469697bf74683a88ce87), which compares them over s, mir, inc and sub. Everything else in this repository is public and kernel-checked but not compared: among it the exact orientation threshold (padovan_exact_orientation_threshold_four), the irrationality of the distinguished slope (Time.beta_irrational), mirror identities for arbitrary substitutions, a rate identity, and the characteristic polynomial and chirality of a twelve-letter substitution for ρQ.

records.title: Exponential separation of analytic self-conformal sets on the real line: Lean formalisation
records.abstract: Lean 4 formalisation of exponential separation for analytic iterated function systems on the real line. Strong exponential separation holds on an open and dense subset in the C2 topology and follows from an explicit criterion involving dual projections. The development characterises conjugacy to self-similar systems and proves dimension consequences, including a drop in the L^q dimensions of the natural measure of a concrete three-map example, together with the cited results of Rapaport and Bowen.

records.title: The Hajnal–Szemerédi theorem on equitable colourings
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Hajnal–Szemerédi theorem (1970), conjectured by Erdős in 1964: every finite graph with maximum degree at most r has an equitable proper colouring with r + 1 colours, i.e. a proper colouring whose colour classes differ in size by at most one. The exact form is also proved: if the number of vertices is s(r + 1), every colour class has exactly s vertices (the colouring form of Erdős Problem #914). Version 2 adds the form with any number k > Δ(G) of colours (Mathlib's SimpleGraph.maxDegree), deduced from the theorem with r = k − 1. The proof follows the short argument of Kierstead and Kostochka (2008): induction on the number of edges; after deleting an edge, a nearly equitable colouring is repaired by moving vertices along paths of an auxiliary digraph on the colour classes (Lemma 2.1); when the large class is inaccessible, a family of terminal classes, solo edges and a discharging count with weights q/|S_z| (Lemmas 2.2–2.3) produce a recolouring that either finishes the colouring or strictly increases the number of accessible classes, using the induction hypothesis on the inaccessible part. The general case is reduced to the divisible one by adding a disjoint complete graph.

records.title: Vizing's theorem and equitable edge colourings
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Vizing's theorem: every finite simple graph G has a proper edge colouring with Δ(G) + 1 colours, stated with Mathlib's line graph (G.lineGraph is (Δ(G) + 1)-colourable, hence χ'(G) ≤ Δ(G) + 1), proved with fans and Kempe chain exchanges. It also proves the equitable refinement: for every c ≥ Δ(G) + 1 there is a proper edge colouring with colours Fin c in which any two colour classes (including unused colours) differ in size by at most one (McDiarmid 1972), obtained by balancing a Vizing colouring with alternating-component moves that strictly decrease a square energy. Version 2 adds the lower bound Δ(G) ≤ χ'(G) (the edges at a vertex of maximum degree form a clique of the line graph) and hence the dichotomy χ'(G) ∈ {Δ(G), Δ(G) + 1} (class 1 / class 2).

records.title: Wagner's planarity criterion and list colouring of planar and K5-minor-free graphs
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of classical results on planar graphs and graphs without a K5 minor. (1) Wagner's theorem (1937): a finite graph is planar if and only if it has neither K5 nor K3,3 as a minor. (2) Škrekovski's theorem (1998): every finite graph without a K5 minor is 5-choosable, proved along the route of Wood and Linusson, and Thomassen's theorem (1994) that every finite planar graph is 5-choosable, as a corollary. (3) DP-colouring: every finite graph without a K5 minor (Li–Wang, 2022), hence every finite planar graph (Dvořák–Postle, 2018), is DP-5-colourable. (4) Voigt's theorem (1993): an explicit planar graph on 238 vertices with lists of four colours has no proper list colouring, so 5 cannot be lowered to 4; its planarity and non-colourability are checked by kernel reduction. (5) Wagner's equivalence of the Four Colour Theorem with Hadwiger's conjecture for K5 (neither side is proved). (6) Wagner's structure theorem (1937, added in version 2): a finite graph has no K5 minor if and only if it is a spanning subgraph of a graph obtained by clique-sums of order at most three, keeping the clique edges, from planar graphs and copies of the Wagner graph V8. Planarity is defined combinatorially, by rotation systems of genus zero (Euler defect 0); as sanity checks K4 is planar and K5, K3,3 are not.

records.title: Near-regular hypergraph matchings and the asymptotic triangle-packing gap
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of four results. (1) A finite nibble theorem: r-uniform hypergraphs whose degrees are at most (1+μ)d everywhere and at least (1−μ)d outside an exceptional set of at most η|V| vertices, with codegrees at most μd, have matchings with at least (1−β)|V|/r edges. (2) The fractional–integral triangle-packing gap is o(n²) uniformly over finite graphs: every large graph has an edge-disjoint triangle family P such that every fractional triangle packing has weight at most |P| + εn² (the triangle case of Haxell–Rödl). (3) The cover form: a fractional triangle cover of weight at most |P| + εn² exists. (4) Version 2, the transfer form used in decomposition theory: every large graph on n vertices that has a fractional triangle decomposition has an edge-disjoint triangle family covering all but at most ηn² edges; it follows from (2), since a fractional decomposition is a fractional packing of weight e(G)/3 and a packing P covers exactly 3|P| edges. The proof of (1)–(3) combines a nibble with second-moment and Freedman-type concentration, a low-degree core reduction, Mathlib's Szemerédi regularity lemma with a cluster linear program rounded by explicit designs, and LP duality.

records.title: Mader's theorem and Hadwiger's conjecture for t ≤ 4
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Mader's theorem (a nonempty finite graph of average degree at least 2^(r−2) has a K_r minor), of Dirac's lemma (a graph without a K4 minor has a vertex of degree at most two, hence at most 2n − 3 edges for n ≥ 2), of Mader's bound for K5 (a graph on n ≥ 3 vertices with at least 3n − 5 edges has a K5 minor; equivalently, without a K5 minor it has at most 3n − 6 edges; added in version 2), and of Hadwiger's conjecture for t ≤ 4 (graphs without a K3 minor are 2-colourable, graphs without a K4 minor are 3-colourable). Minors are branch-set models.

records.title: FixedOrderFactor: the order-r correction factor for mean squares of L(1, chi), and the factor 35/34
records.abstract: For an integer r >= 2 and a finite set N of primes, the random Euler product model for Dirichlet characters of order r replaces chi(q) by independent uniform r-th roots of unity. The development proves that the order-r local factor E|1 - z/q|^(-2) equals (1 + q^-r)/((1 - q^-2)(1 - q^-r)), that its ratio to the full-circle factor (1 - q^-2)^(-1), multiplied over the primes outside N, is zeta^(N)(r)^2 / zeta^(N)(2r), that this correction factor is also the sum of (ab)^-r over the coprime pairs of integers prime to N, and that the model mean is zeta^(N)(2) zeta^(N)(r)^2 / zeta^(N)(2r). The factor exceeds 1, decreases strictly in r and tends to 1; for r = 2k and N empty it equals -binom(4k,2k) B_{2k}^2/(2 B_{4k}). For r = 4 and N = {2} it is 35/34, the ratio by which the limit of Louboutin's mean square of L(1, chi) with the factor at 2 removed changes when the average is restricted to quartic characters; with the forced factor 4/5 at 2 the development also proves the constants pi^2/10, 7 pi^2/68, 7 pi^2/36 and 7/136 = (1/20)(35/34) = (7/72)(9/17). It also identifies the pairs the model keeps: for positive m, n the average of z^m conj(z^n) is 1 exactly when m/n is an r-th power in Q, that is when (m, n) = (d a^r, d b^r) with a, b coprime, and 0 otherwise. Modulo a single prime p with r | p - 1 it proves the finite-character counterpart: there are exactly r Dirichlet characters mod p with chi^r = 1, the sum of chi(a) conj(chi(b)) over them is r when a/b is a nonzero r-th power mod p and 0 otherwise, so every pair (d a^r, d b^r) prime to p survives with sum r; by contrast, summed over all characters mod p, chi(m) conj(chi(n)) has sum 0 for distinct m, n < p. Release v1.2 adds the finite part of the Chebyshev bias in families p = a (mod M) of fixed order r: with rho_s(t) the average of exp(2 pi i u t/s) over the units u mod s, the sum over t < s of rho_s(c t) is s when s | c and 0 otherwise; for M > 0 and s | M the squares in Z/s x| (Z/M)^x give the prime-square term of the explicit formula as s times the square-root count beta(M, a, s) = #{y in (Z/M)^x : y^2 = a, y = -1 (mod s)}, a count of residue classes (the same finite-sum identity over the representatives 0 <= x < M holds for all M and s > 0, but is only an arithmetic identity there: vacuous at M = 0, representative-dependent when s does not divide M); beta does not decrease as s decreases along divisibility, at s = r it is 0 unless a is a square in H = ker((Z/M)^x -> (Z/r)^x) and is then the number of square roots of 1 in H; and for the imaginary families (r even, M = 2r, a = 1 + r) beta vanishes for every s unless 8 | r, and for s = r/d with d odd in every case.

records.title: Fifth dimension subgroups: D₅ = γ₅ when G/γ₂ is finite of exponent 3, candidates for a counterexample, and a reduction of Kourovka 20.84
records.abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization accompanying S. Vorobev, "On the inclusion D_5(G) ⊆ γ_4(G): reductions, the Lie-ring proof, and evidence" (preprint, 2026; submitted to arXiv math.GR on 2026-10-22). The integral dimension subgroups D_n(G) = {g ∈ G : g − 1 ∈ Δ(G)^n} are defined from the augmentation ideal of Mathlib's integral group ring. Kourovka Problem 20.84 asks whether D_5(G) ⊆ γ_4(G) for every group; it is open and is not claimed here. Unconditional results: D_5(G) = γ_5(G) whenever G/γ_2(G) is finite of exponent 3, and more generally whenever G/γ_2(G) is a finite 3-group whose cubes form a cyclic group, and still more generally whenever G/γ_2(G) is a finite 3-group and γ_2(G)/γ_3(G) has exponent at most 3, and still more generally whenever G/γ_2(G) is a finite 3-group, γ_4(G)^3 ⊆ γ_5(G) and γ_2(G)^9 ⊆ γ_4(G), and most generally whenever G/γ_2(G) is a finite 3-group and γ_4(G)^3 ⊆ γ_5(G) (paper, Theorems 6.6, 6.8, 6.9, 6.10 and 6.11), and whenever G/γ_2(G) is a finite p-group, p odd, and [γ_2(G), γ_2(G)] ⊆ γ_5(G), in particular for finite metabelian 3-groups, which is Gupta–Tahara's theorem at p = 3 (paper, Theorem D.1; the inclusion part of Tahara's 1981 description of D_5 is formalized for this); D_5(G) lies in the Jennings product M_5(G) for finite 2-groups of class at most 3; and, for "candidates" (the paper's minimal-counterexample shape among finite 2-groups of class 3), there is no candidate of order 2^11 with Q/P_3 ≅ Z/4 × (Z/2)^7 and none of order 2^11 and rank at least 8 (paper, Lemma 5.6 and Proposition 5.7); the reduction of Problem 20.84 to finite 2-groups of class exactly 3 (Proposition 2.1); and a minimal counterexample is a candidate (Lemma 5.2). The proofs of the last two use D_3 = γ_3, Passi's D_4^2 ⊆ γ_4 and Gruenberg's residual theorem, all proved in the development (dThreeEqGammaThree, passiDFourSquare, gruenbergResidualTwo). One conditional result, with the assumption an explicit hypothesis: D_5 = 1 for groups of order 2^11, class at most 3 and rank at least 8, assuming the paper's computer result for order 2^10 (Proposition 5.7, D_5 form, assuming Proposition 5.3).

records.title: Temporal cliques admit linear spanners
records.abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the theorem that every temporal clique on n vertices admits a temporal spanner with at most 7n edges. A temporal clique is the complete graph on a finite vertex set whose edges carry natural-number time labels, locally injective (two edges sharing an endpoint have distinct labels); a temporal spanner is a set of edges in which every vertex reaches every other one by a journey with non-decreasing labels. The result and its proof are due to Júlia Baligács (arXiv:2606.05156, 2026): the dismountability of Carnevale, Casteigts and Corsini (SAND 2025) reduces cliques to extremally matched bi-cliques, which are then covered by simple and extended stars. The compared statements give the explicit bound 7n and the asymptotic O(n) form with a bound function chosen uniformly for all cliques. They use the same definitions as the registered O(n log n) entry of the same repository. The work is supervised by Arnaud Casteigts and Karine Altisen.

records.title: An explicit version of Chen's theorem assuming the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis
records.abstract: A Lean 4 proof, conditional on the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis and on four cited results, that every even integer N at least e^{e^{13.375}} is the sum of a prime and a square-free number greater than 1 with at most two prime factors. The four cited inputs are explicit hypotheses of the theorem, never axioms: Thm5J, Thm6J and Thm7J, the Lean Lab's transcriptions of Theorems 5, 6 and 7 of M. Bordignon and V. Starichkova, An explicit version of Chen's theorem assuming the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, Ramanujan J. 64, 2024, 1213 to 1242; and LinearSieveT4 1/8349 112 114, the transcription of their Theorem 4, the explicit linear sieve of Bordignon, Johnston and Starichkova with the Table 1 row epsilon inverse 6100, C1 = 112, C2 = 114. In version 2 each of Thm5J, Thm6J and Thm7J also takes 0 <= C1 and 0 <= C2 as premises right after the sieve hypothesis, matching Table 1, which lists positive constants only. These transcriptions use the Lean normalisation U_N = 2 e^{-gamma} C2 Pi_N, twice the U_N printed in the journal; see the fidelity section. GRH for Dirichlet L-functions is the premise inside the conclusion ChenThreshold13375. The journal's own Corollary 1 has the threshold e^{e^{14}}; the threshold e^{e^{13.375}} comes from re-choosing the Section 5.4 parameters inside the authors' method, alpha = 0.00256, A = 10, u = 1500, epsilon = 1/8349, epsilon1 = 10^-20. The numeric inputs are proved here: epsilon at 1500 is below 1/8349 by a kernel certificate, decide +kernel in eleven window modules, and the Section 5.4 bracket combination is at least the main-term constant minus 10^-5, a one-sided lower bound. Chen's weighted inequality, the journal's Lemma 9, is proved unconditionally. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. An AI agent, Claude, wrote all the Lean code; the statements were checked against the paper by AI agents and are offered for human audit.

records.title: Combinatorics and probabilities of Kingman coalescent trees: histories, shapes, topologies, root splits, Colless, and Sackin
records.abstract: This entry formalizes combinatorics and probabilities of trees under Kingman's coalescent, through its embedded jump chain, in which each pair of the k current lineages is the next to merge with probability 1/binomial(k, 2). A ranked labelled history on n leaves is a sequence of n − 1 merges starting from n singletons; there are n!(n − 1)!/2^(n−1) of them, and each has probability 2^(n−1)/(n!(n − 1)!). Ranked and unranked tree shapes are defined as classes of histories under relabelling of the leaves; their numbers satisfy André's recurrence for alternating permutations, shifted by one, and the Wedderburn–Etherington recurrence, respectively, with the cases n = 1 and n = 2. The probability of a labelled rooted binary topology T is 2^(n−1)/(n! ∏(|C| − 1)), the product running over the clades C of T with at least two leaves. The probability that the root splits the leaves into a given set A and its complement is 2/((n − 1) binomial(n, |A|)). The probability that a sample S of a population of N leaves has the population root as its most recent common ancestor is (|S| − 1)(N + 1)/((|S| + 1)(N − 1)), which tends to (n − 1)/(n + 1) for a sample of fixed size n as N tends to infinity. The expected Colless and Sackin indices are n H_{⌊n/2⌋} − 2⌊n/2⌋ and 2n(H_n − 1), where H_m is the m-th harmonic number. Finally, the process of roots of the forest histories is identified with the jump chain of Kingman's partition-valued coalescent, for one step and for t steps.

records.title: Linked-pair panels: panel laws are determined by finitely many Laplace values
records.abstract: This entry formalizes panels of linked site pairs observed through a reporting channel, with the pair coalescence time T following a probability law on the non-negative reals. All L sites of a panel share the same time T; given T = t, the sites are reported independently, and at each site the two lineages share one latent type with weight e^(−kt) and have independent types otherwise, each type being reported through a channel that maps K latent types to probability distributions on a finite set of labels. For an informative channel (one whose rows are not all equal) and a panel of length L, the panel laws of two time laws agree for all outcomes if and only if their Laplace transforms agree at the points rk for r = 0, …, L. If the channel erases all information, every panel law agrees. If the transforms agree up to L and differ at the next point, then panels of length L agree but some panel of length L + 1 differs. For k > 0, agreement of all panels of all lengths is equivalent to equality of the time laws.

records.title: Neutral fixation probability in exchangeable (Cannings) models
records.abstract: This entry formalizes the neutral fixation probability in exchangeable (Cannings) models with N individuals. For a non-degenerate model, the probability that the allele count started from i copies ever reaches N equals i/N, and the same holds for eventual absorption in the fixed state. The loss probability is 1 − i/N. For a degenerate model started away from the full state the probability of fixation is 0, and an example with N = 2 shows that the fixation probability can differ from the frequency without a reachability hypothesis. For N ≥ 2, non-degeneracy is shown equivalent to positive-probability reachability of the boundary {0, N} by the count chain, and to each of three conditions on the offspring number of a single parent. A general fixation statement is given for chains on {0, ..., N} whose state is mean-preserving in one step and from which the boundary {0, N} is reachable. The Moran model is shown to be non-degenerate with fixation probability i/N.

records.title: Shannon's theorem on edge colourings of multigraphs
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Shannon's theorem (1949): every finite loopless multigraph of maximum degree at most Δ has a proper edge colouring with ⌊3Δ/2⌋ colours; and its sharpness: for every Δ the Shannon triangle (three vertices with ⌊Δ/2⌋, ⌊Δ/2⌋ and ⌈Δ/2⌉ parallel edges between the three pairs) has maximum degree at most Δ and no proper edge colouring with fewer than ⌊3Δ/2⌋ colours. Multigraphs are edge families ends : ι → V × V (parallel edges allowed), a lighter representation than Mathlib's multigraph structure Graph α β (Mathlib.Combinatorics.Graph.Basic: vertex and edge sets with an incidence relation IsLink), which at the pinned revision has no degrees or edge colourings; no bridge to Graph α β is proved. Neither result is in Mathlib.

records.title: No formula with denominators of bounded degree, in the total mutation parameter or in rho, for the two-locus sampling recursion
records.abstract: This entry formalizes results on the degree of denominators of any closed-form expression for the solution of the two-locus sampling recursion of the coalescent with recombination, with two alleles at each locus and parent-independent mutation. The mutation rates, the recombination rate rho, and the allele frequencies are independent indeterminates, and the recursion is solved over a field of rational functions in them. An expression is built from rational constants, arbitrary coefficients from the coefficient field, the rates, sums, products, and quotients; it is admissible at degree D when every divisor evaluates to a nonzero polynomial of degree at most D in a designated variable (rho, or the total mutation rate theta_A + theta_B). A closure lemma shows that admissible expressions in inputs with bounded denominators have bounded denominators. For the sample of two lineages that carry the same haplotype at both loci, no admissible expression of degree one in rho, and none of degree two in the total mutation rate, equals the value of the solution; variants bound the total degree of the divisors in the three rates instead. For the samples of m lineages typed at locus A only and m typed at locus B only, all of allele 0, for every bound D there is an m ≥ 2 at which no admissible expression of degree D, in the total mutation rate or in rho, equals the value of the solution. Existence and uniqueness of the solutions are also stated in these settings.

records.title: Weak mixing times minimality: transitivity of the product
records.abstract: A continuous weakly mixing self-map of a nonempty compact Hausdorff space has a transitive actual heterogeneous product with any continuous pointwise forward-minimal self-map of a nonempty compact space. Surjectivity, arbitrarily late thick hitting blocks, syndetic hitting gaps and their intersection are proved.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: A partition-pair decomposition of the two-locus sampling probability with Ewens marginals
records.abstract: This entry formalizes a decomposition of the two-locus sampling probability, under finite-allele parent-independent mutation, in terms of pairs of set partitions of the sample, with Ewens marginals at each locus. A partition-carrying ancestral process with coalescence, mutation, and recombination records, at each locus, which sample members lose their ancestry to the same mutation; the kernel is the probability that it ends with a given pair of partitions. The solution of the two-locus sampling recursion at a fully typed sample is the sum over pairs of partitions of the kernel times the probability that each block receives a single allele consistent with the sample. Summing the kernel over the partition at one locus gives the Ewens partition probability at the other; as the recombination rate tends to infinity the kernel tends to the product of the two Ewens partition probabilities; and with recombination rate 0 the common refinement of the two partitions has the Ewens law with parameter θA + θB. The sampling probability equals the product of its one-locus marginals for all parameter values exactly when at most one lineage is typed at one of the loci (with at least two alleles per locus). A closed form for configurations with two lineages typed at each locus is also stated, together with existence of a solution of the recursion.

records.title: The two-locus sampling recursion of the coalescent with recombination: existence, uniqueness, and probabilistic interpretation
records.abstract: This entry formalizes the two-locus sampling recursion of the coalescent with recombination, with finitely many alleles at each locus and parent-independent mutation. For positive mutation rates and nonnegative recombination rate, a solution exists and is unique, over any linearly ordered field. For real parameters, the solution at a sample typed at both loci equals the probability that the typed ancestral recombination graph, in which a mutation removes the ancestry of a lineage at that locus and assigns a type to the sample members it carries, ends with exactly the types of the sample. The solution sums to 1 over all typings of a sample of given size, tends to the product of the one-locus sampling probabilities as the recombination rate tends to infinity, and at recombination rate 0 gives a solution of a one-locus recursion on pairs of alleles. With mutation rates 0, the expected total branch length of the genealogy at locus A of a sample of size n is 2 times the sum of 1/(i + 1) for i < n − 1. The transition matrix of the typed ancestral chain is shown to be nonnegative with unit row sums.

records.title: Seven linked sites separate a two-island history from every panmictic history
records.abstract: This entry formalizes a statement about blocks of seven completely linked sites with K ≥ 2 equally weighted roots, observed in three sampled sequences under an equal-rates K-state mutation model. A specific two-island history for three lineages (all three lineages start in the same island, the coalescence rate within an island is 1, and the migration rate is 1/100) produces, at mutation scale 1, a law of the seven-site block that differs from the block law of every panmictic history at every mutation scale k > 0. The panmictic histories are those given by a nonnegative locally integrable pairwise coalescence rate whose integrated clock diverges, so the population size may vary arbitrarily in time.

records.title: Total variation bound between an unpruned ancestral recombination process and SMC' on pairwise coalescence times
records.abstract: This entry formalizes a total variation bound between the pairwise coalescence-time process of an unpruned ancestral recombination graph and the SMC' approximation, for N ≥ 1 samples, a unit-length genome, and scaled recombination rate R ≥ 0. The observed object is the collection of pairwise coalescence times of all sample pairs at every rational position in [0, 1). The total variation distance is at most an explicit double bound, which is at most min(1, R² times a quadratic coefficient in N − 1). The distance is 0 for one sample and for zero recombination. Supporting statements show that the event kernels of both processes are Markov, the two laws are probability measures, the number of live lineages of the backward process reaches at most one almost surely, the observed coalescence times are almost surely finite, and the expected number of active events, the expected total time, and the expected largest observed coalescence time are bounded by an explicit absorption budget.

records.title: Tajima's D under Kingman's coalescent: moments of the numerator, the variance estimate, and the expected spectrum
records.abstract: This entry formalizes Tajima's D under Kingman's coalescent with infinitely many sites and mutation parameter θ ≥ 0, for sample size n ≥ 2. The joint law of the genealogy and the mutation counts on its branches is a probability measure. The mean of the numerator is 0 and its variance equals c₁ θ + c₂ θ², where c₁ and c₂ are Tajima's coefficients. The covariance of the pairwise-difference statistic with the number of segregating sites and the mean of their product are stated. The variance estimate based on the number of segregating sites is unbiased for that variance. The expected value of the site frequency spectrum at frequency i is θ/i for 1 ≤ i < n, and these values sum to the mean number of segregating sites; the closed-form coefficient of the expected spectrum equals θ/i and equals that mean. D is defined to be 0 when the variance estimate is nonpositive, and as a result it is 0 when there are no segregating sites and for n = 2 and n = 3; D is a measurable function of the sample.

records.title: When one finite block of linked sites separates a three-sample genealogy from every panmictic history
records.abstract: This entry formalizes conditions under which a single finite block of linked sites separates a three-sample genealogy from every panmictic history. A law of the two coalescence-interval lengths and the tree shape of three sampled sequences is uniformly separated at mutation scale k > 0 when some block of L completely linked sites, observed under the equal-rates mutation model, has a law at ℓ1 distance at least a fixed ε > 0 from the block law of every panmictic history (any nonnegative, locally integrable, time-varying coalescence rate with a diverging integrated clock), at every mutation scale and for every alphabet size K ≥ 2. For laws with nonnegative interval lengths, a positive first coalescence time, and a regular first-survival profile matching the first coalescence time, uniform separation holds if and only if the law differs from the panmictic law with the profile's rate, in which the tree shape is uniform and independent of the times; a version for laws of the interval lengths alone, with a uniform independent shape, is also given. For three-sample symmetric island histories with time-varying coalescence and migration rates under the stated integrability hypotheses, uniform separation holds if and only if the history is not the one with all three lineages starting in the same island, no migration, and a diverging integrated coalescence clock. For finite-phase histories, separation is equivalent to failure of a density identity characterizing the panmictic form.

records.title: Classical identities and a limit theorem of selection theory
records.abstract: This entry collects classical identities and a limit theorem from selection theory. The identities are stated for finite populations; Geiringer's limit theorem is stated for the deterministic infinite-population recombination model on finitely many loci with a common finite allele set. Fisher's fundamental theorem is stated, in Ewens' interpretation, as the equality of the partial change in mean fitness (the change in allele frequencies under selection, weighted by least-squares average effects) with the additive genetic variance divided by mean fitness, for arbitrary genotype frequencies and any number of loci, together with nonnegativity of that change. A grouped covariance decomposition and a multilevel Price equation are stated as identities for arbitrary weights. Hamilton's rule is derived from the least-squares regression of fitness on own and social genotypes, and the existence of the Lande–Arnold gradient, equal to the inverse phenotypic covariance matrix applied to the vector of selection differentials, is stated under a nonsingular phenotypic covariance. Geiringer's theorem is stated as convergence of repeated recombination to the product of the single-locus marginals, under the condition that every pair of loci is separated with positive probability.

records.title: Weak mixing and thick common multi-sensitivity
records.abstract: A continuous surjective weakly mixing map on a nontrivial metric space admits one positive separation constant such that every finite family of nonempty open sets has arbitrarily long, arbitrarily late blocks of common positive separation times. Witness pairs may depend on the set and time. Finite-family common hitting thickness and separated open targets are proved.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: On the local geometry of the tight 39-point code in 𝕆P²
records.abstract:
Cohn, Kumar and Minton constructed a universally optimal code of thirty-nine points in the octonionic projective plane 𝕆P², whose existence was conjectured by Hoggar. Its points form thirteen mutually unbiased Jordan frames, and a four-parameter phase family deforms the code through such configurations. This Lean development describes their local geometry under the automorphism group F₄. At every nonresonant phase, every nearby real solution of the defining equations belongs to one of four smooth families of labelled configurations. In a local slice for F₄, their union has normal form R⁴ × ⋃ᵢ₌₁⁴ R⁶ᵢ, with the R⁶ᵢ in direct sum. The distance to the localized family union is bounded by a phase-dependent constant times the square root of the residual, and the exponent 1/2 is sharp in the ambient configuration space. On an explicit open dense subset of the nonresonant phases, the complexified families are exactly the top-dimensional components of the complex solution germ, each generically reduced. Every neighbourhood of the original code in the space of unlabelled tight 39-point codes modulo F₄ contains points of local dimension 10.

The results are local, the resonant germ at the original code is not classified, and lower-dimensional complex components are not excluded. For exact frames and strongly convex C² overlap potentials, we prove a two-sided comparison of the energy gap with squared overlap errors and, near each nonresonant orbit, a quartic lower bound in distance to the localized family union. Except for attributed third-party material, all text and code are AI-generated under Robert R. MacGregor’s direction. Robert is an amateur who welcomes collaboration (macgregor@gmail.com).

records.title: On the sum of a prime and a square-free number
records.abstract: Conditional on one explicit hypothesis, AP12Lower 0.21, taken as a hypothesis of the theorem and never as an axiom: for every integer x >= 10^9, each reduced residue class mod 12 holds more than 0.21 x / log x primes p <= x. Under it, a complete Lean 4 proof of Theorem 1 of A. W. Dudek, On the sum of a prime and a square-free number, The Ramanujan Journal 42, 2017: every integer N > 2 is the sum of a prime and a square-free number. AP12Lower 0.21 is implied by Corollary 1.6 of M. A. Bennett, G. Martin, K. O'Bryant and A. Rechnitzer, Explicit bounds for primes in arithmetic progressions, Illinois J. Math. 62, 2018, which gives 1/4 in place of 0.21; the entry proves that implication in Lean, with the corollary itself stated as a hypothesis. The even case, every even N >= 4, is proved with no hypothesis. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. The Lean code was written by an AI agent and is offered for human audit.

records.title: Extremal Sidon sets: Fourier uniformity and partition regularity
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of Ortega and Prendiville's results on Sidon sets in integer intervals. It proves Fourier bounds for near-maximal and largest Sidon sets, equidistribution in progressions and Bohr sets, and monochromatic solutions to partition regular linear equations in at least five variables. It also proves sharp obstruction constructions and records a correction to the paper's dimension-independent approximation claim.

records.title: Auslander–Yorke dichotomy for minimal metric maps
records.abstract: For a continuous map of a metric space with every forward natural orbit dense, either the map is sensitive in the open-set pair sense or its natural iterate family is equicontinuous at every point. Stable open sets are propagated using dense orbits and finite early-time continuity. On nonempty spaces nonsensitivity is equivalent to equicontinuity; no compactness or uniform-equicontinuity assertion is required.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: A finite two-temperature lower bound for the GHR sum-difference constant
records.abstract: The Gyarmati-Hennecart-Ruzsa constant C₃ₐ is the supremum of real exponents theta for which every K > 1 admits a positive constant c and arbitrarily large nonempty finite integer sets X with nonempty partners Y satisfying |X+Y| <= K|X| and c|X+Y|^theta <= |X-Y|. This formalization proves the strict bound C₃ₐ > 60709/50000 = 1.21418. A finite type at depth 10^13, separate difference and sum tilts, cyclic compression, and a proved finite-set principle supply the bound. The result concerns extremal sumset and difference-set growth in additive combinatorics. The paper's general limiting theorem is outside the formalized claim.

records.title: Determination Patterns in Infinite Dependency Models
records.abstract: A Lean development of determination in infinite Boolean dependency models, including pattern realization, attainable determinate regions, contextual uniqueness, source-labelled spines, and a copy-majority representation. The Comparator configurations select separately scoped parts of this development; no single component is asserted to cover the whole paper.

records.title: Uniform interior C^{1,α} estimates for infinity-harmonic functions in dimensions d ≥ 3
records.abstract: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the main results of the preprint "Uniform Interior C^{1,α} Estimates for Infinity-Harmonic Functions" (OpenAI, 2026). For every dimension d ≥ 3 there are α ∈ (0, 1/3] and C < ∞ such that every bounded viscosity solution u of the infinity-Laplace equation Δ_∞u = Σ u_i u_j u_ij = 0 on the unit ball of ℝ^d is differentiable on the half ball, with sup |∇u| + [∇u]_{C^{0,α}} ≤ C · osc u (Theorem 1.1). Consequently every infinity-harmonic function on a connected open subset of ℝ^d, d ≥ 3, is C¹ (Corollary 1.2). The proof rests on a Liouville theorem for the degenerate limiting equation D²v[(∇ₓv, 1)] = 0 on space-time, for entire solutions admitting uniform affine fits at all scales (Theorem 3.1), which is also formalized. All three results are proved from Mathlib with no sorry and no axioms beyond propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, including the Crandall–Ishii–Lions theorem of sums and Alexandrov's theorem used along the way.

records.title: Low-discrepancy quasi-uniform digital sequences in every dimension (Halton-type failure and residue sequences)
records.abstract:
Two results of the manuscript "Low-discrepancy quasi-uniform digital sequences in every dimension" (version 1): Corollary cor:halton of Theorem thm:nonqu, and Theorem thm:residue with Corollaries cor:korobov and cor:residueQU for one explicit sequence. Quasi-uniform means here: there is a real B such that h(P_[N]) <= B delta(P_[N]) for every N >= 2, where P_[N] is the set of the first N points, h is the Euclidean covering radius of [0,1]^s (a supremum over the cube of the minimum distance to the points) and delta is the minimum Euclidean distance over pairs of distinct indices. (1) For every prime p, every s >= 2 and all pairwise coprime polynomials b_0, ..., b_(s-1) over Z/pZ of degree >= 1, the Halton-type sequence in these bases (Goda-Hofer-Suzuki, Def. 2: coordinate c of the point with index n = sum_k n_k p^k reads the b_c-adic digits (V div b_c^Q) mod b_c of V = sum_k n_k z^k, each written as its deg(b_c) coefficients, the coefficient of z^(deg(b_c)-1) first) is not quasi-uniform, and for every eps > 0 there are m and two distinct indices v, w < p^m whose points have Euclidean distance less than eps (p^m)^(-1/s). For every prime p and every s such bases exist. (2) Let s >= 2, let p > 2^s be prime and rho = floor(p^(1/s)). Consider the residue sequence with the Faure places a_c = c, scale theta = 1 and the Korobov check vector v = (rho, rho^2, ..., rho^(s-1), -1): the digital sequence over Z/pZ with generator matrices C_c[n][i] = v_c^(-1) [t^n] (c + t)^i w_c(c + t)^(-(n+1)), w_c(z) = prod_(c' != c) (z - c'), and coordinates y_c = sum_n y_(c,n) p^(-n-1) with digits in {0, ..., p-1}. It is a (0,s)-sequence in base p; for every K >= 1, any two distinct indices u, u' < N = p^(sK-1) give points at toroidal Euclidean distance (sum_c (d_c - round(d_c))^2)^(1/2), d = difference of the points, at least (rho - 1) p^(-1/s) N^(-1/s); and it is quasi-uniform. Moreover rho >= 2 and rho^s < p, every v_c is nonzero, the places are distinct, and the power series w_c(c + t) over Z/pZ times its inverse is 1. (The entry states no discrepancy bound; that (0,s)-sequences have low discrepancy is classical and is not part of this entry.)
Comparator configuration: comparatorHeadlineSeqV4.json (4 compared theorems, all proved, no sorry): GeoSeqV4.halton_not_quasiUniform, GeoSeqV4.halton_bases_exist, GeoSeqV4.residue_quasiUniform, GeoSeqV4.residue_data. The Challenge (HeadlineSeqV4/Challenge.lean, 195 lines) imports only Mathlib and defines everything it uses from scratch (digital sequences from infinite generator matrices over ZMod p, the (0,s)-sequence property, Euclidean and toroidal distances, covering radius, minimum distance, quasi-uniformity, the Halton-type points, the residue generator matrices). The Solution (HeadlineSeqV4/Solution.lean) imports a verbatim copy of these definitions (HeadlineSeqV4/Defs.lean, generated by scripts/gen_headline_seq_v4_defs.py) and the full formalization GeoSeq of the same Lake project, proves bridge lemmas (each definition equals the corresponding GeoSeq definition) and obtains the theorems from compared theorems of GeoSeq (configurations comparatorGeoSeqV9.json, comparatorGeoSeqV93.json).

records.title: Generic IP-transitive points in weakly mixing systems
records.abstract: For a continuous map of a second-countable Baire Hausdorff space with topologically transitive square, a residual set of points has IP entering times into every nonempty open set. A nonempty space has a nonempty dense G-delta family of such points; square hitting times are infinite.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Determination Patterns in Infinite Dependency Models
records.abstract: A Lean development of determination in infinite Boolean dependency models, including pattern realization, attainable determinate regions, contextual uniqueness, source-labelled spines, and a copy-majority representation. The Comparator configurations select separately scoped parts of this development; no single component is asserted to cover the whole paper.

records.title: The additive theorem for 2-transitive Galois groups (Girstmair; Dixon, Theorem 1') and its representation-theoretic engine
records.abstract: Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, of the homogeneous case and, at the roots, of the printed form (relations with value in K), with coefficients in any field K of characteristic 0, of the additive theorem for 2-transitive Galois groups (Girstmair, Manuscripta Math. 39 (1982) 81-97, Proposition 4, Assertion 3, p. 86, for every field whose characteristic does not divide |G|; stated by J. D. Dixon, Acta Arith. 82 (1997) 293-302, as Theorem 1', p. 301, with its proof omitted), of its representation-theoretic engine (classical: Huppert, Endliche Gruppen I, p. 597, Satz 20.2, as cited by Girstmair, Acta Arith. 89 (1999) 53-96, p. 78; used by Dixon on p. 297, in the proof of Theorem 1(ii), citing Curtis-Reiner Section 32B), and of two criterion forms over any field whose hypothesis is the irreducibility of the augmentation module instead of 2-transitivity (the 'if' direction of Girstmair 1982, Proposition 4, Assertion 2, in its module form). Eight compared theorems, in namespace DixonRelations, in this order. (1) zeroSum_irreducible, the engine: for a finite group G acting 2-transitively on a finite set Omega with 2 <= |Omega| and a field K of characteristic 0, the augmentation (zero-sum) subspace V0 = {f : Omega -> K | sum_x f x = 0} of the permutation module Omega -> K is an irreducible K[G]-module; proved in the substantive form of simplicity, that a G-invariant subspace W <= V0 with W != bot equals V0. The G-action is the permutation representation (g . f) x = f (g^{-1} . x), and a subrepresentation is a Submodule together with an explicit invariance hypothesis. (2') additive_core_of_irreducible, the zero-sum criterion form: for any field K, any group G (finite or not) acting on a finite Omega, an injective family alpha : Omega -> L into a K-vector space L, K-linear maps phi g with phi g (alpha x) = alpha (g . x) (no homomorphism property assumed), and the hypothesis hirr (every nonzero G-invariant K-subspace of V0 is V0, word for word the conclusion of (1); it holds vacuously when V0 = 0, that is |Omega| <= 1), any c with sum_x c x = 0 and sum_x c x . alpha x = 0 is 0. (2) additive_core, the zero-sum form for an abstract family: the same conclusion for K of characteristic 0 and a finite group G acting 2-transitively on Omega with 2 <= |Omega|; it is (1) followed by (2'). (3) additive_roots_no_relation, the zero-sum form at the roots: for K of characteristic 0 and an irreducible f in K[X] of degree >= 2 whose Galois group acts 2-transitively on the roots of f in the splitting field, any K-valued coefficient tuple c on the roots with sum_r c r = 0 and sum_r c r . r = 0 is 0; G = f.Gal, Omega = f.rootSet f.SplittingField (with Mathlib's instance Polynomial.Gal.galActionAux), the family is the inclusion of the root set, phi g is the field automorphism g read as a K-linear map (the compatibility holds by rfl), and 2 <= |Omega| follows from card_rootSet_eq_natDegree with separability from Irreducible.separable; f.SplittingField appears in the 2-transitivity hypothesis and in the types of c and of the relation hypothesis. (3) is the zero-sum part (value 0, coefficient sum 0) of the homogeneous case of Dixon's Theorem 1' at the roots; the full homogeneous case at the roots is (5), and the inhomogeneous case is (6). (4') relModule_le_span_one_of_irreducible, the span-one criterion form: under the hypotheses of (2') and a transitive action, every coefficient tuple c with sum_x c x . alpha x = 0 is a scalar multiple of the all-ones tuple, i.e. relModule K alpha is contained in the line K . (fun _ => 1). This is the 'if' direction of Girstmair 1982, Proposition 4, Assertion 2 (p. 86: "If G is primitive on G/H, (G,H) admits only trivial relations over K iff the complementary module U(G/H) of K epsilon_0 is simple"), whose hypothesis is, like hirr, the simplicity of a module; Girstmair 1999 restates it in character form as Proposition 12 (p. 78), "essentially contained in Proposition 4 of [11]". (4') assumes transitivity in place of primitivity; for a transitive action, hirr already forces primitivity (elementary, not formalized: the zero-sum functions constant on the blocks of a nontrivial block system form a nonzero proper invariant subspace of V0), so the difference is one of form only. (4) relModule_le_span_one, the span-one form: the same conclusion under the hypotheses of (2); it is (1) followed by (4'). (5) relModule_roots_le_span_one, the span-one form at the roots: under the hypotheses of (3), relModule K of the root family (fun r => (r : f.SplittingField)) is contained in K . (fun _ => 1); it is (4) at the roots. (6) roots_inhomogeneous_iff_const, Dixon's printed form at the roots: under the hypotheses of (3), sum_r c r . r = algebraMap K f.SplittingField k for some k in K if and only if c is constant; in Dixon's notation this is U = K.e. Dixon's Theorem 1' is stated for any subfield K of C and for relations with value in K; compared statements (2), (3), (4) and (5) concern its homogeneous case (value 0) and (6) its printed form (value in K), for every field K of characteristic 0, and (2') and (4') take any field.
