Girstmair 1982 states the additive theorem for every field whose characteristic does not divide |G|, so characteristic 0 is a sub-case of his hypothesis; (2') and (4') take any field, but their content is carried by hirr, which this entry proves only in characteristic 0 and only for 2-transitive actions, as (1). An uncompared bridge, BDS.isAtom_zeroSumSubrep_iff, shows that hirr together with V0 != bot is atomicity of V0 in Mathlib's lattice of subrepresentations of the permutation representation on Omega -> K. (1) is proved by an elementary, character-free stabilizer-averaging argument; Dixon (p. 297) cites Curtis-Reiner Section 32B for the statement only; Curtis-Reiner was not consulted, and nothing is claimed about its proof. (2') applies hirr to relModule K alpha meet V0 and uses injectivity of alpha; (4') shows that a relation and each of its translates differ by a zero-sum relation, so the relation is G-invariant, hence constant by transitivity (no averaging); the forward direction of (6) argues in the same way at the roots for a relation with value in K, using (2), and its reverse direction uses that the sum of the roots of a separable polynomial is fixed by every automorphism of the splitting field, which is Galois over K, and so lies in K. This formalizes classical results; it is not new mathematics. Research context: additive and multiplicative relations among conjugate algebraic numbers are studied in Girstmair (1982, 1999), Smyth (1986), Drmota-Skalba (1991), Baron-Drmota-Skalba (1995), Dixon (1997) and Zheng (2021); in the sources read for this entry the doubly transitive additive case is derived from the criterion and character theory in one sentence (Girstmair 1982, p. 86), set aside because the doubly transitive pairs are classified (Girstmair 1999, p. 78), and stated with its proof omitted (Dixon 1997, p. 301); this entry gives a complete, character-free, machine-checked proof. The namespace BDS of the two entry definitions is the development's historical name (after Baron-Drmota-Skalba); no result of Baron-Drmota-Skalba is formalized. Formalization status (search of 2026-10-28 for the six statements (1), (2'), (2), (3), (4') and (4) as stated here, at the repository heads listed in README.md; a search result, not a guarantee): none of the six statements searched was found in any prover; (5) and (6), searched for on 2026-10-29 at the repository heads listed in README.md, were not found either. The fact behind the reverse direction of (6), that the sum of the roots lies in the base field, is in Mathlib at the pin in Vieta form (Polynomial.Splits.nextCoeff_eq_neg_sum_roots_mul_leadingCoeff), for the multiset of roots. The S_n case of (1) is formalized in augmentation form over every field in which |Omega| != 0 (every field when |Omega| = 2), in particular over Q, in TauCeti (TauCeti.isIrreducible_standardRepresentation, since 2026-08-05) and as Specht-module irreducibility over C in openai/math; the general 2-transitive case of (1) is formalized in character form over C in AxiomMath/CFSG (CFSG.permutation_character_orbit_count, public since 2026-10-27), the closest item found: CFSG also defines the same V0 over C under the same action (CFSG.Wreathed.CentralSL2.sumZeroSubrep) and computes its character, from which the C case of (1) in submodule form would follow in a few lines, but no theorem stating it was found. NOT formalized and NOT claimed: the MULTIPLICATIVE theorem (Dixon Theorem 1(ii), and, per Zheng 2021, arXiv:1912.07202v1, p. 2, Baron-Drmota-Skalba 1995, Theorem 3), under which 2-transitivity does NOT force triviality: for a prime p and b in Q not a p-th power, X^p - b has Galois group AGL(1,p) over Q, acting sharply 2-transitively on the roots, and the ratios of its roots are p-th roots of unity, nontrivial multiplicative relations; Dixon's Theorem 1(ii) gives necessary conditions for that exception; none of that multiplicative content is proved or claimed here. The additive theorem carries no such exception, because the additive module cannot contain any e_gamma - e_delta (Dixon, p. 301). Also not formalized: the 2-transitivity of any particular Galois group (a hypothesis in (1), (2), (3), (4), (5) and (6)); any case of hirr other than the 2-transitive one, (1); the imprimitive case (Girstmair 1982, Proposition 4, Assertion 1; Girstmair 1999, Proposition 12, first sentence) and the fact that hirr forces primitivity for a transitive action; the 'only if' direction of the criterion, the character form of its hypothesis, and the converse of Assertion 3 that Girstmair 1982 states for a splitting field; and the identification of Omega -> K with the scalar extension of Omega -> Q.

records.title: Sharp reset thresholds for bounded-response synchronization games with a sink
records.abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib statements of the theorem M(n,k) = sum_{i=1}^{n-1} ceil(i/k) for k = 1 or n <= k+3 (Lipin-Volkov k-game on automata with a sink), rendered as an upper and a lower bound, with the headline case M(5,2) = 6, proved in Solution.lean from the development SinkReset.Plan written in the conductor formalize run 2026-10-25_formalize-sinkresetthresholds. The endpoints k = 1 (Rystsov's tight bound n(n-1)/2) and k = n-1 were known from Lipin-Volkov; the new content is M(k+2,k) = k+2 and M(k+3,k) = k+4 for k >= 2, including the non-divisible pairs (4,2) and (5,3), which the Lipin-Volkov conjecture (stated for k | n-1 only) does not cover; (5,2) is the first pair with k | n-1 that is neither endpoint, i.e. the first pair on which the Lipin-Volkov conjecture itself was open ((4,2) is the first non-endpoint pair of all).

records.title: PCF all the way down
records.abstract:
Let k be a field of characteristic zero and let f: X → X be a finite surjective map of integral k-schemes of finite type. By the critical locus of f we mean the image in X of the critical locus of the map induced on the normalization of X. By the branch locus we mean the image of the critical locus under f.

We say that f is post-critically finite (PCF) if, for every irreducible divisor D contained in the branch locus, the forward orbit f(D) ∪ f^2(D) ∪ … is algebraic, that is, a finite union of subvarieties, taken as a closed subscheme with its reduced induced structure.

We prove that if f is PCF and A is a preperiodic divisor for f with f^{r+s}(A) = f^r(A), then, setting B = f^r(A) and g = f^s, the restriction of g to B is PCF.

This proves the PCF all the way down conjecture: restricting again to preperiodic divisors and iterating gives PCF maps at every stage.

records.title: The two-qubit Hardy ladder: the closed form P_K*(q) and its unique maximiser for every K, Hardy's optimum at K = 1, and the optimum (8 rho^2 + rho - 11)/25 in the cubic field Q(rho) at K = 2
records.abstract: Kernel-checked optimum of Hardy's K-step ladder for two qubits (Hardy 1993; Hardy 1997; Boschi, Branca, De Martini and Hardy 1997), for a real Schmidt state c0|00> + c1|11> and real projective settings, the probabilities written out as squared real amplitudes. For every K: under the ladder constraints P(A_K = 1, B_K = 1) <= q^2 (1 - q^{2K})^2 / ((1 + q^2)(1 + q^{2K+1})^2), q = c1/c0, with equality attained (Cereceda 2002, eqs. (18)-(19)); the probability is below 1/2 (the two-qubit, real-settings case of a bound that follows in every dimension from Cereceda 2016, eq. (9), with Wehner 2006), and for every eps > 0 and every large enough K some state and settings exceed 1/2 - eps (the "(50 - delta)%" of Hardy 1997 and Boschi et al. 1997). For every K >= 1 the maximiser of the closed form on (0, 1) is the unique zero there of Cereceda's polynomial m_K (Cereceda 2002, eq. (20), stated there without proof): the derivative of the closed form, the existence and uniqueness of the zero, the maximum and its uniqueness, and, over all Schmidt states and real settings, the optimum, its attainment at the Schmidt ratio r, and that every optimal configuration has Schmidt ratio r or 1/r (attainment at 1/r follows from the uncompared symmetry). Worked instances: the K = 1 optimum is phi^{-5} = (5 sqrt 5 - 11)/2 (Hardy 1993), attained at a state with 2 c0 c1 = 3 - sqrt 5 and only where 2 c0 c1 = 3 - sqrt 5 (Hardy's condition); the K = 2 optimum is (8 rho^2 + rho - 11)/25 = 0.17455..., rho the plastic number (the real root of x^3 - x - 1), attained at Schmidt weights c0^2 = rho^{-1}, c1^2 = rho^{-5} (c1/c0 = rho^{-2}) and only where {c0^2, c1^2} = {rho^{-1}, rho^{-5}}. The value 0.17455 is in print numerically; the closed form, the maximiser rho^{-2}, the weights and the minimal polynomial 25x^3 + 17x^2 + 2x - 1 of the value were not found in the literature searched (2026-10-28) and are the entry's new content. Also: the K = 2 value is not totally real (its minimal polynomial has a non-real complex root). Optimality over complex settings is not formalised. Thirty compared statements.

records.title: Proof of WOWII Conjecture 96 (DeLaVina, Graffiti.pc)
records.abstract: A Lean 4 proof of Conjecture 96 of Written on the Wall II (Graffiti.pc): every connected graph G on at least two vertices satisfies α(G) ≤ 1 + min_v disteven(v)·(max_v l(v) − 1), where disteven(v) is the number of vertices at even distance from v and l(v) is the independence number of the neighbourhood of v. The proof gives the stronger bound α(G) ≤ 1 + disteven(v)·(L − 1) for every vertex v, which is sharp for stars.

records.title: Parking functions: total variation threshold and critical profile
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of the total variation threshold for initial coordinates of a uniform parking function. The three recorded results give uniform finite-size bounds, the Gaussian critical profile at scale n/log n (including zero and infinite parameters), and a quantitative relative-entropy and total-variation comparison with independent marginals. The library reconstructs the supplied manuscript through Borel marginal asymptotics, homogeneous log-concavity and entropy methods. It also proves the separate Pitman–Stanley volume-polynomial remark. The results concern probabilists and combinatorialists studying random discrete structures, approximation by independent variables and negative dependence.

records.title: Fractional triangle decompositions of dense tripartite graphs
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the main results of Allsop, Bowtell, Lesgourgues and Petrova, "Improved bounds on completion of partial Latin squares" (arXiv:2609.37877, 2026): there is η > 0 (here η = 1/20000) such that every K₃-divisible spanning subgraph of K_{n,n,n} with minimum partite degree at least (0.769 − η)n has a fractional triangle decomposition (Theorem 1.3). Also formalized: the Farkas characterization (Lemma 2.1); the reduction to triangle-covered, balanced, untied and nonzero edge weightings (Proposition 3.1, Corollary 3.5), with Lemma 3.4 proved through an integral maximum flow; the non-uniform proportional discharging (Definition 4.1) and its two estimates (Propositions 4.2 and 4.3); and the numerical inequality g_d ≥ 1 for the article's piecewise-linear f (Proposition 4.4). The two-variable inequalities of Proposition 4.4, which the article settles by numerical minimisation, are proved exactly by Bernstein certificates checked in Lean. Not formalized: the article's Corollary 1.4 (completion of partial Latin squares), which also needs the fractional-to-exact transfer of Barber, Kühn, Lo, Osthus and Taylor for tripartite graphs.

records.title: A dimension-free weak-type (1,1) bound for the Gaussian Riesz transforms
records.abstract: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the main results of Gutiérrez and Manfredi, "A direct obstacle proof of a dimension-free weak-type (1,1) bound for the Gaussian Riesz transforms" (arXiv:2610.26478). For the Gaussian measure dγₙ = π^{-n/2} e^{-|x|²} dx on ℝⁿ, the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck operator L = -½Δ + x·∇ and the normalized gradient D = 2^{-1/2}∇, the vector Riesz transform R_γ = D L^{-1/2} Π₀ has exactly one linear extension to L¹(γₙ) satisfying t·γₙ{|R_γ f| > t} ≤ 2‖f‖₁ for all t > 0, in every dimension n (Theorem 5.1). The proof goes through a Gaussian obstacle decomposition F = g + L^{1/2}u, with existence, uniqueness and the variational characterization of u, and the identification Dom(L^{1/2}) ⊆ W^{1,2}(γₙ) (Theorem 3.1). Also formalized: the principal-value realization of the extension by the Gaussian Riesz kernels (Proposition 5.3), the coordinatewise, historically normalized and unnormalized-measure bounds (Corollary 5.4), and the complex-valued bound with constant 8/π (Corollary 5.5). The Hermite basis of L²(γₙ) and the spectral calculus of L are built from Mathlib; there is no sorry and no axiom beyond propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.title: Short sums of certain arithmetic functions (Nair–Tenenbaum)
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of Nair and Tenenbaum's uniform upper bounds for short sums of nonnegative arithmetic functions evaluated at integer polynomial values. Theorem 1 retains the coefficient-independent height threshold and the restricted-discriminant dependence of the bound. Theorem 2 gives a greatest-prime-factor bound with a strict exponential gain for arbitrary nonconstant irreducible integer polynomials, including those with fixed prime divisors. Theorem 3 treats prime arguments with the explicit constant-term correction. The development also proves the ten corollaries on progressions, Hooley moments, smooth values, shifted primes, dyadic averages, and Goldbach representations, and Lemma 2 for general class-M weights. Corollary 6 has an explicit nonconstancy condition; the printed Lemma 1 has a checked counterexample and the required replacements are proved.

records.title: SmallRatio: Dedekind sums along Euclid's algorithm and the small-ratio formula
records.abstract: For a prime p and 0 < h < p, the Dedekind sum s(h,p) is determined, up to an explicit error of order log p, by the fractions of small height congruent to plus or minus h: with the sum over the coprime pairs u, v >= 1 with uv < p/2, |12 s(h,p) - p sum ([hv = u mod p] - [hv = -u mod p])/(uv)| <= 6n <= 12 log_2 p + 6, where n is the length of Euclid's algorithm on (p, h). Summed over any set H of residues, in particular over a subgroup of odd order, this gives |12 sum_{h in H} s(h,p) - p S_H(p)| <= |H| (12 log_2 p + 6), where S_H(p) is the signed sum of 1/(uv) over the coprime pairs with uv < p/2 and u/v in H or -H. The development proves Dedekind reciprocity from scratch (by counting lattice points), the identities of Euclid's algorithm and the bound n <= 2 log_2 k + 1, the alternating-sum form 12 s(h,k) = sum (-1)^{j+1} k/(r_j q_{j-1}) + E with |E| <= 4n, and Legendre's pairing of the small coprime pairs with the steps of the algorithm, by a lattice-basis argument instead of continued fractions.

records.title: Uniform attachment with freezing: Scaling limits — Lean formalization
records.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of arXiv:2308.00484, "Uniform attachment with freezing: Scaling limits", published in Ann. Inst. H. Poincaré Probab. Statist. 61(4) 2679–2708 (2025). It proves the Introduction's height theorem, the subcritical Gromov–Hausdorff–Prokhorov (GHP) limit to a measured segment, the critical GHP limit to a random compact measured real tree T(f) together with its geometric properties (leaves carry the mass; binary if and only if the reciprocal-square integral diverges; root condensation otherwise), and the supercritical distance-matrix limit in its corrected zero-diagonal form. All numbered intermediate results are proved, several in corrected or qualified forms. The CRT corollary (cor:CRT) is not formalized. Height and forward-tree modules are adapted from the companion formalization of "Uniform attachment with freezing" by the same contributor (not yet public; see docs/companion-provenance.md).

records.title: Machine-Checked Christofides 3/2-Approximation and Polyhedral Complexity Barriers for the Traveling Salesperson Problem in Lean 4
records.abstract: This formalization develops a machine-checked theory of the Traveling Salesperson Problem (TSP) on finite undirected graphs over Fin n in Lean 4 across two principal modules. First, in Christofides.lean (compared against ChallengeChristofides.lean), we formalize the complete Christofides-Serdyukov 3/2-approximation algorithm for Metric TSP: the Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) lower bound (cost(T) <= OPT), Euler's handshaking parity invariant for odd-degree vertices, the minimum-weight perfect matching upper bound on odd-degree vertices (2 * cost(M) <= OPT) via alternating matching decomposition of shortcut cycles, multigraph degree parity of T U M, constructive existence of Eulerian circuits via Hierholzer cycle splicing and complete Christofides certificates, metric walk shortcutting contraction, and the unconditional 3/2-approximation guarantee in both exact integer scaling and real arithmetic. Second, in TSPComplexity.lean (compared against ChallengeTSPComplexity.lean), we formalize polyhedral and complexity-theoretic barriers for Decision TSP: a fuel-bounded branch-and-cut state machine with verified soundness, completeness, and support-pruned cycle-separation rank decision equivalence; the Dantzig-Fulkerson-Johnson (DFJ) subtour cut inequality (every valid tour crosses any proper nonempty cut at least twice); the continuous Held-Karp LP relaxation embedding; a machine-checked proof that the 10-vertex Petersen graph fractional assignment (x_e = 2/3) strictly separates the Held-Karp relaxation from the integral TSP polytope with zero slack on singleton cuts and slack >= 2/3 on all nontrivial cuts; Yannakakis DFJ slack matrix nonnegativity and conditional Fiorini-Rothvoss PSD extension complexity scaling; and polynomial-time reductions from Hamiltonian Cycle and gadget-parameterized 3-SAT to Decision TSP.

records.title: Maximality of the Došen–Petrić Boolean Category
records.abstract: Let P be a nonempty set of propositional variables. The freely generated zero-identity Boolean category B(P) of Došen and Petrić is maximal: every congruence on its morphisms preserved by the operations on morphisms and uniform formula substitution is either equality or identifies every pair of parallel morphisms. The formalization gives two proofs of maximality and proves the congruence dichotomy. It also proves that the identity and zero endomorphism of each variable are distinct, and that there is no morphism from the terminal object to the initial object.

records.title: There is no universal Fσ equivalence relation
records.abstract: There is no universal Fσ equivalence relation. This is the main result of arxiv:2610.31052. More detail: An equivalence relation E on a Polish space X is said to be Fσ if it is a countable union of closed subsets of X × X. For equivalence relations E and F on Polish spaces X and Y, we say that E is Borel reducible to F, written E ≤_B F, if there exists a Borel function f : X → Y such that for all x, y ∈ X, we have x E y if and only if f(x) F f(y). An Fσ equivalence relation E is universal if for every Fσ equivalence relation F, we have F ≤_B E. The theorem states that there's no such relation.

records.title: fc-poisson-2
records.abstract: A machine-checked proof that the Poisson conjecture fails for two canonical pairs, and hence for every n >= 2, following the explicit counterexample of C. D. Long (2026). The statements and definitions are Formal Conjectures' (PoissonConjecture.lean, arXiv math/0608009), copied verbatim into Challenge.lean, so this entry proves Formal Conjectures' own statements.

records.title: Reductions for Erdős Problem 919
records.abstract: Erdős Problem 919 asks for a graph on the ordinal omega_2 squared with chromatic number aleph_2, or aleph_1, such that every subgraph on a vertex set of smaller order type has chromatic number at most aleph_0. This formalization proves in ZFC that the aleph_2 question is equivalent to the first question of Erdős Problem 918, that the aleph_1 question is equivalent to the existence of a graph on aleph_2 vertices that is not countably chromatic although all its subgraphs on aleph_1 vertices are, that the aleph_2 question implies the aleph_1 question, and that the aleph_1 question has a positive answer under the continuum hypothesis. The proof blows a graph on omega_2 up to a graph on omega_2 times omega_2 in the lexicographic order. It does not settle either question in ZFC.

records.title: The orthogonal art gallery problem is ∃ℝ-complete (point-point and point-boundary), in Lean 4
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of material in a forthcoming manuscript entitled "The Orthogonal Art Gallery Problem is ∃ℝ-complete". A Lean 4 and Mathlib proof, for an explicit single-tape Turing machine model, that deciding whether an orthogonal simple polygon (every edge horizontal or vertical) with rational corners can be guarded by g guards is ∃ℝ-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions, both when the guards must see the whole polygon (point-point) and when they must see only its boundary (point-boundary). Both problems also reduce to ETR by formulas whose only variables are the 2g coordinates of the guards. As far as we could determine, hardness for orthogonal polygons was open: it is treated neither by Abrahamsen, Adamaszek and Miltzow (J. ACM 2021) nor by Stade (SoCG 2025). The hardness proof is a new construction derived from Stade's polygon: needles become corridors, wedges become rectangles with needle cutters, the slanted mouths of the copy nooks are kept through helper guards pinned by four-armed crosses, and the addition gadgets are replaced by new orthogonal rooms. Its visibility, pinning and coverage facts are checked by the kernel as certificates (cone propagation with a symbolic height parameter, polynomial sign tests for the copy nooks, coverage by convex items). The proofs use only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.title: Triangle decompositions of dense tripartite graphs and completion of partial Latin squares
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Corollary 1.6 for r = 3 of Barber, Kühn, Lo, Osthus and Taylor, "Clique decompositions of multipartite graphs and completion of Latin squares" (J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 151 (2017), arXiv:1603.01043): fractional triangle decompositions above a threshold give triangle decompositions above the same threshold. Precisely: if δ ≥ 3/4 and, for every ε > 0, every K₃-divisible tripartite graph with three parts of size n ≥ n₀(ε) and minimum partite degree at least (δ + ε)n has a fractional triangle decomposition, then for every ε > 0 there is n₀ such that every K₃-divisible tripartite graph with parts of size n ≥ n₀ and minimum partite degree at least (δ + ε)n has a triangle decomposition (BKLOT2017.corollary_1_6). The hypothesis δ ≥ 3/4 is an extra assumption of the Lean statement: the article does not need it because the fractional threshold is known to be at least 3/4, which is not formalized here. Combined with the fractional bound of Allsop, Bowtell, Lesgourgues and Petrova (pinned entry PALOMAR-2026-10-30-000008), this gives the unconditional statement with threshold 0.769 − 1/20000 (BKLOT2017.corollary_1_6_ablp). The proof follows the iterative absorption of the article (absorbers, vortex of partitions with random reserves, cover-down, balancing graph, assembly) but replaces the regularity-based Section 8 by a route through the fractional threshold and the Haxell–Rödl transfer. Version 2 adds Theorem 1.4 and Corollary 3.2 for r = 3, the completion of partial Latin squares: for every ε > 0 and all large n, every partial Latin square of order n in which every row, every column and every symbol is used at most (1 − δ − ε)n times extends to a Latin square, above the fractional threshold δ ≥ 3/4 (BKLOT2017.theorem_1_4, from Cor16 δ by BKLOT2017.corollary_3_2) and unconditionally with 1 − δ = 0.231 + 1/20000 (BKLOT2017.theorem_1_4_ablp).

records.title: Optimal clique partitions under local perturbations
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the main results of the author's preprint "Optimal Clique Partitions under Local Perturbations" (Erdős #81 series, Paper VI). For a graph G on n vertices with a core P of size p = ⌊(n+1)/3⌋, h = Δ(G △ (K_P ∨ I_O)) and u, s, m the numbers of core, crossing and exterior edges: if p ≥ 18h + 1 then cp(G) = cp_{≤4}(G) = s − u − 2m = M(n) + C − A − 2m with M(n) = ⌊n(n+1)/6⌋ (Theorem A), and cp_{≤3}(G) − cp(G) = m (Theorem B); if p ≥ 63h, every assignment of the orders 4 or 5 to the exterior edges is realized by an optimal partition (Theorem C); for p ≥ 16 each assignment has at least p^{⌊p²/64⌋} optimal partitions and 2^m p^{⌊p²/64⌋} ≤ N(G) ≤ (n+1)^{5e(G)} (Theorem E). Also: the formula for other core sizes in an explicit window (Proposition 2.1), the intrinsic maximum over all cores (§8.1), the exact optimum with one exceptional vertex, cp = cp_{≤4} = cp*_= = s − u − 2m + D(a,b), ν₃ = ν₃* = u + min(a,b) and the restriction gap (Theorem D), and the complete-join variant cp(G) = M(n) − 2m (Theorem A.1). Twelve statements in all. The constants 18, 63, 16 and 24 are those of the paper; their optimality is not claimed.

records.title: Uniform attachment with freezing: SIR epidemic and infection-tree limits
records.abstract: Lean proofs of the local, fluid and terminal geometric limits of the SIR epidemic and its infection tree. The selected results include the finite-rate geometric Bienaymé limit, strong-rate non-tightness, the finite-rate fluid and height/distance survival mixtures, and the strong-rate fluid, height, distance and maximum-height limits. The physical model uses independent exponential recoveries and infection-age contact paths; existence for positive rates and the relevant clock-law identifications are proved. This entry covers T06–T07 and shares its proof repository with the other main-result groups.

records.title: Erdős Problem 835 when k + 1 is composite: the chromatic number of J(2k, k) exceeds k + 1
records.abstract: Erdős Problem 835 asks whether, for some k > 2, the k-element subsets of a 2k-element set can be coloured with k + 1 colours so that every (k + 1)-element set sees all k + 1 colours among its k-element subsets; equivalently, whether the Johnson graph J(2k, k) has chromatic number k + 1 for some k > 2. Jie Ma and Quanyu Tang showed that this fails whenever k + 1 is not prime. This Lean 4 formalization proves, with Mathlib only: the equivalence between the colouring property and χ(J(2k, k)) = k + 1 for k > 0; χ(J(2k, k)) > k + 1 for every k > 2 with k + 1 composite; the consequence for every odd k > 2; and χ(J(18, 9)) > 10. The proof is a double count of the k-subsets of one colour inside a (k + j)-set, which forces k + 1 to divide (k + j).choose j for 1 ≤ j ≤ k; a prime p < k + 1 dividing k + 1 violates this at j = p. The case where k + 1 is prime, and so the problem itself, remains open; no new mathematics is claimed.

records.title: A formal proof of an affine reverse Faber-Krahn inequality
records.abstract: The three principal manuscript results M01, M02 and M03, with their original domains and quantifier order. M01: one finite C>0 before every n>0 and compact convex Euclidean body K with nonempty interior; there exists a literal real special-linear matrix S with finite actual H0 Rayleigh infimum on interior(S K) and lambda_1(interior(S K))*volume(K)^(2/n)<=C*n. M02: one finite C>0 before every n>0 and origin-symmetric compact convex volume-one K with nonempty interior in maximal Gaussian measure position; its actual H0 Rayleigh infimum is at most C*n. M03: for each real P>=2 one finite C(P)>0 precedes every n>0, every even isotropic probability law nu satisfying the conventional compact-set IsLogConcaveMeasure condition, least Poincare constant at most P and finite actual Gaussian-relative Fisher information, and every origin-symmetric compact convex body D with nonempty interior supporting nu almost everywhere; lambda_1(interior D)<=C(P)*(n+sqrt(n*I(nu|gamma))). The log-concave density is derived from the law's original finite-information hypothesis; no density witness, covariance lower bound, ellipsoid-existence conclusion or desired spectral estimate is an additional premise. This standalone combined M01/M02/M03 package passed its own ordinary Linux sandboxed Comparator --paranoid with all six configured kernels. Its actual build, complete fixed-statement comparison, private proof inspection, axiom reports and separate AI reviews are retained under verification/.

records.title: Rare subtree patterns in size-conditioned Bienaymé trees: Poisson approximation and declumping
records.abstract: Lean proofs of the four Introduction theorems of Rare subtree patterns in size-conditioned Bienaymé trees: Poisson approximation and declumping, including periodic offspring laws. Secondary results, proof departures, manuscript corrections and remaining background obligations are recorded in FORMALIZATION_REPORT.md.

records.title: The Murty–Simon conjecture on diameter-2-critical graphs
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the proof by Sanjana Das and Jacob Fox of the Murty–Simon conjecture (arXiv:2610.39032, 2026). A graph is diameter-2-critical if its diameter is 2 and deleting any edge increases the diameter. Theorem 1.1: every diameter-2-critical graph on n vertices has at most ⌊n²/4⌋ edges (murty_simon), and a diameter-2-critical graph with ⌊n²/4⌋ edges is isomorphic to K_{⌈n/2⌉,⌊n/2⌋} (murty_simon_equality). Also: for n ≥ 3, K_{⌈n/2⌉,⌊n/2⌋} is diameter-2-critical with ⌊n²/4⌋ edges, so the bound is attained (murty_simon_sharp); Lemma 1.2, |E(G) \ M| ≤ |non-edges of G| for every maximal matching M of a diameter-2-critical graph G (lemma_1_2); and Lemma 1.3, a diameter-2-critical graph with equality in Lemma 1.2 for every maximal matching is triangle-free (lemma_1_3). Five statements; the bound holds for every n, with no lower bound on n.

records.title: The height of the infection tree
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of all 31 numbered results of The height of the infection tree under the embedded SIR epidemic model, with six explicit statement corrections or endpoint conventions. The height theorem retains arbitrary asymptotic infection-rate sequences and the full Bernoulli mixture across early extinction and macroscopic survival. The strong profile theorem retains exact lattice heights, the Gaussian logarithmic correction and compact-parameter uniformity. These results concern probabilists studying random trees, branching processes and epidemic geometry. The proposed Palomar entry selects the two main theorems and the following parameter-uniform strengthening; the full library and result-by-result coverage record are included.

records.title: Linearity bounds for APN functions
records.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of linearity bounds for almost perfect nonlinear (APN) maps F: 𝔽₂ⁿ → 𝔽₂ⁿ. Write N = 2ⁿ and let L(F) denote the maximum Walsh magnitude over components indexed by nonzero vectors. For n ≥ 5, the formalization establishes L(F) ≤ N − 6, together with L(F) ≤ N − √N/4 − 2 when n is even. For n ≥ 4, ordering the Walsh magnitudes in nonincreasing order as L_k(F) gives L_k(F) ≤ (N/√k)√(1 + (2^(k−1) − 1)/N) for 1 ≤ k ≤ N(N − 1). In particular, L₂(F) ≤ 2⌊N/3⌋ and L₄(F) ≤ N/2. Further bounds relate linearity to the count q of nonplateaued components with nonzero indices. In odd dimension, q > 0 implies L(F)² ≤ N(1 + √(q(N − 1))). In even dimension, whenever 1/2 ≤ C < 1, the condition q ≤ (4C − C² − 1)N/4 + 1 implies L(F) ≤ CN. Additional results sharpen the upper bound on the linearity in certain odd dimensions and constrain the second-largest Walsh magnitude when the linearity is close to N.

records.title: Dimension-free KLS Poincare bound for isotropic log-concave densities
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib library for Poincare inequalities, log-concave probability measures and stochastic localization. Its dimension-free KLS theorem bounds the intrinsic local-slope Poincare constant by one universal constant times the covariance operator norm, including dimension zero and singular affine supports, for log-concave probability laws with finite second moment. The proof follows Bizeul-Klartag-Lehec through finite-horizon cutoff localization, the compact Letwin constant-8 quadratic variance bound and approximation. Supporting results include Cheeger-Buser comparisons, covariance and energy interfaces and moment-map calculus. This Palomar configuration compares two density statements. Each asserts the existence of a positive constant C that works in every dimension n >= 1 and for every measurable isotropic log-concave probability density. The pinned OpenAI statement gives Var(f) <= C * E|grad f|^2 for smooth compactly supported tests and is the statement registered in PALOMAR-2026-11-01-000014 v1. The density-coordinate formulation of Bizeul-Klartag-Lehec Theorem 1.1 applies to every locally Lipschitz f in L^2 and uses an extended nonnegative squared-gradient integral that may be infinite. The locally Lipschitz definitions and bridge are new project code, not part of the OpenAI model. No numerical final KLS constant or uncut Eldan construction is claimed.

records.title: Odd zeta values and powers of pi
records.abstract: Lean proofs of three-Lambert-series formulas for pi^(4m-1), pi^(4m+1), zeta(4m-1) and zeta(4m+1), for m>=1, together with a separate formula for pi and the signs of the rational denominator coefficients.

records.title: Superfluid stiffness and nonclassical rotational inertia of the dilute hard-sphere Bose gas
records.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of the principal superfluid-stiffness, nonclassical rotational-inertia, winding, and high-temperature normal-phase results of the supplied manuscript, with concrete hard-sphere path measures and Dirichlet-form response definitions.

records.title: Fluctuation bounds for first-passage percolation
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of two papers of S. Armstrong and A. Bou-Rabee on the fluctuations of passage times in first-passage percolation. "Curvature and variance in lattice first-passage percolation": for independent, identically distributed edge weights on Z^d, d >= 2, whose law nu has an exponential moment and nu({0}) below the critical probability of bond percolation (Assumption (W)), and for constants delta in (0, 1], r > 0, Lambda >= 0 and lambda > 0, there are epsilon > 0 and C such that E exp(|T(0, x) - mu(x)| / (C |x|^((1 - epsilon)/2))) <= 2 for every unit vector xi in R^d, rational or not, at which the time constant mu has a quadratic expansion on the orthogonal hyperplane with these constants (Assumption (Curv): a linear term, a quadratic form at least lambda |h|^2, and a remainder at most Lambda |h|^(2 + delta) for |h| <= r), and every x in Z^d other than 0 within distance |x|^(3/4) of the ray through xi; epsilon and C do not depend on the direction (Theorem 1.1). The repository also proves the variance bound that follows, Var T(0, x) <= 2 C^2 |x|^(1 - epsilon), and Var T(0, floor(n xi)) <= n^(1 - epsilon) for every sufficiently large integer n, uniformly in the direction, the floor taken coordinatewise. "Fluctuation bounds for rotationally invariant first-passage percolation": for the random density psi(chi * W) of Gaussian white noise W on R^d, d >= 2, with chi smooth, radial and supported in the closed unit ball and psi continuous with values between two positive constants, the passage time T over rectifiable curves has a time constant mu = lim t^(-1) E T(0, t e_1), and there are epsilon > 0 and C such that E exp(|T(0, x) - mu |x|| / (C |x|^((1 - epsilon)/2))) <= 2 for every point x with |x| >= 1 (Theorem 1.1); the same holds for every density of white noise or of a homogeneous Poisson process that is jointly measurable, determined by the noise in the closed unit ball around each point, bounded between two positive constants and equivariant under rotations and translations (Assumption A, Theorem 1.2). The repository also proves the variance bounds that follow, Var T(0, t e_1) <= t^(1 - epsilon) for every sufficiently large t and Var T(0, x) <= |x|^(1 - epsilon) for every point x with |x| sufficiently large. Every result of the literature that the proofs cite is stated and proved in the repository.

records.title: Rational structures on quivers and a generalization of Gelfand's equivalence: Theorem B
records.abstract: For every field E of characteristic 0 and every integer l >= 0 (lambda = l^2), the category HC_lambda(sl_2, SO(2))_E of E-rational Harish-Chandra modules for (sl_2, SO(2)) with generalized infinitesimal character lambda is equivalent to the category Rep^nil(Gamma_E) of finite-dimensional nilpotent representations of an E-rational quiver Gamma_E: the Gelfand quiver (with the relation a_- b_- = a_+ b_+) if l >= 1 and the cyclic quiver if l = 0, carrying the action of Gal(E(sqrt(-1))/E) that swaps the two outer vertices when sqrt(-1) is not in E.  For E = C this is Gelfand's classical equivalence; E = Q is Theorem A of the paper.  Harish-Chandra modules over E are modelled by Galois descent: an E-vector space M_E together with the weight decomposition and the sl_2-action on L_E (x)_E M_E, L_E = E(sqrt(-1)), and the condition that these structures are defined over E.  The compared statement asserts the existence of an equivalence; the underlying formalization proves that the paper's explicit functor E_E is one.

records.title: The ten minimum universal sets of MacMahon cubes
records.abstract: A universal inventory of six-coloured MacMahon cubes can build a 2 by 2 by 2 model of every target variety, using eight distinct physical copies, without requiring internal face colours to match. We prove that the minimum inventory size is twelve and classify all ten labelled inventories attaining it, even when repetitions are allowed. They are exactly the two-triangle sets in Conway's tableau. The proof derives row and column sums of two from usability inequalities, proves symmetry, and eliminates every other degree-two inventory by corner coverage. Finite kernel-checked witnesses establish sufficiency. The formalization also verifies the proper cube rotations, outward faces, and completeness and uniqueness of the thirty geometric representatives.

records.title: Colorability and realizability defects in resource-dominated packing relaxations
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the main results of the author's preprint "Colorability and Realizability Defects in Resource-Dominated Packing Relaxations" (Erdős #81 series, Paper V). For a conflict system (finite objects with a symmetric irreflexive conflict relation) and a multiset X of objects, the loss between fractional and integral packings is bounded by the colourability defect D_q of the conflict graph H[X] of the copies (Lemma 3.1, Corollary 3.2, Theorems 3.3, 3.4, 3.4w), and, more generally, by the cost of a realizability certificate whose classes are realized in a fixed target system (Theorems 4.2 and 4.4). Applications: host completion through list edge colouring of bipartite multigraphs (Theorem 5.2: Galvin and Borodin–Kostochka–Woodall; Corollary 5.3; Example 5.5, a quadratic separation on K_{r,r}), the vertex-copy inequalities ν₃*(G_{v→u}) + ν₃*(G_{u→v}) ≤ 2ν₃*(G), ν₃(G_{v→u}) + ν₃(G_{u→v}) ≤ 2ν₃(G) + oct(H[T₂]) and ≤ 3ν₃(G) for triangle packings (Theorems 6.1, 6.2, Corollary 6.2a) and mixed triangle/K₄ copy inequalities (Theorem 7.3). Eighteen statements in all.

records.title: Clique partitions of chordal graphs: quantitative stability and sharp eventual bounds
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the chordal results of the author's preprint "Clique partitions with rooted simplicial defect: quantitative stability and sharp eventual bounds" (Erdős #81 series, Paper IV). With M(n) = ⌊n(n+1)/6⌋: there is b such that every chordal graph on n vertices has a clique partition into pieces of order at most four with at most M(n) + b pieces (Theorem A); for n large every chordal graph on n vertices has one with at most M(n) pieces, and some chordal graph on n vertices has one with exactly M(n) pieces that is optimal among all clique partitions (Theorem B, the bound asked in Erdős Problem #81 and its sharpness); 1/6 is the least quadratic coefficient (§6.3); the uniform mixed rounding of fractional triangle/K₄ packings (Theorem 3.1); integral stability with explicit constants and edit distance at most 16δ to a complete-split graph, for 0 ≤ δ ≤ γn² with γ = 10⁻¹⁶/4 (Theorem 6.1); same-root control of near-optimal partitions: one clique root satisfies all the conclusions of Theorem 6.1 and, for it, every partition with at most M(n) + τ pieces has at most τ + 48δ noncanonical pieces (Corollary 6.1a); the root-defect identity (6.7b); and the eventual classification of the extremal chordal graphs as complete-split graphs with a core of optimal size (Corollary 6.2). Version 2 adds the fixed-defect results for graphs of rooted simplicial defect at most s: the sharp eventual bound Q_s(n) = M(n + s) − C(s + 1, 2), attained by a partition optimal among all clique partitions (Theorem C); same-root stability with A_s = 2·10⁴¹·(s + 1)⁸ for 0 ≤ δ ≤ γn², edit distance at most A_s δ, at most τ + (1 + 7A_s)δ noncanonical pieces carrying at most 10τ + 10(1 + 7A_s)δ edges (Theorem C′); comparison with an optimal-size template at distance at most A_s δ + n√((1 + 4A_s)δ) and the equality case cp = c₄ = Q_s(n) (Corollary 6.3); the necessity of the square-root term (Proposition 6.3a); the bounds F₄(G) ≤ M(n − s) + ns (minus C(s + 1, 2) when 4s ≤ n) and their integral form up to εn² (Proposition 6.4); the sublinear-defect bound n²/6 + o(n²) and root stability (Theorem 6.5); the bound Q_s(n) for all s ≤ S once n ≥ T(P(S)), an explicit tower (Corollary 6.6); and the annex inequality: a chordal K_{d+2}-free graph has fractional triangle packing number at most ν₃ + (10 + d/2)n (G.1). 21 statements. The thresholds N and γ in Theorems B, C, C′ and Corollary 6.3 are existential; b, N, A_s and the tower are not claimed optimal.

records.title: Two application notes of the Erdős #81 series: realizability transfer and exact chordal stability
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the two research notes of the author's Erdős #81 series, in one package. Note I, "From realizability certificates to the Erdős 81 bound": a realizability certificate of Paper V for an auxiliary conflict system whose target is the physical system of copies of K₃ and K₄ in G (conflict when they share an edge, gain C(|K|,2) − 1), with q ≥ 1 classes and budget q·e(G) + cost ≤ q·T + w(X), gives a clique partition of G into pieces of order at most four with at most T pieces (note_I_partition_of_certificate; no chordality); a physical packing with e(G) − g(P) ≤ T does the same (note_I_partition_of_paid_packing); with a certified fractional optimum w, the far branch (e(G) − w < n²/6 − ηn², every η > 0, large n, no chordality) and the near branch (chordal, n ≥ 4·10¹², η = 10⁻¹⁶) give partitions with at most M(n) = ⌊n(n+1)/6⌋ pieces (note_I_far_certificate, note_I_near_certificate); assembled through the transfer, every large chordal graph has such a partition (note_I_erdos81_eventual) and every chordal graph one with at most M(n) + b pieces for an absolute b (note_I_erdos81_all_orders). Note II, "Exact stability for nearly extremal chordal clique partitions": for n large, every chordal graph on n vertices with cp(G) ≤ M(n) and 2000 (M(n) − cp(G)) ≤ n has the root P = {v : n < 2 deg v}, which is a clique, with cp(G) = B(n,|P|) − A − 2m = cp_{≤4}(G), M − cp = (M − B) + A + 2m, edit distance to K_P ∨ I_O equal to A + m and at most M − cp, and (6|P| − 2n − 1)² ≤ 24(M − cp) + 25 (note_II_eventual_root_stability). Seven statements; the thresholds N and the constant b are existential.

records.title: Kotzig's theorem on light edges of planar graphs
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Kotzig's theorem on light edges and its relatives, for finite simple graphs with the combinatorial planarity (genus-zero rotation systems) of the registered entry Kuratowski's theorem. The weight of an edge uv is deg u + deg v. A planar graph of minimum degree at least three has an edge of weight at most 13 (kotzig_borodin; the form without 3-connectivity conjectured by Erdős and proved by Borodin); a planar graph of minimum degree at least four has an edge of weight at most 11 (light_edge_minDegree_four); Kotzig's theorem (1955): a 3-connected planar graph has an edge of weight at most 13, and at most 11 if it has no vertex of degree three (kotzig); Wernicke's theorem (1904): a planar graph of minimum degree at least five has a vertex of degree five adjacent to a vertex of degree at most six (wernicke). Four statements. The proof is a discharging argument carried out directly on the rotation system, without triangulating.

records.title: Borodin's light triangles in planar graphs of minimum degree five
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Borodin's theorem on light triangles, for finite simple graphs with the combinatorial planarity (genus-zero rotation systems) of the registered entry Kuratowski's theorem. The weight of a triangle is the sum of the degrees of its vertices. Every plane map of a graph of minimum degree at least five has a face of length three of weight at most 17 (light_face), and hence a planar graph of minimum degree at least five has a triangle of weight at most 17 (light_triangle). Two statements. The proof is a discharging argument run on the rotation system, with face charges in place of an edge-maximal counterexample; the local analysis at 5-vertices (32768 configurations of neighbour degrees capped at eight and corner types) is checked by decide in the kernel.

records.title: Light stars and paths in planar graphs of minimum degree five (Jendrol'–Madaras)
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Theorems 1, 2 and 3 of Jendrol' and Madaras (1996), for finite simple graphs with the combinatorial planarity (genus-zero rotation systems) of the registered entry Kuratowski's theorem. Every planar graph of minimum degree at least five has: a vertex X of degree five with three distinct neighbours A1, A2, A3 such that deg A1 = 5, deg A2 ≤ 6 and deg A3 ≤ 7, or deg A1 = deg A2 = deg A3 = 6 (light_star, Theorem 1; in particular a 5-vertex with three neighbours of degree at most seven, "Lebesgue's star"); a vertex of degree five with four distinct neighbours of degree at most ten (light_star4, Theorem 2); and a path on four vertices whose degrees sum to at most 23 (light_path4, Theorem 3). Three statements. The proofs are discharging arguments run on the rotation system with face charges instead of triangulating or using edge-maximal counterexamples; the local analyses (32768, 16384, 32768 and 100000 configurations) and the parity of an 11-cycle are checked by decide in the kernel.

records.title: Full beta lambda calculus and finite Turing machine computability
records.abstract: Closed untyped de Bruijn lambda terms under full beta reachability of Church numerals compute exactly the unary partial numerical functions computed by finite three-symbol unary Turing machines. The package defines translations in both directions and proves pointwise numerical-result and no-result equivalences.
authors: Ruy José Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Erdős Problem 935: powerful parts of products of consecutive integers
records.abstract: For the powerful part Q_2(m) of m, this formalization proves that limsup Q_2(n(n+1)...(n+l))/n^2 is infinite for every l >= 2 (the second question of Erdős Problem 935), and at least 1 for every l >= 1 (a consequence of a result of Mahler noted by Erdős). Both use solutions of the Pell equation x^2 = 8y^2 + 1.

records.title: On the Riemann hypothesis and the difference between primes
records.abstract: A Lean 4 proof of Theorems 1, 2 and 3 of A. W. Dudek, On the Riemann hypothesis and the difference between primes, Int. J. Number Theory 11, 2015, arXiv 1402.6417. Each theorem is conditional on the Riemann hypothesis, the paper's own hypothesis, stated with Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis. Theorem 2: for every real x at least 2 there is a prime in the interval from x - (4/pi) sqrt(x) log x to x. Theorem 1: there is c > 0 such that the interval from x to x + c sqrt(x) log x holds more than sqrt(x) primes for every real x at least 2. Theorem 3: for every epsilon > 0 and all large x there is a prime in the interval from x - (1 + epsilon) sqrt(x) log x to x. Each theorem also takes one cited input as an explicit hypothesis, never as an axiom: HSWN70 gZ, the zero count of Hasanalizade, Shen and Wong, arXiv 2107.06506, Corollary 1.2, for T at least 70, stated for gZ, the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function counted with multiplicity. The paper cites the zero count of Trudgian 2014 at this point, whose constant Hasanalizade, Shen and Wong report to be in error; the corrected count is used instead. The bounds of Schoenfeld 1976 for psi - theta, which the paper also cites, are not an input here: the needed estimate is proved. Dudek's Lemma 4 and the explicit formula for psi_1 are proved as well. An AI agent, Claude, wrote the Lean code, with the ported PrimeNumberTheoremAnd files credited to their authors in PORTING.md; the statements were checked against the paper by AI agents and are offered for human audit.

records.title: Mémoire sur les nombres premiers
records.abstract: A Lean 4 proof, with no unproved steps and no hypotheses, of explicit two-sided bounds for Chebyshev's function psi from P. L. Chebyshev, Mémoire sur les nombres premiers, 1852, with Chebyshev's constant A = log 2/2 + log 3/3 + log 5/5 - log 30/30 = 0.92129.... For every natural number n at least 30, psi of n is at least A n - 5 log n + 2 log 30 - 1; for every natural number n, psi of n is at most 6A/5 n + 2 log^2 n + 160. The proof uses Chebyshev's combination of log n!, log of the factorials of n/2, n/3 and n/5, and log of the factorial of n/30, as in the paper, with error terms weaker than Chebyshev's. Mathlib has Chebyshev type bounds only with the constants log 2 and log 4. The Lean code was written by an AI agent and is offered for human audit. Goldbach's conjecture is open and is not claimed.

records.title: Uniform attachment with freezing: equivalence in law of the forward and reversed constructions
records.abstract: Lean proof that the forward uniform-attachment/freezing construction and the reversed growth-coalescent construction give the same distribution of labelled rooted trees, after the prescribed erasure of active reverse labels. The equality includes the extinction endpoint. It is stated on a canonical encoding that retains the complete graph and relevant labels. The dictionary to literal isomorphism-class language is mathematically reviewed but is not an additional Lean quotient-law equivalence theorem. This entry covers T05 and shares its proof repository with the companion asymptotic and SIR entries.

records.title: Computability theory for closed lambda programs
records.abstract: Formalizes recursively enumerable completeness of full-beta Church-numeral reachability, an extensional Rice theorem, and a computable universal-existential normal-form completeness theorem for numerical totality of closed untyped lambda programs.
authors: Ruy José Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: The Hamiltonicity threshold of the random graph G(n, p) (Komlós–Szemerédi)
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the sharp Hamiltonicity threshold of the binomial random graph: if ω(n) → ∞, then G(n, (log n + log log n + ω(n))/n) is Hamiltonian with probability tending to 1, and G(n, (log n + log log n − ω(n))/n) is Hamiltonian with probability tending to 0 (Komlós–Szemerédi 1983; Bollobás 1984). The edge probability is clipped to [0, 1] (min 1 above, max 0 below). The statements are given in the finite product model of the registered entry PALOMAR-2026-10-28-000021 (one independent Bernoulli(p) coin per pair of distinct vertices of Fin n) and, as corollaries, for Mathlib's SimpleGraph.binomialRandom with the edge probability projected to [0, 1]. Hamiltonicity is Mathlib's SimpleGraph.IsHamiltonian.

records.title: Light 3-stars and light pairs of faces in plane graphs of minimum face size five (Madaras)
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Theorems 1.1 and 1.3 of Madaras (2004), for finite simple graphs with the combinatorial planarity (genus-zero rotation systems) of the registered entry Kuratowski's theorem. In every plane map of a finite simple graph of minimum degree at least three whose faces all have length at least five, some vertex x of degree three has three distinct neighbours a, b, c with deg a = deg b = 3 and deg c ≤ 4 (light_star3); in particular the star K1,3 is light, with degree sum at most 13. In the same setting, some face of length five shares an edge with a face of length at most six such that all vertices of both faces have degree at most nine (light_pair; the two faces may coincide when the graph is not 2-connected). Two statements. The proof of Theorem 1.1 is a discharging argument on the rotation system with charges deg − 4 and ℓ − 4 in which every face gives each corner at a 3-vertex a weight depending only on the degrees of the two neighbours along the face, and vertices of degree at least five give 1/5 to each 3-neighbour; the local inequalities are checked by decide in the kernel. This replaces the article's transfer of charge between adjacent 3-vertices. Theorem 1.3 is proved by a second discharging with charges 2 deg − 6 and ℓ − 6: vertices give their charge to their corners, and every face gives 1/5 across each edge to an adjacent poor face (length five, all degrees at most five, at most one of degree at least four).

records.title: Numerical refinement and equivalence of closed lambda programs
records.abstract: Classifies full-beta numerical graph inclusion and extensional equivalence for closed untyped lambda programs, including fixed-zero restricted hardness and computable many-one completeness for universal-existential normal forms.
authors: Ruy José Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Weighted independent sets in clique-free graphs
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of a weighted independent-set existence bound for finite clique-free graphs. For every integer r at least four, positive real degree weights s, and nonnegative real objective weights a, a K_r-free graph has an independent set whose a-weight is at least c_r times the sum of a_v f(s(N(v))/s_v), where f is Shearer's function. The coefficient is the explicit positive rational c_r = 1/(1 + 1152 B_0 r), with a fixed absolute constant B_0, and has proved upper and lower bounds of order 1/r. The proof combines scalar potentials, a weighted triangle dichotomy, sparse neighborhood restriction, deletion identities, and compactness induction.

records.title: Discrete Beurling number systems with integer error below every power, without a zero-free half-plane (assuming the short-interval prime number theorem (84))
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of S. Lavery, "Discrete Beurling number systems with integer error below every power of x and no zero-free half-plane". The headline theorem, BModel.one_zero_system_exists, constructs a discrete Beurling generalized number system whose integer counting function satisfies N(x) = x + O_ε(x^ε) for every ε > 0, while its zeta function is zero-free on no half-plane Re s > 1 − ε (a discrete [1, 0]-system in the sense of Broucke–Debruyne–Révész). The second theorem, BModel.corollary_2_2_complete, is Corollary 2.2: the answer to Question Q (must N(x) = Ax + O(x^θ) with θ < 1/2 force a zero-free half-plane?) is negative. The project also proves Theorem A for every θ ∈ (0, 1/2 − 10⁻⁴]: a system with N(x) = x + O(x^θ log* x) whose zeta function has zeros ρ_k with 1 − Re ρ_k = (log log x_k + O(1))/log x_k, i.e. at distance 1·log log x_k / log x_k from the line Re s = 1. The method is integer-first: a randomised greedy rule chooses each generalized prime so that the integer count tracks a target x + R(x) whose oscillation R plants the zeros; the main work is a positive drift for the queue of composites at every scale, using a Beurling–Saias-type resolvent bound, a local prime number theorem for the realised system and a cluster-counting theorem, with numerical certificates checked by the Lean kernel (decide +kernel). In Lean both theorems are conditional on one explicit hypothesis, BaseRange.Huxley84, eq. (84) of the paper: a short-interval prime number theorem for the rational primes (relative error ≤ (log q)⁻³ on every interval of length ≥ (2q)^{7/12} in [q, 2q], for large q). This is a known theorem (Heath-Brown 1988 with the de la Vallée Poussin error term) that is not in Mathlib; it is a hypothesis of the theorems, not an axiom. The paper and the formalization were produced with heavy AI assistance (Claude agents; the Lean development was started by Aristotle, Harmonic) and have had no human expert review.

records.title: Uniform attachment with freezing: height and distance asymptotics
records.abstract: Lean proofs of the height and distance asymptotics for uniform attachment trees with freezing in Uniform attachment with freezing. The selected results are the three parts of the universal height theorem and the four conclusions of the linear-growth theorem: the deterministic height scale, uniform-vertex height, independent-pair distance and maximum-height limits. Sampling includes frozen vertices where required and coincident pairs. This entry covers T03–T04; the companion local-limit, construction-equivalence and SIR results use separate entries from the same repository.

records.title: BandParityTower: the band-parity tower and its limit modulo eight
records.abstract: For a prime p let a = v_2(p-1), m = (p-1)/2^a, H_a the subgroup of (Z/p)^x of order m and s(x) = (-1)^<x>. The development proves the tower of band-parity laws of Paper I of the author's series: the cyclotomic tower (every coordinate of the band-parity sum of the character of order 2^a is congruent modulo 4 to an explicit count), the band-parity tower f_a = sum over H_a of s(u) s(u^2) = m (mod 4) at every odd prime, the doubling count sum over 2H_a of s(u) s(2u) = 2 N_a - m, the imaginary law e_a = 2 N_a - m (mod 4) at every prime p = 1 (mod 4) with its level-3 form, the collapse e_a = +-f_a when 2 is a 2^(a-1)-th power residue, and E. Lehmer's criterion for 2 to be a 2k-th power residue. It also proves the power-map family, the companion law Re C = Im C = kappa (mod 4) at p = 1 (mod 8), and Lehmer-type invariants of the inversion map modulo 4; and, modulo 8, the joint-parity form, the dichotomy, squaring cycles and the order-three pair, the defect lemma, odd multipliers as floor sums and the fifth-interval formula linking M_H(5) to B_{1,theta_p}.

records.title: Erdős Problem 654: distinct distances from a point when no four points are concyclic
records.abstract: Erdős asked whether, for every set of n points in the plane with no four on a circle, some point has at least (1 - o(1))n distinct distances to the other points. Feng et al. (arXiv:2601.22401; construction found by their agent Aletheia) answered no, using 4m points on the coordinate axes at powers of 2 and 3. This formalization proves the negative answer and their statement (for every m >= 10 there are 4m points, no four on a circle, each with at most 3m - 1 distinct distances to the other points), using a different set on the same axes: (±2i, 0) and (0, ±(2j - 1)) for 1 <= i, j <= m. An auxiliary lemma gives the bound for every m >= 1.

records.title: Erdős Problem 657: Straus's observation on isosceles-free point sets with few distances
records.abstract: Erdős asked whether a set of n points in the plane with no isosceles triangle must determine at least f(n)n distinct distances for some f(n) tending to infinity, and asked the same in R^k for each fixed k. Straus observed that no such bound holds uniformly in the dimension. In the form stated in formal-conjectures: for every k there are 2^k points in R^k with no isosceles triangle and at most 2^k - 1 distinct distances. This formalization proves that statement, using the points whose i-th coordinate is 0 or sqrt(2^i); the sources consulted do not record Straus's own construction.

records.title: Kac's return-time formula for any measure-preserving map
records.abstract: A machine-checked proof of Kac's return-time formula. For a measure-preserving map f and a measurable set A, the integral over A of the first return time to A equals the measure of the points whose orbit ever meets A. The return time is valued in the extended naturals, infinite for a point that never returns, and with that convention the formula holds for every measure, with no finiteness, sigma-finiteness, conservativity or ergodicity assumption. For an ergodic map of a probability space and mu(A) > 0 the integral is 1, so the mean return time to A, starting in A, is 1 / mu(A).

records.title: QuarterSumLadder: the quarter-sum ladder and the weight-two congruences
records.abstract: For a prime p = 1 (mod 8) and a quartic character chi modulo p (even, with w = chi(2) = +-1), the development proves that the coordinates of B_(2,chi) = c0 + i c1 are integers with c0 = 4(E_1 + E_-1), c1 = 4(E_i + E_-i) and c0 + c1 = p - 1 modulo 8, and that 8 divides both exactly when w = 1, i.e. when 2 is a fourth power. A Gauss-Lehmer product argument gives the quartic Gauss lemma w = (-1)^(R_1 + R_3) for the quarter counts R_r, the parity of the four quarter counts when w = 1, and the parity of R_2 through the order of 2. For the quarter sum Omega = x + iy (2N(Omega) = h^-(K) for the imaginary cyclic quartic field K of conductor 4p, not formalized) it proves criteria in the quarter counts for 2^k | 2N(Omega), 2 <= k <= 6, a classical evaluation of the fourth, the coordinate valuation formula, a congruence modulo 16 linking c0 - c1 to x - y, and the valuation of B_(2,chi) at 1 + i on its first three cases.

records.title: Absolutely maximally entangled states of seven parties: for d >= 2, AME(7, d) exists exactly when d >= 3
records.abstract: Machine-checked proofs that no absolutely maximally entangled state of seven qubits exists, and that for local dimension d >= 2 an absolutely maximally entangled state of seven parties exists exactly when d >= 3. The statements and definitions are Formal Conjectures' (Open Quantum Problem 35), copied verbatim into Challenge.lean, so this entry proves Formal Conjectures' own statements; one proof step inside the definition combineFirst is changed so that Comparator can match it, and the definition is unchanged. The proofs follow Huber, Gühne and Siewert (2017) and Shi, Zhang, Zhao and Li (2026).

records.title: Erdős Problem 393: f(n) tends to infinity, assuming the abc conjecture
records.abstract: Let f(n) be the least m >= 1 such that n! = a_1 ... a_t with a_1 < ... < a_t = a_1 + m. Assuming the abc conjecture, f(n) tends to infinity. The proof follows Luca's proof that abc implies finitely many solutions of P(x) = n!, for the polynomials prod_{i in T} (x + i): for a fixed set T of d offsets, the shift y = d a + sum(T) gives d^d prod_{i in T} (a + i) = y^d + y^k R(y) with k + deg R <= d - 2 and R(0) != 0, and abc, with rad(n!) <= 4^n, bounds y by an exponential in n, while y^d >= n!. It does not assume Luca's theorem; only the reduction from f(n) to these polynomials is specific to Problem 393.

records.title: Checking the odd Goldbach conjecture up to 10^20
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the mathematics of Y. Saouter, Checking the odd Goldbach conjecture up to 10^20, Math. Comp. 67, 1998, 863 to 866. Proved with no hypothesis: Lemma 1, the paper's form of Theorem 5 of Brillhart, Lehmer and Selfridge 1975, for every even F; Theorem 1, the primality criterion for N = 2^22 R + 1 below 10^20 with R odd and any base a with a^((N-1)/2) = -1 modulo N; Lemma 2 by quadratic reciprocity; Theorem 2, the case of base 5; the primality of the 100 rungs of Table 1 and of the first and last primes printed in the paper. The printed ladder constant 1258213 is a misprint for 12582913, and this repair is proved. The entry does not reverify Saouter's computation: his ladder of about 250 million rungs is checked only through its first 100 rungs. As a derived result, not a theorem of the paper, every odd number from 7 to 10^20 is a sum of three primes, conditional on one cited input taken as an explicit hypothesis, never as an axiom: EvenGoldbachUpTo of 4 * 10^18, the published computation of T. Oliveira e Silva, S. Herzog and S. Pardi, Math. Comp. 83, 2014, not proved here. That proof uses Saouter's prime ladder with 25 Proth rungs as in Helfgott and Platt, so the paper's range is reproduced by a different ladder on a much larger even input than Saouter's 4 * 10^11. Ternary Goldbach for all odd numbers is Helfgott's theorem, from his 2013 preprint, and is not formalized here. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. AI agents wrote the Lean code, which is offered for human audit.

records.title: Light paths and only paths in 3-connected planar graphs (Fabrici–Jendrol')
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the two theorems of Fabrici and Jendrol' (1997), for finite simple graphs with the combinatorial planarity (genus-zero rotation systems) of the registered entry Kuratowski's theorem. Theorem 1 (light_path): a 3-connected planar graph that contains a path on k ≥ 1 vertices contains such a path whose vertices all have degree at most 5k. Theorem 2 (only_paths_light): for every connected planar graph H that is not a path (not isomorphic to pathGraph on its vertex count) and every m, there is a 3-connected planar graph containing a copy of H in which every copy of H (an injective edge-preserving map) has a vertex of degree at least m. Two statements. Theorem 1 follows the proof reproduced in the Jendrol'–Voss survey (maximal counterexample, chords at major vertices, a major vertex with at most five major neighbours). Theorem 2 uses a different construction from the article's: H is completed to an edge-maximal planar graph, whose faces are triangles, and two chains of repeated stellations are inserted in every face, so that the light vertices induce disjoint paths; the result is a plane triangulation, hence 3-connected. The extremal example for 5k is not formalized.

records.title: An absolutely maximally entangled state of twelve five-level systems: AME(12, 5) exists
records.abstract: A machine-checked proof that an absolutely maximally entangled state of twelve five-level systems exists. The statement and definitions are Formal Conjectures' (Open Quantum Problem 35, `ame_12_5_open`), copied verbatim into Challenge.lean, so this entry proves Formal Conjectures' own statement; one proof step inside the definition combineFirst is changed so that Comparator can match it, and the definition is unchanged. The witness is the graph state of the AME(12, 5) graph of S. Bevins and Y. Bidav. The proof is a general graph-state criterion over ZMod 5 plus 924 kernel-checked cut certificates.

records.title: QuarticPairing: the pairing of the twists in Conjecture 1.2 of David, Dunn, Hamieh and Lin
records.abstract: Conjecture 1.2 of C. David, A. Dunn, A. Hamieh and H. Lin (arXiv:2306.11875) asserts that the sums S_beta(X; l) of normalized quartic Gauss sums g(c) over primary primes c of Z[i] with N(c) <= X and c = beta (mod 4), twisted by (conj(c)/|c|)^l and weighted by the von Mangoldt function, are b_beta X^(3/4) + O(X^(1/2+eps)) with b_beta nonzero when l = 0 and O(X^(1/2+eps)) when l is nonzero. The development proves that if g(c)^2 = -kappa c/|c| for a fixed unit kappa on the support of the weight (the identity (1.2) of the same paper), then g(c) conj(c)/|c| = -kappa conj(g(c)), so S_beta(X; 1) = -kappa conj(S_beta(X; 0)), and the cases l = 0 and l = 1 of the conjecture force b_beta = 0, which the conjecture excludes; the same holds when the identity fails on an exceptional set of weight O(X^(1/2+eps)). More generally S_beta(X; 1 - l) = -kappa conj(S_beta(X; l)) for every l. The corrected conjecture, with main term -kappa conj(b_beta) X^(3/4) at l = 1, is shown equivalent under the identity to its cases l <= 0, and that main term is shown to be the only one compatible with the case l = 0. It also proves the pairing identities A(nu^3, -m) = -kappa conj A(nu, m) for the twisted moments and the fact behind the special role of order four: if |g| = 1 and g^k = xi then conj(g) = g^(k-1) conj(xi). The Gauss sum and the von Mangoldt function are abstract functions on the Gaussian integers, so no quartic residue symbol is defined.

records.title: Finite numerical domains of closed lambda programs
records.abstract: Classifies finite numerical domains of closed untyped lambda programs under full beta reduction, and gives an exact initial-segment versus total-domain gap for the hardness construction.
authors: Ruy José Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Exact directed L/X diameter of the symmetric group
records.abstract: For every n >= 5, the directed Cayley graph of the symmetric group S_n with unit-cost generators L = (0 1 ... n-1) and X = (0 1) has diameter (3n^2 - 8n + 12)/4 for even n and (3n^2 - 8n + 9)/4 for odd n. The formalization proves matching upper and lower bounds, and the existence of a literal L/X word within the sharp bound between every ordered pair of permutations. The independent statement takes the maximum of minimum word lengths over all ordered pairs. No inverse shift is included among the unit-cost moves.

records.title: The Arithmetic of Time: reversible units of a degree-nine field. The units of K = LM (L, M cubic) with rank-one Hermitian symbol are exactly those of trivial relative norm to L and to M, a group of rank two, and exactly those whose Schur multipliers run both ways
records.abstract: Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, of ten statements. Let K be a number field of degree 9 containing a totally real cubic field L and a cubic field M with one real place. Then K = LM has signature (3, 3), and its nine embeddings are the pairs (lambda, mu). A slot assignment, fixed by a labelling of L's embeddings and a non-real embedding mu_1 of M, places the nine conjugates of x in K in a 3 x 3 Hermitian array, the symbol of x; the symbol of x^-1 is its entrywise (Hadamard) inverse. (1) For every finite index type, a positive semidefinite complex matrix with no zero entry has positive semidefinite Hadamard inverse iff it is w w* (rank one); (2) for every complex matrix with no zero entry (positive semidefiniteness not assumed), the Schur multipliers of the matrix and of its Hadamard inverse are both completely positive iff it is w w*. Statements 1-2 are supporting lemmas. (3) The setting: L and M are linearly disjoint, L M = K, and K has 3 real and 3 complex places. (4) The slot assignment exists, is a bijection Fin 3 x Fin 3 ~ (K -> C) with real diagonal and conjugate-symmetric slots, and is unique. (5) For x != 0 in K, the symbol of x is rank one iff N_{K/L}(x) and N_{K/M}(x) are one and the same positive rational number. (6) For a unit u, the symbol is rank one iff N_{K/L}(u) = N_{K/M}(u) = 1. (7) These units H are torsion-free and their logarithmic embedding spans a Z-module of rank 2, so H is isomorphic to Z^2 (the isomorphism is not itself a Lean term). (8) For a unit u, the Schur multipliers of the symbols of u and of u^-1 are both completely positive iff u is in H. (9) There is a unit of infinite order all of whose powers run both ways. (10) The degree-four contrast: in a field with two real places and one complex place, both Schur multipliers of the 2 x 2 place symbol of a unit u and of u^-1 are completely positive iff u is positive at both real places and |sigma(u)| = 1. Statements 4-6, 8 and 9 hold for every labelling and every non-real mu_1. The compositum place bookkeeping is ported, with citation, from the registered entry PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012; it is not re-proved. Application to time (no compared statement asserts it): in the arithmetic of time the tick is multiplication by a unit; if a unit acts by multiplication on a Hermitian register of its places and an admissible tick must be completely positive, then in degree four a tick u != 1 runs both ways only through a conjugate on the unit circle (Salem type); in a field such as Q(Q), Q^4 = Q + 1, the only such elements are +-1 (not proved in this entry; it follows from statement 17 of the registered entry PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012, since Q(Q) is contained in Q(rho, Q)), so there the arithmetic gives time a direction; in degree nine a rank-two group of units runs both ways, so the direction is not a property of arithmetic in general: it rests on the degree-four shape and on Q(Q) having no conjugate on the unit circle. The ticks are completely positive, not trace-non-increasing. Companion of the registered entry PALOMAR-2026-08-19-000006 (the arithmetic of time), whose README Scope section is reproduced verbatim in this entry's README.

records.title: MellinDuality: Mellin duality for the band-parity companion
records.abstract: For an odd prime p, an odd character chi modulo p and m >= 0, the multiplier family C(a) = sum over 0 < n < p/2 of chi(n) (-1)^(n + <a n^(2m)>) has Fourier transform over the characters 2 sum_a conj(psi)(a) C(a) = G(conj psi) G(chi psi^(2m)), with the multiplier constant G(psi) = sum_m psi(m) (-1)^m = 2 (1 - 2 psi(2)) B_(1,psi). The development proves this Mellin duality over any commutative ring, its inversion over the odd complex characters and its form bilinear in first Bernoulli numbers, the half-sum identity, the exponent family and its two collapses. At p = 5 (mod 8), for the quartic character, it proves the coset decomposition of the family, its exact sums over the cosets of the fourth powers, conjugate dynamics, the two second-moment identities, the decomposition of the second-order products of the band-parity companion by coprime pairs, and Parseval's identity for the band weight. Through the inversion and Parseval's identity over the odd characters it proves, for every a not divisible by p, the exact second moment sum over odd chi of |sum over odd psi of psi(a) (1 - 2 conj(psi)(2)) (1 - 2 chi(2) psi(2)^2) B_(1,conj psi) B_(1,chi psi^2)|^2 = ((p - 1)/2)^4.

records.title: Cofinite numerical domains of closed lambda programs
records.abstract: Classifies cofinite numerical domains of closed untyped lambda programs under full beta reduction, using finite-injury markers and computable three-quantifier normal forms.
authors: Ruy José Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Effective Rice–Shapiro theorem for closed lambda programs
records.abstract: Characterizes recursively enumerable extensional numerical properties of closed full-beta lambda programs by effectively enumerable families of finite graph tables, with finite-witness and extension consequences.
authors: Ruy José Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: QuadraticFloorII: fibre sums and quartic traces at conductor 8lp
records.abstract: Sequel to QuadraticFloor. For an odd prime p, the alternating floor sums S_{A,B,C}(p) = sum over 0 <= n < p of (-1)^floor((A n^2 + B n + C)/p) with admissible (B, C) are averages of first Bernoulli numbers of the odd characters vartheta_{p,psi} = eta_p chi_{-4}^delta psi modulo 8Ap. The development proves that, weighted by psi_0(b)^2 and summed over the units b modulo A, these sums give minus the sum of B_{1,vartheta_{p,psi}} over the fibre psi^2 = psi_0^2, which is real when psi_0^4 = 1; that for a prime l = 1 (mod 4), a quartic character xi modulo l and an odd prime p != l the real part of B_{1,Theta_{l,p}}, Theta_{l,p} = vartheta_{p,xi}, and the Bernoulli number of eta_p (./l) are signed combinations of floor sums (the case l = 13 included); the Euler-factor relation B_{1,f 1_{l does not divide}}^{(ml)} = (1 - f(l)) B_{1,f}^{(m)} and the class-number shapes of the coefficients three and five; the quarter-range formula B_{1,vartheta_{p,psi}}^{(8Ap)} = -sum_{0<x<=2Ap} vartheta_{p,psi}(x); and an elementary proof that both coordinates of B_{1,Theta_{l,p}}^{(8lp)} are even integers, for every odd prime p. Every Bernoulli number is taken at a stated modulus; 8lp is the conductor of Theta_{l,p} only for p != l.

records.title: Recursion and effective inseparability for closed lambda programs
records.abstract: Proves a uniform recursion theorem for closed lambda numerical semantics and a productive-map effective inseparability result for the closed zero and one numeral languages.
authors: Ruy José Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Injective padding and one-one completeness for closed lambda programs
records.abstract: Formalizes syntax-injective semantics-preserving padding and primitive-recursive one-one completeness of a concrete closed lambda zero-result language, with productive-complement consequences.
authors: Ruy José Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Productive complements and one-one completeness for extensional lambda properties
records.abstract: Formalizes a general constructive reduction from productivity and an injectivization theorem for numerical-extensional closed lambda languages.
authors: Ruy José Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Written on the Wall II, Conjecture 84: tree(G) ≥ 2 rad(G) / δ(G)
records.abstract: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Conjecture 84 of DeLaViña's "Written on the Wall II" (conjectures of Graffiti.pc): for every finite simple connected graph G with positive minimum degree δ(G), the maximum number of vertices of an induced subtree satisfies tree(G) ≥ 2·rad(G)/δ(G). The formal statement is the one recorded in google-deepmind/formal-conjectures (WrittenOnTheWallII/GraphConjecture84.lean, theorem `conjecture84`), copied verbatim together with its definition of `largestInducedTreeSize`. The proof formalizes the argument of J. J. Gebendorfer's manuscript "Induced trees in graphs with a cut vertex" (28 October 2026): the case δ(G) ≥ 2 follows from a diametral geodesic, and the case δ(G) = 1 from the stronger theorem tree(G) ≥ 2·rad(G) for every connected graph with a cut vertex, proved by a minimal-counterexample reduction to a 2-connected core with pendant paths of equal positive length. Along the way the induced-tree consequence tree(H) ≥ 2·rad(H) − 1 of Chung's induced-path bound (Erdős–Saks–Sós 1986, Theorem 2.2) is proved, which is all the argument needs.

records.title: Erdős Problem 1033: a butterfly blow-up beating 2(√3 - 1)
records.abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib proof that the Bollobás–Erdős question of Erdős Problem 1033 has a negative answer. For every t ≥ 1 an explicit blow-up of the butterfly graph (two triangles sharing a vertex) on n = 668t vertices has 111561t² > n²/4 edges, and every triangle has degree sum exactly 978t, while 978/668 < 2(√3 - 1). Hence it is false that every graph on n vertices with more than n²/4 edges has a triangle with degree sum at least (2(√3 - 1) - o(1))n.

records.title: Productive closed lambda languages and one-one completeness
records.abstract: Formalizes a non-extensional creative-to-one-one completeness argument for predicates on closed lambda syntax, using uniform finite avoidance and computable fresh-output selection.
authors: Ruy José Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Effective isomorphism from one-one equivalence
records.abstract: Formalizes the effective-isomorphism theorem for arbitrary predicates on natural numbers: mutual computable injective reductions yield a computable permutation with computable inverse preserving membership.
