authors: Ruy José Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Erdős Problem 654: the Aletheia counterexample
records.abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib proof that Erdős Problem 654 has a negative answer: for every m ≥ 10 there is a set of n = 4m points in the Euclidean plane, no four on a circle, in which every point has fewer than 3n/4 distinct distances to the other points. Consequently it is false that every n-point planar set with no four concyclic points has a point with (1 - o(1))n distinct distances. The construction (Aletheia; Feng et al., arXiv:2601.22401) places the points (0, ±3^(k+1)) and (±2^(j+1), 0) on the two coordinate axes.

records.title: Computable bijection between recursive computations and closed lambda terms
records.abstract: Constructs computable inverse maps between recursive-code/input pairs and all closed lambda terms, preserving defined evaluation as Church-zero observation.
authors: Ruy José Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: A value-preserving unary recursive-code and lambda isomorphism
records.abstract: Constructs computable inverse maps between recursive codes and closed untyped lambda terms that preserve every unary partial numerical function.
authors: Ruy José Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Triangle decompositions III: physical typed absorption and prescribed statistics
records.abstract: The Lean source supplement of Paper III of the Nash-Williams series (preprint 1.0), packaged with a Mathlib-only Challenge. Theorem T: for fixed labels I, allowed label multisets F and constants alpha > 0, C >= 1, h >= 6, every labelled graph of order at least n0 that has an exact diffuse fractional triangle seed of constant C (H1), whose edge indicator lies in the integer lattice spanned by its allowed triangles (H2), with at least alpha n common neighbours labelled k for every pair of distinct vertices and every label k completing an allowed type (H3), and at least alpha n^(i-4) physical hinges of some order 6 <= i <= h for every pair of allowed triangles on a common edge (H4), has an allowed triangle decomposition. Theorem T+: for every eta > 0 and q the decomposition can moreover be chosen so that every family of at most n^q triangle tests bounded by 1, and the Pasch count, are within eta n^2 of their values under the seed. Applications: Latin squares following a bounded stochastic profile with prescribed statistics and Pasch count (Theorem 8.1), the uniform and signed rank-one profiles with their intercalate counts (Corollaries 8.2 and 8.3), two Latin squares each of which separately approximates, up to eps m^2, the same prescribed statistics and the same eight coarse-block targets (their own values need not coincide), with intercalate counts near different targets (Theorem 8.4, m divisible by four), and the balanced complete five-partite graph with parts of size 3|A| and rainbow triangles (Corollary 8.5). Seven statements. All thresholds are existential; the explicit tower bound of Section 7 is not compared.

records.title: Counting sets with small sumset
records.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of Green's paper Counting sets with small sumset, and the clique number of random Cayley graphs. For a finite abelian group Γ, let S_k^m(Γ) be the family of the sets X in Γ with |X| = k whose restricted sumset X ∔ X = {x + y : x, y in X, x ≠ y} has m elements. The paper bounds |S_k^m(Γ)| for Γ = Z/NZ and Γ = F_2^n, through a bound for the number of Freiman isomorphism classes of sets with small restricted sumset in a vector space. It deduces that the Cayley sum graph of a random subset of Z/NZ almost surely has clique number at most 160 log_2 N, and that the Cayley graph of a random subset of F_2^n almost surely has clique number between C_1 n log_2 n and C_2 n log_2 n. The formalization proves these results with C_1 = 1/4 and C_2 = 308, both as limits and as explicit bounds on the number of exceptional sets.

records.title: Full beta normal-order normalization for untyped lambda terms
records.abstract: Defines the deterministic full-beta leftmost-outermost strategy and proves it reaches any reachable normal form on de Bruijn terms, including open terms.
authors: Ruy José Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: A call-by-name to call-by-value CPS adequacy theorem
records.abstract: Proves closed-source weak call-by-name convergence is equivalent to weak call-by-value convergence of a concrete CPS translation with exact translated-value readback.
authors: Ruy José Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Erdős Problem 338: restricted order of robust sets of positive lower density
records.abstract: If A \ F is a basis for every finite set F and A has positive lower density, then A has a restricted order: every sufficiently large integer is a sum of a bounded number of distinct elements of A. This is a partial result on Erdős Problem 338 (Erdős and Graham ask whether every such A, without the density condition, has a restricted order). The proof counts pairs to show that, for every R, the numbers with at least R representations as a sum of two distinct elements of A have positive lower density, uniformly in R; uses Kneser's theorem for finite abelian groups to write all large numbers of one residue class as sums of a bounded number of such numbers; fixes the residue class with distinct elements of A; and chooses the representations greedily so that all summands are distinct.

records.title: Effective inseparability of closed lambda normal-form languages
records.abstract: Proves that closed terms with numeral normal forms and those with nonnumerical normal forms form disjoint r.e. effectively inseparable languages.
authors: Ruy José Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Weil Bounds Toolkit
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the classical prime-modulus Kloosterman-Weil bound |S_p(m,n)| <= 2 sqrt(p) for nonzero m, n, proved by the Carlitz-Stepanov method following Harcos's exposition, together with an exact Chinese-remainder factorization of unit Kloosterman sums, a squarefree-modulus bound for a unit first coefficient, a bound for the sum defined at the reduced modulus q/gcd(A,q), and interval-length-uniform and weighted bounds for centered incomplete reciprocal sums.

records.title: Fractional clique decompositions of dense partite graphs
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the main theorem of R. Montgomery, "Fractional clique decompositions of dense partite graphs" (arXiv:1603.01039; Combin. Probab. Comput. 26 (2017)): for r ≥ 3, every balanced K_r-divisible r-partite graph with parts of size n in which every vertex has at least (1 − 1/(10⁶r³))n neighbours in every other part has a fractional K_r-decomposition (Theorem 1.1); and its non-partite consequence: every graph on n vertices with minimum degree at least (1 − 1/(10⁶r³))n has a fractional K_r-decomposition. The whole proof is formalized: clique counts (Proposition 3.2, Lemma 3.3), the two gadgets (Lemmas 4.2, 4.3), the splitting lemma (Lemma 4.4), the moving lemmas (Lemmas 5.2, 5.3, 5.6) and the final averaging. Not formalized: Theorem 1.2 (integral decompositions), which also needs the fractional-to-exact transfer of Barber, Kühn, Lo, Osthus and Taylor.

records.title: Pointwise Ergodic Theorems Along $\lfloor p^c\rfloor$ for Every $c>1$
records.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of the variational estimate, common pointwise limit for von Mangoldt and prime averages, and logarithmic Mobius cancellation in Pointwise Ergodic Theorems Along $\lfloor p^c\rfloor$ for Every $c>1$. The author selected the a.e. conclusion for the submitted prime-convergence statement. All results are stated for sigma-finite measure-preserving systems.

records.title: Resolution of Singularities of an Algebraic Variety Over a Field of Characteristic Zero
records.abstract: Heisuke Hironaka's 1964 papers 'Resolution of singularities of an algebraic variety over a field of characteristic zero I,II' were seminal achievements in the history of algebraic geometry. They had inestimable impact on a broad range of research areas in mathematics including geometry, topology, number theory, differential equations, and mathematical physics. The achievement was recognised by a Fields medal awarded to Hironaka in 1970. The papers constitute a veritable tour de force contained in 217 densely-packed pages. The algebraic and combinatorial complexity of the papers is daunting, especially towards the later portions, and have led to a significant level of persistent incomprehension even on the part of domain experts. Because more transparent proofs of the same result appeared in the 1990s, the question of understanding the original papers in detail has become somewhat forgotten. In the associated repository, we have formalised Hironaka's argument in full, modulo results he cites. We have also compiled an erratum, and included complementary arguments for a few portions of the paper that had non-trivial gaps. In a separate publication, we will give some of the narrative background, the interesting story of the mathematical community's tortuous efforts to understand these great works. The size of the formalization has forced us to split this work over three Palomar entries, one for each comparator configuration. The related entries can be found at PALOMAR-2026-11-04-000004 and PALOMAR-2026-11-04-000012 respectively.

records.title: A quantitative homotopy-interleaving gap over the cyclic-four group algebra
records.abstract: Over the group algebra F2[C4] of the cyclic group of order four in characteristic two, we give an explicit five-stage real-indexed persistence diagram F of unbounded chain complexes. Its stages are shifts of the periodic free resolution of the trivial module, on half-open intervals [i, i+1), with zero diagram before time 0 and from time 5 on. We compare three distances from F to the zero diagram: the homology interleaving distance (supremum over all degrees of the interleaving distances of the F2-homology persistence modules); the interleaving distance in an arbitrary localisation of the category of whole real diagrams at the objectwise quasi-isomorphisms (the derived category of real diagrams); and the strict homotopy-interleaving distance, which allows arbitrary finite zigzags of objectwise quasi-isomorphisms of both entire diagrams, including nonzero acyclic replacements of zero. The Lean development proves d_CohI(F,0) = 1/2 < d_IHC(F,0) = 1 < 5/4 <= d_HI(F,0) <= 5/2. So the three distances are quantitatively separated by a single explicit example. The lower bound for the strict metric comes from a fourfold defining-system obstruction for the resolution. The derived upper bound comes from a natural nullhomotopy of the two-unit shift. The upper bound 5/2 for the strict metric is witnessed directly, because every five-unit shift of F vanishes.

records.title: Deterministic generalized k-server: tower lower bound and strict upper bound
records.abstract: For generalized k-server, each named server moves in its own metric space, a request specifies one point per space, and matching any coordinate serves the request. The development proves a height-k tower lower bound on the deterministic competitive ratio on k real lines for k at least three, allowing arbitrary additive constants. It also proves existence of a lazy deterministic algorithm on arbitrary metric spaces with arbitrary positive movement weights and prescribed initial configuration, with an explicit factor depending only on k and no additive cost or horizon input. The refined deterministic factor is at most tower(k+4) for k at least two.

records.title: Sparse multi-base representations and asymptotic Hadamard existence
records.abstract: Lean formalization of sparse multi-base representations and unconditional asymptotic Hadamard existence, gap, flatness and conditioning bounds. The required logarithm-ratio separation is proved independently from mathlib.

records.title: Goldbach numbers in short intervals of length x^(26/1075+ε)
records.abstract: A Lean 4 proof that for every ε > 0 and all large natural x there is a Goldbach number, an even sum of two primes, in the interval from x to x + 3 x^(26/1075+ε). The theorem is conditional on two cited results taken as explicit hypotheses, never as axioms, and neither is proved here: LiRow052, R. Li, arXiv 2308.04458, Theorem 2, the row θ = 0.52, primes in the intervals from n - n^(0.52+ε) to n with a lower bound of the right order, with some positive constant since the printed constant differs between versions of the paper; and LiPrintedExceptionalCount, R. Li, arXiv 2407.05651 v6, Theorem 1.1, primes in the intervals from n to n + n^(1/21.5+ε) for almost all n. The argument adapts Theorem 7.1 of arXiv 2407.05651 v6, page 27, exponent 21/860 from the 0.525 of Baker, Harman and Pintz. The exponent 26/1075 is lower by 1/4300, and the gain is only the replacement of 0.525 by Li's 0.52. Li prints this exponent himself, as Theorem 7 of arXiv 2308.04458, with no ε and no factor 3, so this is a formal check of a known result and not a new exponent. Li's later note, Primes in almost all short intervals II, claims 1/22+ε in place of 1/21.5+ε, so 26/1075 is not claimed as the best exponent. Both cited papers are used here in their arXiv preprint form. Proved with no cited input: the passage from a count of primes in the intervals below n to a count in the windows from x - 2Y to x - Y, and the combinatorial step from the two counts to a Goldbach number. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. AI agents wrote the Lean code, Claude, Codex and Gemini, as listed in PORTING.md, and it is offered for human audit.

records.title: A finite-machine observer for lambda normal forms
records.abstract: Constructs one finite Turing machine that distinguishes Church-numeral and nonnumerical full-beta normal forms and does not halt exactly when no normal form is reachable.
authors: Ruy José Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Exact beta-step cost of call-by-name CPS translation
records.abstract: Proves an exact affine relationship between weak call-by-name head contractions and weak call-by-value contractions of a CPS translation, including translated closing-context tests.
authors: Ruy José Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: The Jacobian conjecture in dimension 2n implies the Poisson conjecture in dimension n
records.abstract: A machine-checked proof that, over a field of characteristic zero, the Jacobian conjecture in dimension 2n implies the Poisson conjecture in dimension n (K. Adjamagbo and A. van den Essen, 2007, Theorem 7). The statement and definitions are Formal Conjectures' (poisson_conjecture.variants.jacobian_implication in PoissonConjecture.lean, arXiv math/0608009), copied verbatim into Challenge.lean, so this entry proves Formal Conjectures' own statement. A Poisson endomorphism's Jacobian matrix lies in Mathlib's symplectic group, so its determinant is a unit; the Jacobian conjecture then gives a polynomial inverse.

records.title: Helfgott's Proposition 6.2 on the ternary Goldbach minor arcs
records.abstract: A Lean 4 proof of Lemma 6.1 and Proposition 6.2 of H. A. Helfgott, The ternary Goldbach conjecture is true, arXiv 1312.7748v2, Section 6.1, pages 46 to 48. Lemma 6.1 is a summation by parts bound. Proposition 6.2 turns l2 bounds on S1 over the major arcs and l-infinity bounds on S2 off them into a bound for the integral of |S1|^2 |S2| over the minor arcs, without the factor log x that a plain product of norms would lose. Lemma 6.1 is stated as in the paper. Proposition 6.2 is given in three forms: an abstract measure form with a natural upper endpoint; the arcs of display 3.5 for a finite exponential polynomial S1 and a natural upper endpoint; and absolutely summable coefficients with a real upper endpoint, over any increasing measurable family of sets. The hypotheses 6.4 and 6.5 of the Proposition stay hypotheses, as in the paper, and are not proved for any exponential sum. This is one step of Helfgott's proof. The ternary Goldbach theorem itself is not formalized here, nor is Theorem 6.3 of the paper. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. AI agents wrote the Lean code, Claude, Codex and other lab agents, as listed in PORTING.md, and it is offered for human audit.

records.title: Does freezing impede the growth of random recursive trees?
records.abstract: We formalize the principal results of “Does freezing impede the growth of random recursive trees?” for uniform attachment trees with freezing. We prove uniform height lower bounds over all admissible operation sequences with n attachment steps: the height is at least e log n − 5 log log n with probability tending to one, uniformly over these sequences, and the same lower bound holds for expected height for sufficiently large n. We also formalize deletion comparisons: deleting attachment or freezing steps can increase expected height, whereas deleting the attachment–freezing pair at the first change of sign stochastically decreases height.

records.title: ConjCoord: a class number congruence modulo 16 for p = 5 (mod 16) and Conjecture coord of Paper V
records.abstract: For primes p = 5 (mod 16), p = a^2 + b^2 with b even, the companion note proves h(-8p) = h(-4p) + 8 [b = +-6 (mod 16)] (mod 16), which settles Conjecture 5.3 of Paper V of the K Project series. The proof writes 4(h(-8p) - h(-4p)) as a combination of representation numbers of x^2 + 2y^2 + 4z^2 and x^2 + 2y^2 + 2z^2. It shows that a weight-2 form Phi built from sieved theta series vanishes modulo 256, by Sturm's theorem and a finite check below the bound 512, and reads off the coefficient at p. This development formalizes the proof with the modular input (Serre-Stark modularity and Sturm's theorem) and Gauss's three-square class number formula as explicit hypotheses. It proves the finite check by kernel computation, the iteration of Sturm's theorem, the inversion of theta(1), the bijections relating the ternary forms to sums of three squares, the uniqueness argument for p = a^2 + b^2, the congruence, Conjecture 5.3 given Paper V Theorem 5.2(iv), and the corollaries on the octant sum and with Desnoux's congruence.

records.title: Complete minors and average degree (Kostochka–Thomason)
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Kostochka–Thomason theorem, following the short proof of Alon, Krivelevich and Sudakov. complete_minor_of_edges (their Theorem 1): there is d0 such that for every integer d ≥ d0, every nonempty finite simple graph with at least d·|V| edges has the complete graph K_t as a minor for every natural number t ≤ d / (10 √(ln d)). kostochka_thomason: there is a constant c > 0 such that for every integer d ≥ 2, every nonempty finite simple graph with at least d·|V| edges (average degree at least 2d) has a K_t minor for every t ≤ c·d / √(ln d). Minors are branch-set models, with the definition of the registered entry Mader's theorem and Hadwiger's conjecture for t ≤ 4, whose library is a pinned dependency. Two statements; the thresholds d0 and c are existential (the proof gives d0 = ⌈exp(R0²)⌉ + 1 with R0 ≥ 1400).

records.title: Two-colour Zig-Zag Numberlink on rectangles
records.abstract: A Lean 4 proof that two-colour Zig-Zag Numberlink on rectangular grids (the paired 2-disjoint path cover problem: two vertex-disjoint paths s0 → t0 and s1 → t1 that together visit every cell) is decided by an explicit procedure, and that an explicit construction finds a solution whenever one exists. For both sides at least 11, an instance is solvable exactly when it passes a finite catalogue of forbidden patterns; for a side at most 10, a plug dynamic program decides it. The finite cases of the characterization are 21 boxes of slice certificates and 59 window certificates, all checked by the kernel.

records.title: FixedNumerator: the local step in extending a theorem on quartic Gauss sums over primes to a fixed numerator
records.abstract: Theorem 1.1 of C. David, A. Dunn, A. Hamieh and H. Lin (arXiv:2306.11875) bounds the sums of normalized quartic Gauss sums g(c) over primary primes c of Z[i] in a class modulo 4, twisted by (c/|c|)^l. The companion note extends it to g(nu, c) with any fixed numerator nu. The only new ingredient is a local identity that splits off the primes dividing nu from the coprimality conditions of the Type I Dirichlet series. This development formalizes that step from the identities of DDHL Section 3, taken as hypotheses on an abstract symbol and Gauss sum: the splitting identity g(mu, pi^k c') = (-1)^C(c', pi^k) g(mu, pi^k) g(mu pi^(2k), c') with no condition linking mu and pi, and DDHL (3.6). It proves the identity for the truncated series as an exact finite identity (Lemma 2.2), and removes pi from the coprimality condition for every valuation e = ord_pi(mu) (Corollary 2.3): on the series prime to pi the valuation reduces modulo 4; for every e the splitting has the terms k = 4j <= e and k = e + 1; and for the four exact valuations e = 1, 3 it gives single equations with an explicit finite inverse, for e = 0, 2 the coupled pair of DDHL (8.6)-(8.7). It also proves lower bounds for the determinants on Re s >= 1 and the 2-adic facts behind the signs.

records.title: Resolution of Singularities of an Algebraic Variety Over a Field of Characteristic Zero
records.abstract: Heisuke Hironaka's 1964 papers 'Resolution of singularities of an algebraic variety over a field of characteristic zero I,II' were seminal achievements in the history of algebraic geometry. They had inestimable impact on a broad range of research areas in mathematics including geometry, topology, number theory, differential equations, and mathematical physics. The achievement was recognised by a Fields medal awarded to Hironaka in 1970. The papers constitute a veritable tour de force contained in 217 densely-packed pages. The algebraic and combinatorial complexity of the papers is daunting, especially towards the later portions, and have led to a significant level of persistent incomprehension even on the part of domain experts. Because more transparent proofs of the same result appeared in the 1990s, the question of understanding the original papers in detail has become somewhat forgotten. In the associated repository, we have formalised Hironaka's argument in full, modulo results he cites. We have also compiled an erratum, and included complementary arguments for a few portions of the paper that had non-trivial gaps. In a separate publication, we will give some of the narrative background, the interesting story of the mathematical community's tortuous efforts to understand these great works. The size of the formalization has forced us to split this work over three Palomar entries, one for each comparator configuration. The related entries can be found at PALOMAR-2026-11-03-000021 and PALOMAR-2026-11-04-000012 respectively.

records.title: Schatten-class truncated Toeplitz operators
records.abstract: Lean formalization of Schatten-class truncated Toeplitz operator results from the local Lopatto–Rochberg manuscript. Includes analytic and coanalytic Besov classifications for every real p>0, compactness and interpolation criteria, splitting and polynomial-symbol results, and Hilbert–Schmidt energy, differential and squared-kernel quotient descriptions.

records.title: The natural proofs barrier (Razborov and Rudich)
records.abstract: A Lean 4 proof of Theorem 4.1 of A. A. Razborov and S. Rudich, Natural proofs (1997). If a generator G_k from k bits to 2k bits, computed by circuits of polynomial size, has hardness at least 2^(k^ε) for some ε > 0 and infinitely many k, then no P/poly-natural combinatorial property is useful against P/poly. The proof follows the paper. The generator gives Goldreich–Goldwasser–Micali functions of n variables with polynomial-size circuits, which a useful property must reject. The circuit that decides the large constructive subproperty then tells these functions apart from random functions. A hybrid argument over the levels of the tree and over the nodes of a level, with all other nodes fixed, gives a circuit of size 2^O(n) that tells one output of G_k apart from a uniform string with advantage 2^(-O(n)), which contradicts the hardness for n a small power of k.

records.title: A Schur 6-colouring of [1, 538]
records.abstract: A Lean 4 check, with Lean core only, of the existence of a colouring of the integers 1 to 538 with 6 colours and no monochromatic x + y = z, with x = y allowed. So the integers 1 to 538 are the union of six sum-free sets, which gives S(6) ≥ 538 for the Schur number S(6). The largest lower bound in the sources that the author read on 3 November 2026 is S(6) ≥ 537, by Chen, Zhu and Long. The paper paper/schur-six-538.md in this repository states the result.

records.title: Uniform attachment with freezing: local limits and geometric Bienaymé trees
records.abstract: Lean proofs of the local-limit criterion and geometric Bienaymé limit for uniform attachment trees with freezing. The selected conclusions characterize convergence by the divergence of the freezing reciprocal sum, identify the common limit for approximating schedules, and identify the iid-sign limit as a Bienaymé tree with offspring probabilities (1-p)p^k for 0 <= p < 1. The compared carrier is chronological; the full ambient transport is proved in the library outside these selected targets. This entry covers T01–T02 and shares its proof repository with the other result groups.

records.title: Overfullness of critical graphs with small minimum degree (Cao–Chen–Jing–Shan; Chen–Cao)
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Theorem 1.2 of Cao, Chen, Jing and Shan with a weaker constant. overfull_of_critical: if a finite simple graph G is Δ-critical (connected, its line graph is not Δ(G)-colourable, and G − e is Δ(G)-edge-colourable for every edge e) and 3|V(G)| + 7δ(G) ≤ 4Δ(G) + 10, then G is overfull: |E(G)| > Δ(G)·⌊|V(G)|/2⌋. The article assumes 4Δ − 7δ ≥ 3n − 17; the hypothesis here is 4Δ − 7δ ≥ 3n − 10, stronger by 7, because two common-neighbour counts in the article's proof (Case 2 of Section 3 and the fork branch of Case 1) use one more unit of degree than is available and are short by 2 under the article's constant. With the constant −10 every count closes, and the proof needs neither n ≥ 13 nor the Chetwynd–Hilton theorem for Δ ≥ n − 3. One statement. The proof includes the lemmas the article imports: Vizing's adjacency lemma, the multifan lemma, Kierstead paths on four vertices, the fork lemma of Cao and Chen, the short-kite lemma of Cao, Chen and Shan, and the kite lemma (Lemma 2.8, in the form used by Theorem 1.2), with proofs written from scratch where the article only cites them. Version 2 adds two statements. overfull_of_critical_cc: Theorem 1.3 of Chen and Cao (arXiv:2512.07252) with a weaker constant: a Δ-critical graph with 2|V(G)| + 5δ(G) ≤ 3Δ(G) + 6 is overfull (the article assumes 3Δ ≥ 2n + 5δ − 12; the constant −6 comes from counting common neighbours of three vertices without the article's refinements). overfull_of_critical_ccjs: CCJS Theorem 1.2 with its original constant: a Δ-critical graph with 4Δ − 7δ ≥ 3n − 17 and n + δ ≥ 27 is overfull (then 3Δ ≥ 2n + 5δ − 6). Three statements.

records.title: OSreconstruction
records.abstract: A machine-checked proof of the Osterwalder-Schrader correspondence between Euclidean Schwinger functions and relativistic Wightman distributions, in both directions, for every spatial dimension d >= 1. The Euclidean side is a family of Schwinger functions on the zero-diagonal Schwartz space (OS II's test space) satisfying E0-E4; the relativistic side is a family of tempered distributions satisfying the Wightman function axioms (Poincare covariance, spectrum condition, locality, positivity, Hermiticity, clustering). They are linked by a Wick pairing: one holomorphic kernel on the forward tube whose boundary values give the Wightman distribution and whose restriction to Wick- rotated points gives the Schwinger function. Three theorems are verified: E'->R (OS axioms plus linear growth yield Wick-paired Wightman distributions); E'->R' in OS II's form (with growth E0' (4.1), the Wightman distributions exist, satisfy the output bound R0' (4.3), and are unique among Wick-paired families; the two growth conditions are proved equivalent); and R->E (every Wightman family yields, via an explicit constructor, Schwinger functions satisfying E0-E4, with no growth hypothesis). The asymmetry is OS II's correction of OS I and is reproduced faithfully: growth is assumed on the Euclidean side and not recovered, so the two directions do not compose to a biconditional. Scope: theorems about Wightman functions, not the GNS reconstruction of operators. Four conventions are weaker than the textbook ones and are visible in the Challenge: the forward tube carries the extra condition Im z_0 in the open forward cone; locality is stated for adjacent transpositions; reflection positivity goes through a totalized coercion onto zero-diagonal tests; growth is a hypothesis, not a conclusion. To our knowledge this is the first machine-checked proof of the OS reconstruction theorem; its audience is constructive and axiomatic QFT, where it is the bridge every Euclidean construction crosses. The companion formalization of the massive free field and the Proca Wick square inhabits its hypotheses.

records.title: Infinite cycles in the interchange process in five dimensions (Elboim-Sly), formalized in Lean 4
records.abstract: A complete Lean 4 formalization of D. Elboim and A. Sly, Infinite cycles in the interchange process in five dimensions (arXiv:2211.17023v3). In the interchange process on Z^d, each edge carries an independent rate-one Poisson clock and swaps the particles at its endpoints when it rings; run for time beta, it yields a random permutation pi_beta of Z^d. Toth conjectured that pi_beta has infinite cycles for d >= 3 and beta large; Elboim and Sly proved this for d >= 5. The library proves their Theorem 1 (for d >= 5 and beta large, pi_beta almost surely has an infinite cycle), the quantitative bound from its proof (the cycle of the origin is finite with probability less than 2/beta), and the multiscale induction behind both, Theorem 3.2, whose hypotheses (H1)-(H5) control relaxed times, local probabilities, displacement, a Brownian coupling and the proximity of two walks for the cyclic random walk at every scale. The model is constructed on the infinite lattice (Poisson clocks, existence and uniqueness of particle trajectories, bijectivity of pi_s), and nothing the paper cites is assumed: Poisson point processes and their exploration, the zero-one law, continuous-time random walk estimates, Brownian motion and its hitting and escape estimates, Freedman's inequality and the strong approximations are proved from Mathlib. Zaitsev's multidimensional KMT theorem, the paper's one external input, is replaced by two couplings proved in the library: a KMT coupling for Poisson increments and a strong approximation for bounded sign-symmetric vectors; the exponent of the Brownian coupling in (H4) becomes 41/100 instead of 2/5, and Theorem 1 is unchanged. Every statement is checked against a Mathlib-only restatement with leanprover/comparator, and the library uses only Lean's standard axioms.

records.title: Resolution of Singularities of an Algebraic Variety Over a Field of Characteristic Zero
records.abstract: Heisuke Hironaka's 1964 papers 'Resolution of singularities of an algebraic variety over a field of characteristic zero I,II' were seminal achievements in the history of algebraic geometry. They had inestimable impact on a broad range of research areas in mathematics including geometry, topology, number theory, differential equations, and mathematical physics. The achievement was recognised by a Fields medal awarded to Hironaka in 1970. The papers constitute a veritable tour de force contained in 217 densely-packed pages. The algebraic and combinatorial complexity of the papers is daunting, especially towards the later portions, and have led to a significant level of persistent incomprehension even on the part of domain experts. Because more transparent proofs of the same result appeared in the 1990s, the question of understanding the original papers in detail has become somewhat forgotten. In the associated repository, we have formalised Hironaka's argument in full, modulo results he cites. We have also compiled an erratum, and included complementary arguments for a few portions of the paper that had non-trivial gaps. In a separate publication, we will give some of the narrative background, the interesting story of the mathematical community's tortuous efforts to understand these great works. The size of the formalization has forced us to split this work over three Palomar entries, one for each comparator configuration. The related entries can be found at PALOMAR-2026-11-03-000021 and PALOMAR-2026-11-04-000004 respectively.

records.title: Existence of the q-colorability threshold for sparse random graphs
records.abstract: For every integer q at least 3, the formalization proves the existence of a limiting q-colorability threshold for sparse random graphs. A single constant alpha_q in [1/2, log(q)/log(q/(q-1))] gives the transition for the uniform model with floor(c n) edges and the transition at d = 2 alpha_q for the binomial model with edge probability d/n. For every fixed eta in (0,1), there is C > 0 such that, for all sufficiently large n, the first loss of q-colorability under independent uniform additions of unordered pairs of distinct vertices lies within C n (log n)^(-3/2) steps of deterministic integer centers with probability at least 1-eta. The centers divided by n converge to the same alpha_q. Repeated edges are retained in this process. The scope is Theorems 1.1 and 1.2 of the included manuscript.

records.title: Bicolouring Steiner triple systems (Colbourn–Dinitz–Rosa product, Dinitz–Stinson conditions)
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the product theorem of Colbourn, Dinitz and Rosa for bicoloured Steiner triple systems and of the necessary conditions of Dinitz and Stinson. A bicolouring of an STS colours the points so that every block receives exactly two colours. bicolourable3_mul (CDR 1999, Theorem 2.4): if there is an (a, b, c)-bicolourable STS(u) with c = max(a, b, c) and c ≤ a + b, and an (x, y, z)-bicolourable STS(v), then there is an (ax + by + cz, ay + bz + cx, az + bx + cy)-bicolourable STS(uv). Dinitz–Stinson Proposition 1.2: for a bicoloured STS on v points with colour classes of sizes c_k, 3 Σ c_k (c_k − 1) = v (v − 1) (IsSTS.three_mul_sum); no two distinct colour classes have size 2 (not_two_classes_of_size_two); and with three colour classes at most one class size is odd (Bicolourable3.not_two_odd). Four statements. The proof of Theorem 2.4 includes Lemma 2.3 of the article (forbidden latin squares exist when max(a, b, c) ≤ n/2), Ryser's theorem on completing latin arrays, and de Werra's equalized edge colourings of bipartite graphs.

records.title: Odd-ordered Cayley graphs satisfy Erdős–Gyárfás
records.abstract: Every Cayley graph of a finite group of odd order with an inverse-closed, identity-free generating set of size at least three contains a simple cycle of length 2^n for some n ≥ 2. For a noncyclic group of odd order, two such cycles can be chosen as translates meeting at exactly one vertex. A symmetric figure-eight lifts through an abelian normal subgroup of an odd-order group, and a power-of-two cycle lifts through a normal 2-subgroup of a finite group. The cycle conclusion also holds for finite nilpotent groups with a generating set satisfying the same degree condition.

records.title: Plantholt's overfull criterion for graphs of high minimum degree, with 1-factorization theorems for dense regular graphs (6/7 and 11/12)
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Theorem 1.2 of M. Plantholt, Overfull conjecture for graphs with high minimum degree (J. Graph Theory 47, 2004), and of a 1-factorization theorem for dense regular graphs in the style of Chetwynd and Hilton (1989). theorem_1_2: if c ≥ 3/4 is such that every regular graph of even order n and degree at least c n is 1-factorizable, and G has even order n with (3δ − Δ)/2 ≥ c n, then G is Class 1 (χ′ = Δ) if and only if G has no Δ-overfull subgraph. lineGraph_colorable_of_isRegular: a d-regular graph of even order 2n with 11 n ≤ 6 d is d-edge-colourable, i.e. 1-factorizable; this is a weaker form of Chetwynd–Hilton 1989, Theorem 2 (d ≥ ½(√7 − 1)|V|), proved with the same architecture. overfull_criterion: Plantholt's theorem with c = 11/12, i.e. if G has even order n and 11 n ≤ 6 (3δ − Δ), then G is Class 1 if and only if it has no Δ-overfull subgraph. lineGraph_colorable_of_isRegular67: the theorem of Chetwynd and Hilton (Proc. London Math. Soc. 50, 1985) that a d-regular graph of even order 2n with 12 n ≤ 7 d (degree at least 6/7 of the order) is 1-factorizable. overfull_criterion67: Plantholt's theorem with c = 6/7, i.e. even order n and 12 n ≤ 7 (3δ − Δ). Five statements. A Δ-overfull subgraph has an odd number ≥ 3 of vertices and more than Δ ⌊|V(H)|/2⌋ edges; edge colourings are colourings of the line graph.

records.title: Equitable strong (vertex-distinguishing) edge colourings: Rudašová–Soták, Theorem 3.1
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Theorem 3.1 of J. Rudašová and R. Soták, Vertex-distinguishing proper edge colourings of some regular graphs (Discrete Math. 308, 2008). exists_equitable_strong: if a finite simple graph G has a strong (vertex-distinguishing) proper edge colouring with m colours and m ≤ k, then G has an equitable strong proper edge colouring with k colours. One statement. Edge colourings are colourings of the line graph; the palette of a vertex is the set of colours of its edges; strong means distinct vertices have distinct palettes; equitable means the colour classes differ in size by at most one.

records.title: SmallGroups
records.abstract: Lean 4 proofs of four existence theorems: a two-generator, three-relator universal group with infinite cyclic abelianization and a displayed normal generator; an effective two-generator, four-relator family with undecidable triviality and universal nontrivial members; a torsion-free two-generator, four-relator group with undecidable word problem, infinite cyclic abelianization, and a displayed normal generator; and an effective two-generator, five-relator family with undecidable triviality whose members are all torsion-free.

records.title: Anomalous regularization of passive scalars up to the Obukhov–Corrsin exponent
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of S. Armstrong and V. Vicol, "Anomalous regularization of passive scalars up to the Obukhov–Corrsin exponent" (2026, included as doc/paper.pdf). The velocity field b is constructed as in Armstrong and Vicol, "Anomalous diffusion by fractal homogenization": a bounded, Z^2-periodic, divergence-free field on R x T^2, built from shear flows alternating in direction at infinitely many scales, Hölder continuous in space and time with exponent alpha < 1/3, with its scale separation parameter q taken close to 1 depending on s. For the advection-diffusion equation d_t theta + b . grad theta = kappa Laplacian theta on T^2 and every s < (1 - alpha)/2, with b built for that s, it proves: the solutions are bounded at positive times in C^{0,s}(T^2) by C times the L^2 norm of the initial datum, uniformly in kappa in a union of bands accumulating at zero (Theorem A); every solution dissipates a fixed fraction of its variance in unit time, and the variance decays exponentially, with constants independent of kappa in the bands, of the L^2 datum and of the initial time (Theorem B); the local form of Theorem A in space-time tubes that follow the flow of the coarse velocity fields, without boundary conditions (Theorem C); and the compactness of the solutions as kappa tends to zero in the bands, with limits that solve the transport equation and satisfy the bounds of Theorems A and C (Corollary D). It also contains every statement of Part I of the paper.

records.title: Balanced edge colourings: Balister–Kostochka–Li–Schelp 2004, Theorems 1, 6, 10(2) and Corollary 12
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of four results of P. N. Balister, A. V. Kostochka, H. Li and R. H. Schelp, Balanced edge colorings (J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 90, 2004). Edge colourings with k colours are colourings of the line graph with Fin k; the palette of a vertex is the set of colours of its edges; numPal C S counts the vertices with palette S and cost C is the sum of the squares of these counts. theorem1 (Theorem 1): in a k-colouring of least cost, palettes of the same size are used numbers of times differing by at most two. theorem6 (Theorem 6): a proper 3-colouring of the edges (a map Sym2 V → Fin 3 proper at every vertex) can be replaced by a proper 4-colouring in which distinct vertices with the same key see different colour sets, when two distinct vertices with equal key, degree and colour set have degree 3 and no three distinct vertices of degree 3 share a key. theorem10 (Theorem 10, part 2): if 3 ≤ k, Δ(G) ≤ k, n_0, n_1, n_2 ≤ 1, n_3, n_4, n_k ≤ 2, n_{k-1} ≤ k + 1 and n_d ≤ (d-4)/(d-3) · min(2 C(k-3, d-3), C(k, d)) - 2 for 5 ≤ d ≤ k - 2 (n_d the number of vertices of degree d), then G has a strong (vertex-distinguishing) edge colouring with k + 1 colours. corollary12 (Corollary 12): if Δ(G) ≥ √(2n) + 4 (n vertices), δ(G) ≥ 5 and k is least with n_d ≤ C(k, d) for all d, then G has a strong edge colouring with k + 1 colours and every strong edge colouring uses at least k colours. Four statements.

records.title: Baranyai's theorem
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Baranyai's theorem: if k divides n, the k-subsets of an n-set can be partitioned into (n−1 choose k−1) parallel classes, each a partition of the set into n/k blocks of size k (a 1-factorization of the complete k-uniform hypergraph); and of Baranyai's rounding lemma: every real matrix can be rounded entrywise to floors or ceilings so that all row sums, column sums and the total are also rounded. The proof includes the integral max-flow theorem for integer capacities. Mathlib has neither result.

records.title: Finite-order exponential mixing does not imply the central limit theorem
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of Theorems A, B, and C of the paper. It constructs stationary processes with finite-order exponential mixing and no Gaussian subsequential limit, then realizes the phenomenon in analytic and smooth dynamical systems.

records.title: The settling sum of the plastic number: sum_{n >= 1} ||rho^n||^2 = rho. The squared distances from the powers of the plastic number to the nearest integers sum to the plastic number itself; the even-power trace of its two hidden conjugates is rho; with the general cubic complex-pair form
records.abstract: Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, of six statements. Write ||x|| = |x - round x| for the distance from a real number to the nearest integer, and let rho be the plastic number, the real root of x^3 = x + 1 and the smallest Pisot number (Siegel 1944). Convergence of sum_{n >= 1} ||theta^n||^2 for a Pisot number theta is elementary, and Pisot (1938) proved the converse; neither gives the value. (1) For every real rho with rho^3 = rho + 1, sum_{n >= 1} ||rho^n||^2 = rho (as a HasSum). (2) The tsum form of (1). (3) For every complex alpha != rho with alpha^3 = alpha + 1 (one of the two conjugates inside the unit disc), sum_{n >= 0} (alpha^(2n) + conj(alpha)^(2n)) = rho: the even-power trace of the hidden pair is the generator, the mechanism behind (1), because x^3 - x - 1 = (x - 1) x (x + 1) - 1 makes the resolvent trace sum_{roots} 1/(1 - r^2) vanish. (4) For a real theta, a complex alpha with ||alpha|| < 1, and integers a, b, c that are the elementary symmetric functions of (theta, alpha, conj alpha): sum_{n >= 1} (S_n - theta^n)^2 = Re(geo alpha), where S_n are the Newton power sums of x^3 - a x^2 + b x - c and geo alpha = alpha^2/(1 - alpha^2) + conj(alpha)^2/(1 - conj(alpha)^2) + 2 alpha conj(alpha)/(1 - alpha conj(alpha)). (5) Under the same hypotheses, for every N with ||alpha||^N < 1/4, sum_{n >= 1} ||theta^n||^2 = Re(geo alpha) + sum_{n = 1}^{N} (||theta^n||^2 - (S_n - theta^n)^2): Pisot's convergence in quantitative form for the cubic complex-pair case; (1) is the case a = 0, b = -1, c = 1, N = 10 (the smallest N with rho^(-N/2) < 1/4; the n = 10 correction term is zero), with Re(geo alpha) = 2 rho^2 + 3 rho - 2 and correction 2 - 2 rho - 2 rho^2. (6) x^3 = x + 1 has exactly one real solution. Statements 4-5 assume neither theta > 1 nor irreducibility. Pisot's theorem itself is not formalized. Not compared, proved in the repository's library only: the threshold from which the Perrin numbers are the nearest integers to rho^n (n >= 10, sharp at n = 9), a claim previously stated without proof at OEIS A001608 (R. Stephan, 2002); it was a compared statement in the withdrawn submissions of 2026-11-03/04 and was removed from the compared set on 2026-11-05 so that every compared result is one first presented here. Application to time (no compared statement asserts it): in the arithmetic of time the tick is multiplication by rho on Q(rho) and the record is the integer lattice; statement 1 says the total squared distance by which the tick history falls short of its record is exactly one tick's unit, rho, and statement 3 says that unit is returned by the two conjugates that are not seen; the quartic companion Q, Q^4 = Q + 1, is not Pisot, so by Pisot's theorem its series diverges (not proved here). That physical time is this arithmetic is the identification stated in the companion entry PALOMAR-2026-08-19-000006 (the arithmetic of time), as an identification; the theorems here are its arithmetic content. That entry's README Scope section is reproduced verbatim in this entry's README.

records.title: The Strong Perfect Graph Theorem
records.abstract: A Lean 4 proof of the Strong Perfect Graph Theorem of Chudnovsky, Robertson, Seymour and Thomas: a finite graph is perfect if and only if it is Berge. A graph is perfect if every induced subgraph has chromatic number equal to its clique number. It is Berge if neither the graph nor its complement contains an induced cycle of odd length at least five. The proof follows the paper of Chudnovsky, Robertson, Seymour and Thomas (Annals of Mathematics, 2006). It formalizes the decomposition theorem for Berge graphs (Theorem 1.3 of the paper) through the numbered results of Sections 2 to 24. It also proves the earlier results that the paper cites, among them Lovász's weak perfect graph theorem, the results of Cornuéjols and Cunningham on 2-joins, of Chvátal and Sbihi on homogeneous pairs, of Chvátal on star cutsets, and of Roussel and Rubio. The statement in Challenge.lean uses only Mathlib's definitions of induced subgraphs, chromatic number, clique number, cycle graphs and induced containment.

records.title: Maximum-modulus points of entire functions (Erdős Problem 1117), in Lean 4
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of both maximum-modulus counting questions of Hayman–Lingham Problem 2.16 (Erdős Problem 1117). For an entire function f and a radius r, let ν(f, r) be the number of points on the circle |z| = r where |f| attains its maximum on that circle. The registered theorem proves two things: some non-monomial entire function has ν(f, r) unbounded along radii tending to infinity; and for every non-monomial entire function there is one finite bound B with ν(f, r) ≤ B along a cofinal set of radii, so the counts never tend to infinity. The first part follows Pardo-Simón and Sixsmith's finite-order construction and proves the approximation step of Rempe-Gillen that it uses; the second follows Li's cofinal-bound argument. The theorem depends only on the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.title: The Dixmier conjecture implies the Jacobian conjecture, and is false in dimension 3 and above
records.abstract: A machine-checked proof that, over a field of characteristic zero, the Dixmier conjecture in dimension n implies the Jacobian conjecture in dimension n (Bass, Connell and Wright, 1982), and so, with an explicit counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture padded to every dimension n >= 3 and proved here, that the Dixmier conjecture is false in every dimension n >= 3. The four statements and their definitions are Formal Conjectures' (DixmierConjecture.lean, arXiv math/0608009), copied verbatim into Challenge.lean, so this entry proves Formal Conjectures' own statements. The proof builds the polynomial representation of the Weyl algebra, shows it faithful in characteristic zero, and uses the classical Weyl-algebra lift described by Bass, Connell and Wright (1982, p. 297), who credit Vaserstein and Kac.

records.title: Representation embeddings and the third Brauer–Thrall conjecture
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization, built on Mathlib, of the principal results of the paper Representation embeddings and the third Brauer–Thrall conjecture. Over an algebraically closed field, every representation-infinite finite-dimensional algebra admits a faithful representation embedding of a colimit-closed category of Kronecker modules that preserves infinite dimensions (Theorem A). Hence, for every infinite cardinal κ, it has 2^κ pairwise non-isomorphic indecomposable modules of dimension κ whose endomorphism rings are local with residue field k and whose radicals satisfy (rad End M)^n = 0 for one n ≤ max(30, 4 dim A) independent of κ; for κ ≥ |k| this is the largest possible number (Corollary 1.1, in full). Weaker parts of the corollary are also compared: modules of every infinite dimension, the endomorphism control without the count and the bound, and the count without the bound. The cited inputs are proved in the library: Bongartz's Theorem 6 and Göbel and Simson's rigid families over infinite fields.

records.title: Generic Degree Three in JC(3): Collision Geometry and Galois Group S3
records.abstract: Motivated by Alpöge's generic-degree-three counterexample to JC(3), we formalize the collision geometry of complex three-dimensional Keller maps of that degree. Using classical Keller–Galois rigidity, we identify the residual generic collision factor with the normal closure of the induced function-field extension, whose Galois group is S3. The decomposition separates the diagonal and proves nonvanishing of the collision obstruction.

records.title: Triangle decompositions of typical graphs of fixed density (Keevash, Counting designs, Theorem 2.1, weaker form)
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of a weaker, fixed-density form of Theorem 2.1 of P. Keevash, Counting designs (J. Eur. Math. Soc. 20, 2018). density G is |E(G)| / C(n, 2); IsTypical G c h says that every nonempty set S of at most h vertices has (1 ± |S| c) d(G)^|S| n common neighbours; Tridivisible G says that every degree is even and 3 divides |E(G)|; IsTriangleDecomposition G D says that D is a family of triangles of G and every edge lies in exactly one of them. typical_triangle_decomposition: there is h such that for every d0 > 0 there are c0 > 0 and n0 such that every (c0, h)-typical tridivisible graph on n ≥ n0 vertices with density at least d0 has a triangle decomposition. This is weaker than the article in two ways: the density is bounded below by a fixed constant (the article allows d(G) > n^(-10^-7) with c < c0 d(G)^(10^6)), and the typicality is (c, h)-typicality for an absolute, not explicit, h (the article assumes c-typicality, which concerns only degrees and pairs). One statement.

records.title: Spectral Geometry — exact multiplicity of a compact crossing on an infinite octagonal graph
records.abstract: On the real square-summable states of the infinite centered octagonal cut-and-project vertex graph, take the graph Laplacian with edge weight 1/16, onsite potential V(x)=1+|p(x)|² and natural domain D(V). Add t times the coordinate projection onto the eight neighbors of the origin. At t*=17/16+√2 the two alternating ring modes meet at E*=13/4+√2. The full eigenspace at E* has real dimension exactly two. Every solution of the eigenvector equation is its amplitude at the lift (1,0,0,0) times the first compact state plus its amplitude at (1,1,0,0) times the second. No support restriction is assumed. Locality, symmetry and a strictly positive exterior energy force the exterior part to vanish; the complete central kernel supplies the two ring patterns.

records.title: The Johnson bound for the independence number of the Johnson graph
records.abstract: The Johnson graph J(n, k) has the k-subsets of an n-set as vertices, two of them adjacent when they share k - 1 elements; an independent set is a constant-weight binary code of length n, weight k and minimum distance 4. This Lean 4 formalization proves Johnson's 1962 bound α(J(n, k)) ≤ johnsonBound n 4 k, where johnsonBound is the recursive bound A(n, d, w) ≤ ⌊n/w · A(n - 1, d, w - 1)⌋, as stated in google-deepmind/formal-conjectures (Erdős Problem 835), where it is a solved statement left without proof. The proof is by recursion on (n, k): double counting the pairs (point, member) and shortening the members through a point. No new mathematics is claimed.

records.title: Reasonable bounds for restricted polynomial progressions in F_p^n
records.abstract: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Theorem 1.1 of Burgin, Fragkos, Kruzel, Lacey and Stokolosa (arXiv:2610.12831). For k ≥ 2 there are M_k ≤ exp(7 k log k) and P_k ≤ exp exp(25 k² log k), and an absolute constant C₁, such that for every prime p ≥ P_k there are C, c > 0 with the following property. Every A ⊆ F_p^n with n > exp^{(K)}(1) and density at least C / (log^{(K)} n)^c, where K = k^{C₁ k}, contains a restricted polynomial progression x, x + P_1(y), …, x + P_{k-1}(y), with P_j(y) = (y_1^j, …, y_n^j) and y ∈ {0, 2, 3, …, M_k}^n \ {0}. Moreover, the k points of any such progression are pairwise distinct. The formalization also proves the two theorems that the paper cites from the literature and does not prove. The first is the inverse theorem of Bhangale, Khot, Liu and Minzer for noise stability under distributions with no abelian embedding (Theorem 1.4 of the paper, which is Theorem 1 of their "On approximability of satisfiable k-CSPs: VII"), in full generality. The second is Dimitrov's theorem on the Schinzel–Zassenhaus conjecture (Theorem 5.11 of the paper). Only Lean's standard axioms are used.

records.title: Gale's feasibility theorem, the Gale–Ryser theorem and Hoffman's circulation theorem
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of D. Gale, A theorem on flows in networks (Pacific J. Math. 7, 1957) and of Hoffman's circulation theorem (A. J. Hoffman, 1960, in the form of A. Schrijver, A Course in Combinatorial Optimization, Theorems 4.6 and 4.7). A network is a finite node type N with capacities c : N → N → ℝ, c ≥ 0 (finite capacities only); a flow is f : N → N → ℝ with f x y + f y x = 0 and f ≤ c; a demand d : N → ℝ is feasible if some flow has net inflow ∑_y f y x ≥ d x at every node. feasibility: d is feasible if and only if d(Sᶜ) ≤ c(S, Sᶜ) for every S ⊆ N (Gale's Feasibility Theorem). feasibility_int: the same for integer c and d with an integer flow (Gale's remark). feasibility_second: Gale's second formulation (for every set Y of nodes of positive demand, some flow meets the demand at all nodes of nonpositive demand and the aggregate demand of Y). gale_ryser_unsorted, gale_ryser: for a : Fin m → ℕ and b : Fin n → ℕ, a 0-1 matrix with row sums at most a i and column sums b j exists if and only if ∑_{j∈Y} b j ≤ ∑_i min(a i, |Y|) for all column sets Y, equivalently, for b nonincreasing, ∑_{j<k} b j ≤ ∑_{j<k} #{i | j < a i} for all k ≤ n (Gale's Problem I, §3). gale_ryser_exact: if moreover ∑ a = ∑ b, the row sums can be made exactly a (the Gale–Ryser theorem). hoffman, hoffman_int: on a finite directed multigraph (arc type A, tail and head maps src, tgt : A → V) with bounds d ≤ c on the arcs (real, respectively integer), there is a circulation f (real, respectively integer) with d ≤ f ≤ c if and only if d(δ^in(U)) ≤ c(δ^out(U)) for every U ⊆ V. Eight statements; no definitions beyond Mathlib's.

records.title: Finite nonlinear MkCS exact penalty thresholds
records.abstract: An adapted finite nonlinear QUBO formalization for the maximum k-colorable vertex-subset problem: binary-domain attainment, ordered color-pair normalization, weak optimal-value equality with auxiliary repair, strict optimizer feasibility, the one-color exception and attained boundary ties.

records.title: The Lennon–Pittel conjecture on random stable matchings
records.abstract: We prove the Lennon–Pittel conjecture for balanced stable marriage with independent, uniform strict preferences. Let S_n count the stable complete matchings between two sides of size n. For every positive nonincreasing sequence epsilon_n tending to zero, the probability that S_n is at least epsilon_n times its expectation tends to one. This gives a lower-tail estimate at the scale of Pittel's first-moment asymptotic. An accompanying working paper is in preparation.

records.title: The Colbourn–Dinitz–Rosa conjecture and the exact block-type spectrum
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of two results on strictly 3-bicolored Steiner triple systems. For every positive triple of class sizes a,b,c, existence is equivalent to n=a+b+c being 1 or 3 modulo 6, the identity a²+b²+c²-ab-ac-bc=n, and the exclusion of two classes of size 2. For every sufficiently large admissible profile, the number of AAC blocks is characterized exactly by two explicit arithmetic tests. The first result settles the class-size conjecture posed by Colbourn, Dinitz and Rosa in 1999; the second applies the typed absorption theorems of Triangle decompositions III. Both statements are compared in one shared development.

records.title: Bigon-free dichotomy for combinatorial pseudoline arrangements
records.abstract: A combinatorial arrangement of pseudolines in the real projective plane, given as a generalised map with flags labelled by lines, in which no line carries fewer than three vertices, is four lines in general position or contains five lines in general position, a pencil of three and a pencil of two in which none of these five lines joins the two centres, or the complete quadrangle.

records.title: Sparse kernels and necessary sampling for binary Walsh matrices
records.abstract: Finite quantitative sparse-kernel and necessary expected-row bounds for independently subsampled binary Walsh matrices, with uniform asymptotic and recovery/RIP consequences.

records.title: A tight bound for Green's arithmetic triangle removal lemma in vector spaces
records.abstract: Lean 4 formalisation of the main results of Jacob Fox and László Miklós Lovász, A tight bound for Green's arithmetic triangle removal lemma in vector spaces (arXiv:1606.01230): the arithmetic triangle removal lemma in F_p^n with a polynomial bound (Theorem 1), the Kleinberg–Sawin–Speyer bound on multicolored sum-free families (Theorem 2), the count of triangles spanned by vertex-disjoint triangles (Theorem 3), and the tightness of the exponent in Theorem 1 (the second part of Theorem 1).

records.title: Bounded finite conic-union hulls
records.abstract: The boxed finite conic-union continuous hull and compact lift. Finite bounds, explicit dependent residual dimensions and cone hypotheses are retained. Empty branches/index sets are allowed; this is not a general whole-GDP ideality theorem.

records.title: Duke–Schulze-Pillot: the upper bound of Lemma 5(ii) and a conditional Theorem 3(ii)
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization around W. Duke and R. Schulze-Pillot, Representation of integers by positive ternary quadratic forms and equidistribution of lattice points on ellipsoids (Invent. Math. 99, 1990). q(x) = ½ xᵗAx for a symmetric integer 3 × 3 matrix A with q > 0 on ℚ³ \ {0}, h ∈ ℚ³, r(q, h, n) = #{x ∈ h + ℤ³ : q(x) = n} and, for F ⊆ ℝ³, r(q, F, h, n) = #{x ∈ h + ℤ³ : q(x) = n, x/√n ∈ F}. Unconditional results: card_divisors_le_rpow (d(n) ≤ C_ε n^ε); repCount_le (r(q, h, n) ≤ C_ε n^{1/2+ε} for n ≥ 1); average_le (the same bound for every nonnegatively weighted average of such counts, which includes r(spn_N q, h, n): this is the upper half of Lemma 5(ii)). Conditional results: thm3_ii (Theorem 3(ii), r(q, F, h, n) = R(n) μ(F) + O(n^{1/2 − 1/175 + ε}) for n ≥ 1 in a set S) and spn_upper (R(n) ≤ C_ε n^{1/2+ε}) are proved under two hypotheses that are NOT proved here: hThm1, the estimate of Theorem 1 of the paper (|r(q, F, h, n) − r(q, h, n) μ(F)| ≤ C (n^{−1/175} r(q, h, n) + n^{1/2−1/175+ε}) on S), and hThm3i, the estimate of Theorem 3(i) (|r(q, h, n) − R(n)| ≤ C n^{1/2−1/28+ε} on S); R stands for r(spn_N q, h, n), μF ∈ [0, 1] for μ(F), and S for the restricted set of n. The lower bound n^{1/2−ε} ≪ r(spn_N q, h, n) of Lemma 5(ii) (Siegel's ineffective bound) is not formalized.

records.title: Finite optimal-polish discovery for center-cut histories
records.abstract: A qualified actual-trial history theorem for convex MINLP, with full source definitions, pre-discovery exactness and fixed-fiber NLP polishing.

records.title: Thomassen: exponentially many 5-list-colourings of planar graphs
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of C. Thomassen, Exponentially many 5-list-colorings of planar graphs (J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 97, 2007): a finite planar graph with n vertices, every vertex of which has a list of at least five colours, has at least 2^{n/9} distinct list colourings (two_rpow_card_div_nine_le_ncard_listColourings: (2 : ℝ) ^ (n / 9) ≤ the number of maps f : V → C with f v ∈ L v and f u ≠ f v on every edge). Planarity is combinatorial: a plane map is a rotation system whose hypermap with the dart reversal has Euler defect 0 (definitions copied verbatim from the registered entry thomassen-girth-five, PALOMAR-2026-10-28-000023, so that the Challenge depends on Mathlib only). The proof follows the paper: Theorems 1–4, Claims 8–13 and the lemmas on generalized wheels they use are proved for an abstract interface of near-triangulations, which is realised by plane near-triangulations using the separation theorems of the dependency; every planar graph is a spanning subgraph of a plane near-triangulation. One statement; the definitions of the Challenge are compared with those of the Solution.

records.title: Critical trees are neither too short nor too fat
records.abstract: Lean 4 proofs of the main results of Addario-Berry, Donderwinkel and Kortchemski, "Critical trees are neither too short nor too fat" (arXiv:2311.06163). For every critical offspring law, the height of the size-conditioned Bienaymé tree divided by log n tends to infinity and its width divided by n tends to zero in probability, along admissible sizes. These bounds are sharp: for every function f tending to infinity, a single critical offspring law has limsup P(height < f(n) log n) = 1 and limsup P(width > n/f(n)) = 1. For critical offspring laws in the local domain of attraction of the asymmetric Cauchy law (mu_n = L(n)/n^2 with L slowly varying), the height divided by an explicit scale h_n and the width divided by n E[Y 1{Y >= a_n}] both converge to 1 in probability, and height times width is O_P(n log n). The entry also includes the stochastic ordering of heights of uniform labelled trees with given degree sequences (Addario-Berry and Donderwinkel, Theorem 9), used in the paper. All 23 named results of the paper (its theorem, proposition, lemma and corollary environments) are proved in the repository; this Palomar entry compares the headline results.

records.title: The three squares theorem (Gauss–Legendre)
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of the three squares theorem of Legendre (1798) and Gauss (1801): a natural number is a sum of three squares if and only if it is not of the form 4^a (8 b + 7) (sum_three_sq_iff), with the corollary that every n ≡ 3 (mod 8) is x₀² + x₁² + x₂² for some x : Fin 3 → ℤ (exists_sum_sq_of_mod_eight_eq_three). The proof uses ternary quadratic forms of determinant one: a positive definite integral ternary form of determinant one is equivalent to x² + y² + z² (proved with Minkowski's convex body theorem), and for n ≢ 0 (mod 4), n ≢ 7 (mod 8) such a form with diagonal entry n is built from a prime in an arithmetic progression (Dirichlet's theorem, as in Mathlib) and quadratic reciprocity for the Jacobi symbol. Two statements; no definitions beyond Mathlib's.

records.title: Finite sequence routing formulations and continuous timing
records.abstract: A qualified finite sequence-routing formalization connecting the complete source binary rows with padded elementary customer routes and exact transition cost. For fixed valid slots, explicit zero-depot clock/travel conditions give continuous timing feasibility through the earliest-schedule recurrence and an attained minimum total return over timing assignments. Capacity and global route optimization are outside scope.

records.title: The Banach-Mazur rotation problem in finite dimensions: a transitive isometry group forces a Euclidean norm
records.abstract: A machine-checked proof that a finite-dimensional real normed space whose linear isometries act transitively on the unit sphere is Euclidean. This is the finite-dimensional case of the Mazur rotations problem, which appeared in Banach's 1932 book and is surveyed by Cabello Sanchez, Ferenczi and Randrianantoanina; its audience is the geometry of Banach spaces and their symmetries. It is the statement banach_mazur_rotation_problem.finite_dimensional of Formal Conjectures (BanachMazurRotation.lean), which marks it research solved. The result is classical and no priority is claimed. The proof takes the classical route: the isometries form a compact group, averaging a squared Euclidean norm over Haar measure gives an invariant quadratic form, and transitivity makes it a multiple of the squared norm. Mathlib has no topology on the isometry group, so the entry also builds it as a compact topological group with Haar measure. The general problem for separable Banach spaces, which Formal Conjectures marks research open, is not addressed.

records.title: Classification of globally periodic rational difference equations
records.abstract: A complete classification of the globally periodic rational difference equations x_{n+K} = (A_0 + A_1 x_n + ... + A_K x_{n+K-1}) / (B_0 + B_1 x_n + ... + B_K x_{n+K-1}) with nonnegative coefficients, acting on positive initial data, answering Problem 11 of Gasull's survey of open problems in low-dimensional dynamical systems. Such an equation is globally periodic (every positive solution satisfies x_{n+p} = x_n for a common p >= 1) if and only if, up to rescaling x_n -> alpha x_n and unfolding (multiplying every index by an integer), it is one of the five known examples: x_{n+1} = x_n, x_{n+1} = 1/x_n, x_{n+2} = x_{n+1}/x_n, the Lyness equation x_{n+2} = (1 + x_{n+1})/x_n, and Todd's period-8 equation x_{n+3} = (1 + x_{n+1} + x_{n+2})/x_n. The result holds at every order K. Previously the question had been settled for K in {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11} (Cima, Gasull and Mañosas 2004) and for some special families, but the general case was open.

records.title: Pálvölgyi's cyclic heptagon is not Euclidean Ramsey, so Graham's spherical-set conjecture (formal-conjectures erdos_174.variants.graham) is false; and generic seven points on a circle are not Ramsey (Theorem A.3 of arXiv:2609.23327)
records.abstract: For every transcendental r > 2, the seven points (0, 0) and (j, ±√(j(2r − j))), j ∈ {1, 3, 4}, lie on the circle of centre (r, 0) and radius r and are not Euclidean Ramsey (Pálvölgyi, A cyclic non-Ramsey heptagon, arXiv:2609.23327, Theorem 1); consequently not every finite cospherical subset of a Euclidean space is Ramsey. The second statement is the negation of the conjecture that every finite spherical set is Ramsey (posed by Erdős, Graham, Montgomery, Rothschild, Spencer and Straus in 1973), in exactly the form in which google-deepmind/formal-conjectures states it as erdos_174.variants.graham (formal-conjectures PR #7706, which re-tags that statement as solved and links this proof). Ramsey is formal-conjectures' definition, Erdos174.IsRamsey, copied byte for byte: a finite set A in R^n such that for every number k ≥ 1 of colours there is a dimension d for which every k-colouring of R^d has a monochromatic distance-preserving copy of A. All four compared statements use only Mathlib and that definition. The conjecture was refuted in September 2026 by Pálvölgyi's paper (whose proofs it attributes to ChatGPT) and by OpenAI's classification of finite Euclidean Ramsey configurations, whose Lean proof (openai/math) already exhibits non-Ramsey twelve- and nine-point sets on a circle in OpenAI's own vocabulary. The proof here is Pálvölgyi's derivation-energy argument run against OpenAI's tensor criterion: a derivation D of R with D r = 1, the pairing x ⊗ y ↦ D x · D y on OpenAI's coefficient tensor ring, the weights 2, −2, −2, 2, 2, −1, −1 and the energy −24/((2r − 1)(2r − 3)(2r − 4)) ≠ 0 show that the heptagon fails OpenAI's field criterion, and the necessity half of OpenAI's classification (proved in their Lean) turns that into not Ramsey; formal-conjectures' IsRamsey, which also allows the dimension d = 0, is then reduced to OpenAI's Ramsey. The witness for the second statement is the heptagon at r = 2 + OpenAI's Liouville-type parameter, which is transcendental. Also proved, with the same definition: Theorem A.3 of the paper's appendix as printed, without its measure clause (for distinct t1, t2, t3 and t4, ..., t7 algebraically independent over Q(t1, t2, t3), the seven points ((1 − ti²)/(1 + ti²), 2ti/(1 + ti²)) are not Ramsey; the appendix is labelled by its author as written by ChatGPT and unchecked), and its corollary for seven parameters algebraically independent over Q, in the shape of OpenAI's nine-point theorem (distinct points on the unit circle, not Ramsey). Its proof follows the appendix: Lemma A.1 in its symmetric form, a derivation vanishing on Q(t1, t2, t3) with prescribed values on t4, ..., t7, weighted moments by Lagrange interpolation, and again the necessity half of OpenAI's classification. The 16 OpenAI Lean files the proofs import are included, ported to the Lean module system by header-only changes. All proofs depend on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only.

records.title: Four squares in caps, and Jacobi's four-square theorem for odd N
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of two results on sums of four squares. (1) Jacobi's four-square theorem for odd N: the number of x : Fin 4 → ℤ with x₀² + x₁² + x₂² + x₃² = N equals 8 ∑_{d ∣ N} d (jacobi_four_squares_odd), following the proof of Andrews, Ekhad and Zeilberger (1993): two finite q-series identities proved by WZ telescoping, combined into a finite identity that is read modulo X^{N+1} in ℚ⟦X⟧. (2) Four squares in caps (four_squares_in_caps): for every unit vector q ∈ ℝ⁴ and every δ > 0 there is M₀ such that every odd m ≥ M₀ is β₀² + β₁² + β₂² + β₃² with β : Fin 4 → ℤ and |βᵢ − √m qᵢ| ≤ δ √m for all i, i.e. the integer points of the sphere of radius √m meet every cap of fixed angular radius. The proof uses the Duke–Friedlander–Iwaniec delta method (in Heath-Brown's form) with Gaussian weights: an exact formula through the theta transformation, Fourier bounds for the cut-off weight, and the Weil bound for Kloosterman sums, imported from the Weil Bounds Toolkit (PALOMAR-2026-11-03-000018) as a lake dependency. The main term is not evaluated: it depends on the center of the cap only through its norm, so comparing caps with a grid of centers reduces the theorem to the lower bound r₄(m) ≥ 8m for odd m, which (1) provides. All constants are effective but not explicit in the statement (M₀ is existential). Two statements; no definitions beyond Mathlib's.

records.title: Central limit theorem for the complex eigenvalues of Gaussian random matrices
records.abstract: This project formalizes the main central limit theorem of “Central limit theorem for the complex eigenvalues of Gaussian random matrices” by Advay Goel, Patrick Lopatto, and Xiaoyu Xie (arXiv:2306.10243v2), using an expanded local manuscript as the detailed proof source. The local manuscript was prepared to ease autoformalization by adding details to the proofs. Its main theorem (Theorem 1.3) is identical to the main theorem of the arXiv version: the hypotheses and conclusion are unchanged. Only this main theorem is advertised.

records.title: Overfull criteria for edge colouring (Plantholt; Chen–Cao; Cao–Chen–Jing–Shan), unified
records.abstract: A thin wrapper that restates, in one vocabulary and with Mathlib definitions only, the overfull criteria proved in PALOMAR-2026-11-04-000016 and PALOMAR-2026-11-04-000009. class_two_iff_overfull_subgraph: a finite simple graph of even order n with 12 n ≤ 7 (3δ − Δ) is of class two (its line graph is not Δ-colourable) iff it has a Δ-overfull subgraph (odd order at least 3, more than Δ (|V(H)| − 1)/2 edges); this is Plantholt's criterion with Chetwynd–Hilton's 6/7. critical_overfull: a Δ-critical graph (connected, class two, every edge-deleted subgraph Δ-colourable) with 2n + 5δ ≤ 3Δ + 6 (Chen–Cao), or 3n + 7δ ≤ 4Δ + 10 (Cao–Chen–Jing–Shan, variant), or 3n + 7δ ≤ 4Δ + 17 and n + δ ≥ 27 (Cao–Chen–Jing–Shan) has odd order, is overfull (|E| > Δ ⌊n/2⌋), and so is a Δ-overfull subgraph of itself. The only new proof is the elementary step from overfullness to odd order at least 3 (degree sum) and the conversion to the subgraph form. Two statements; no definitions beyond Mathlib's.

records.title: A local T(b) theorem for perfect multilinear Calderón–Zygmund operators (Mirek–Thiele), formalized in Lean 4
records.abstract: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the three main theorems of M. Mirek and C. Thiele, "A local T(b) theorem for perfect multilinear Calderón–Zygmund operators", Proc. London Math. Soc. 114 (2017): the perfect multilinear local T(1) theorem (Theorem 1.3), the perfect multilinear local T(b) theorem with general testing functions on admissible collections of paths (Theorem 1.4), and the perfect multilinear global T(b) theorem (Theorem 1.11), for n-linear forms on dyadic test functions in R^d satisfying the dyadic decay, perfect smoothness and qualitative truncation conditions. The development follows the paper's proof of Theorem 1.4 (stopping times, pruning, the telescoping identities, the discrete Carleson embedding and the outer-measure Hölder inequalities of Do–Thiele, the contraction step and its iteration) and the global/local reduction of Theorem 1.11, including the atom estimate for the dyadic Hardy norm for all exponents (Burkholder's L^p bound for the dyadic square function by Marcinkiewicz interpolation). Theorem 1.3, cited as folklore in the paper, is proved by a dyadic paraproduct argument with a dyadic John–Nirenberg inequality for the paraproduct symbols. All constants depend only on the dimension, the linearity, the testing constant and the exponents.

records.title: Finite integer penalties and literal routing QUBO transport
records.abstract: A complete source-based finite penalty/energy family: the generic full ordered QUBO identity and strict integer-row minimizer equivalence, consistent fixed-coordinate energy/minimizer transport, and the literal incidence, time-indexed arc and sequence applications. The statements retain actual rows, repeated costs, full offsets, source free/fixed partitions, feasibility conditions, strict sufficient thresholds and finite source energy attainment. Capacity, physical route completeness and solver/quantum performance are outside scope.

records.title: Walecki's decompositions of complete graphs into Hamiltonian cycles and paths
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of Walecki's theorem: for every m, the complete graph on 2m + 1 vertices is the edge-disjoint union of m Hamiltonian cycles (hamiltonian_cycles_odd), and the complete graph on 2m vertices is the edge-disjoint union of m Hamiltonian paths (hamiltonian_paths_even). Both are stated for an arbitrary finite vertex type of the given cardinality, with Mathlib's Walk.IsHamiltonianCycle and Walk.IsHamiltonian, pairwise disjoint edge lists, and every edge of the complete graph on some cycle (path). The proof is Walecki's zig-zag construction: on ZMod (2m) the paths i, i+1, i−1, i+2, i−2, …, i+m (0 ≤ i < m) are Hamiltonian; an edge {x, y} of the i-th path has x + y ∈ {2i, 2i+1}, which makes the paths edge-disjoint, and m (2m − 1) = C(2m, 2) shows that they cover all edges; closing each path through a new vertex gives the cycles. Two statements; no definitions beyond Mathlib's.

records.title: The König constant is one
records.abstract: Verification that the König constant is one, as shown in the source.

records.title: Fournier's theorem: graphs whose maximum-degree vertices induce a forest are of class one
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of Fournier's theorem (1973): if the vertices of maximum degree of a finite simple graph G induce a forest, then G has a proper edge colouring with Δ(G) colours (fournier: G.lineGraph.Colorable G.maxDegree under (G.induce {v | G.degree v = G.maxDegree}).IsAcyclic). The proof takes an edge-minimal subgraph H of G that is not Δ(G)-edge-colourable; Vizing's theorem gives Δ(H) = Δ(G), and Vizing's adjacency lemma applied to every edge xy of H gives a neighbour of x of maximum degree other than y, so the maximum-degree vertices of H span a subgraph of minimum degree at least 2 inside the forest, which is impossible (the end of a longest path). Vizing's theorem and the adjacency lemma are imported as lake dependencies from PALOMAR-2026-10-15-000004 and PALOMAR-2026-11-04-000009. One statement; no definitions beyond Mathlib's.

records.title: Three-point ordered convolution-square classification
records.abstract: For three-element finite supports S and T in any abelian group, equality of all labelled coefficients of their ordered additive convolution squares is equivalent to a translation by an element annihilated by doubling, or to the explicit exceptional paired shape in the statement. Diagonal pairs are included. The full proof development is contained in this snapshot. This is an adaptation of an existing public Couret formalization; mathematical novelty and independent human review are not established.

records.title: The Minimum Number of Coprime Adjacencies in a Permutation
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the exact minimum number of coprime adjacent pairs over all permutations of the first n positive integers, valid unconditionally for every n at least four. The proof constructs optimal paths in the graph joining noncoprime integers.

records.title: The Anning-Erdős theorem: an infinite set of points in the plane with integer distances lies on a line
records.abstract: A machine-checked proof that an infinite set of points in the Euclidean plane whose pairwise distances are all integers is contained in a line (Anning and Erdős, 1945). Formal Conjectures states it next to the Erdős-Ulam problem on dense rational-distance sets, which is open; its audience is distance problems in discrete geometry. It is the statement erdos_ulam_problem.variants.anning_erdos of Formal Conjectures (ErdosUlamProblem.lean), which marks it research solved. The result is classical and no priority is claimed.
