The proof follows Erdős's short argument: for three points A, B, C not on a line, the differences |PA| - |PB| and |PA| - |PC| take finitely many values, and in place of the bound on how often two hyperbolas meet, each pair of values is shown to allow only finitely many points P, as the roots of a quadratic in |PA|.

records.title: KarcherIndex
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the Morse index and nullity of Karcher saddle towers, formalizing results from arXiv:2608.13451v2. For the Enneper-Weierstrass realizations, the two-period quotient Xi_{k,2} has index 4k-3 and bounded Jacobi-field nullity 3 for every k >= 3. For the six-ended family Xi_{3,m}, every positive integer m has index 6m-4 floor(m alpha*)-3 and nullity 7 when m alpha* is an integer, and 3 otherwise. The same threshold alpha* lies in (1/3,1/2), with certified strict bounds 0.4323617 < alpha* < 0.4323619. As in the paper, index and nullity are defined using complex-valued functions, with dimensions taken over the complex numbers. The development constructs realizations from the explicit data and supplies the geometric-to-analytic identifications, rather than assuming the existence of a realization. Supporting results include proper embeddedness and the equivalence of boundedness and finite Dirichlet energy for smooth geometric Jacobi fields on the finite period quotients.

records.title: The orthogonal boundary-point art gallery problem is ∃ℝ-complete, in Lean 4
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of material in a forthcoming manuscript entitled "The Orthogonal Art Gallery Problem is ∃ℝ-complete". A Lean 4 and Mathlib proof, for an explicit single-tape Turing machine model, that deciding whether an orthogonal simple polygon (every edge horizontal or vertical) with rational corners can be guarded by g points of its boundary, which together must see the whole closed polygon (the boundary-point variant), is ∃ℝ-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions. The orthogonal point-point and point-boundary variants are the subject of the author's earlier entry PALOMAR-2026-11-01-000004 v1, whose definitions this entry reuses unchanged. For general polygons the boundary-point variant is treated by Abrahamsen, Adamaszek and Miltzow (J. ACM 2021); orthogonal polygons are not. The hardness proof is a new construction: the ETR-INV instance is compiled to rows of fourteen relation profiles, and the polygon is a hub with one floor slot per variable and one door per row, behind each of which hangs an orthogonal wing (a staircase corridor ending in an arithmetic room) whose boundary guards copy the slot values through the door and enforce the row relation. Its finite visibility facts are kernel-checked certificates on the wing charts, parametric in the size and value parameters. The proofs use only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.title: Cardinalities of three-point ordered convolution-square fibres
records.abstract: In any finite abelian group G, fix a three-element support S and retain the entire labelled ordered additive convolution square, including diagonal pairs. The number of three-element supports with the same square is h or 2h, where h is the number of elements u satisfying u+u=0; in particular it is at most 2h. The full proof is included. This adapts a prior public Couret formalization; novelty and independent human review are not established.

records.title: Statistical thresholds for Tensor PCA
records.abstract: We formalize in Lean the principal statistical and constrained-landscape results of Statistical thresholds for Tensor PCA by Jagannath, Lopatto and Miolane, following a local expanded manuscript prepared solely by Patrick Lopatto, the formalization’s maintainer. This elaborated manuscript was prepared to facilitate autoformalization. At nonnegative signal strength in the ordered Gaussian tensor model, we prove the detection threshold below and above criticality for even orders k ≥ 6. For k ≥ 3, we prove the maximum-likelihood value limit at every nonnegative signal strength and the maximum-likelihood absolute-overlap limit away from criticality. We prove optimality bounds for independently randomized measurable unit estimators at nonnegative noncritical strengths, and tensor MMSE formulas at positive noncritical strengths. We also prove the discontinuous overlap transition, consistent testing among fixed nonempty finite families of distinct supercritical strengths, constrained expected and almost-sure energy limits for signed overlaps in [-1,1], and associated variational and landscape conclusions. Almost-sure limits concern fixed parameters and allow arbitrary coupling across dimensions. For interior overlaps, the four-parameter variational reduction establishes equality of infima; unrestricted minimizer attainment is not claimed.

records.title: Conditional logarithmic partner ranks in exponential matching markets
records.abstract: Switching costs relax pairwise stability by requiring both members of a blocking pair to gain more than a common nonnegative cost. In balanced markets with n firms and n workers and independent rate-one exponential utilities, this package proves a conditional benchmark for ordinal partner ranks in Lean. Fix a matching and condition the market on its stability. If twice the cost divided by log n tends to rho in [0,1), the conditional probability that average one-based firm partner rank is at most n^t tends to (t-rho)/(1-rho) for every rho<t<1; rank 1 is best. Equivalently, the logarithm of average firm rank divided by log n converges in distribution to the uniform law on [rho,1]. Bounded or vanishing costs give rho=0, with persistent dispersion across polynomial rank scales under this conditioning. The theorem removes the original conjecture's supercritical lower bound. The proof also includes positive conditioning probability, exact integral identities, score limits, and rank-transfer estimates. This fixed-matching conditioning does not determine ranks under a uniform stable lottery in an ordinary random market, or dispersion of stable outcomes within a typical realized market. An accompanying working paper presenting these results and their economic interpretation is in preparation. A link will be added here when it is publicly available.

records.title: The Reinhardt conjecture, formalized in Lean 4
records.abstract:
The Reinhardt problem asks for the centrally symmetric convex disk in the plane whose densest packing by congruent copies is least dense. Karl Reinhardt (1934) and, independently, Kurt Mahler (1947) found the smoothed octagon, a regular octagon whose corners are cut off by arcs of hyperbolas, each asymptotic to the next two side lines, with greatest packing density delta_oct = (8 - 4 sqrt 2 - log 2)/(2 sqrt 2 - 1) = 0.902414..., and Reinhardt conjectured that no centrally symmetric convex disk packs worse. The conjecture has been open since 1934; Thomas Hales cast it as a problem of Bolza in the calculus of variations (2011) and then as an optimal control problem on SL2(R) (2017), and Hales and Koundinya Vajjha studied that problem in Packings of Smoothed Polygons (2024).

This entry proves the conjecture with its equality case. Every centrally symmetric convex disk has greatest packing density at least delta_oct, with equality if and only if the disk is the image of the smoothed octagon under an invertible affine map; and the smoothed octagon, in Reinhardt's description, is a centrally symmetric convex disk of greatest packing density delta_oct.

The proof follows Hales's control formulation. A worst disk is realized by a global minimizer of the control problem, which lifts to a Pontryagin extremal, stays in Hales and Vajjha's compact domain, switches finitely often and is normal. Its switch signs fall into five classes, each excluded for periods with at least six pieces by scalar estimates; periods with at most five pieces cost at least the octagon's area, with equality only for the octagon. The scalar estimates are inequalities, polynomial identities, monotonicity and convexity arguments; a few polynomial signs are checked by explicit Bernstein expansions, and no interval cover is used. The geometric and control-theoretic foundations, among them Fejes Toth's lattice theorem, Theorem 5.0.2 of Hales and Vajjha and the Pontryagin maximum principle, come from the pinned libraries lean4-smoothed-polygon and lean4-optimal-control.

records.title: Log-Sobolev inequality on finite cyclic groups
records.abstract: Lean verification of the inequality in Theorem 1: the word-length log-Sobolev inequality on ZMod n for n ≥ 4 and nonnegative real functions.
